## 8. Experience architecture

The macro-structure of the experience: the layers a user moves through, the routing/component architecture that implements them, and the connective systems that prevent Bevel-style fragmentation. Rationale stays here; §16 owns per-screen specs; §47+ owns full folder layouts.

### 8.1 The five experience layers

```
L0  Ambient      — widgets, complications, notifications, watch glances
L1  Today        — one screen: how am I doing now (the daily contract)
L2  Pillars      — Sleep / Recovery / Strain / Fitness / Nutrition / Biology / Cycle / Journal-Logs
L3  Metrics      — universal metric detail (any measurable thing, one template)
L4  Workbench    — raw data explorer, correlations, experiments, reports, export, AI deep analysis
```

- Casual users live in L0–L1, visit L2 occasionally, may never see L4. Power users treat L4 as home base; L0–L1 remain their glance layer too.
- Rule: **every element at layer N links coherently to N+1** (tap the ring → pillar; tap a pillar metric → metric detail; every metric detail offers "open in Workbench"). No dead ends; no layer-skipping surprises.

| Layer | Owning tracks | Primary code homes | Data entry point |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 | TRACK-AMBIENT | `ios/BadanWidgets/`, `ios/BadanWatch/`, `android/widgets/`, `android/wear/` | `GetTodayOverviewQuery` snapshot cache + `core-notify` |
| L1 | TRACK-IOS-SHELL / TRACK-AND-SHELL | `Features/Today/` both apps | `GetTodayOverviewQuery` |
| L2 | TRACK-IOS-FEATURES / TRACK-AND-FEATURES | `Features/<Pillar>/` both apps | per-pillar queries (`GetSleepPillarQuery`…) |
| L3 | same | `Features/MetricDetail/` (one template, ~300 instances) | `GetMetricDetailQuery(metricId, period)` via `core-registry` |
| L4 | TRACK-CORE-DATA + features | `Features/RawData/`, `Features/Correlations/`, `Features/Reports/`, `Features/Export/` | `SampleRepository`, `core-export`, `core-insight` |

### 8.2 The daily contract (L1)

The Today screen promises: *in under ten seconds you'll know (1) how you slept, (2) how ready you are, (3) whether anything is unusual, and (4) one thing worth doing.* Everything else on Today is optional modules the user (or preset) curates — mirroring Bevel's Edit Home, but with presence-based defaults (P5) and preset packs (§19.3). Contractually: `GetTodayOverviewQuery` must resolve from local cache in <400 ms cold (§15.4) and returns exactly the module list the policy + presence rules allow; the One True Sentence is generated by `core-insight` and linted by `core-phrasing` before render.

### 8.3 Pillar pages (L2) — the Bevel-plus template

Each pillar page follows one grammar (adopted from Bevel's observed pillar pages, extended), implemented as an ordered list of design-system sections so pillars are assembled, not hand-built:

| # | Section | Design-system component | Feeding source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hero (score/state + emotional art + date) | `PillarHero` | pillar query + art state mapper |
| 2 | Key facts row (2–4 stat cards, deviation badges) | `StatCard` row | `core-baseline` deviations |
| 3 | **Narrative** (coaching paragraph + "why" — BADAN addition) | `NarrativeCard` | `core-insight` + `core-phrasing` |
| 4 | Context strip (active statuses affecting this pillar — BADAN addition) | `ContextStrip` | `StatusInterval` query |
| 5 | Timeline slice (this pillar's events today) | `TimelineList(filtered)` | `timeline_feed` (§8.6) |
| 6 | Trends list (band-chart cards → metric details) | `TrendRow` list | `core-registry` pillar metric order |
| 7 | Related-pillar links ("Late meal 11:40 PM → see Nutrition" — BADAN addition) | `CrossLinkCard` | cross-pillar insight candidates |
| 8 | Learn (resources + definitions) | `ResourceCards` | `contentcms` + registry definitions |

### 8.4 The universal metric detail (L3)

One template for *every* metric — biometric, nutritional, lab, medication adherence, symptom frequency, subjective mood:

value+date → status vs personal band → chart (type per metric family, declared in the registry entry's `chart_family` field) → period controls (`7D|30D|3M|6M|1Y|All` + calendar) → Trends Analysis rolling-delta table → **Anatomy** (inputs/quality/provenance — BADAN addition) → correlated events overlay toggle (meds changes, statuses, cycle phase — BADAN addition) → resources/definition → actions (log related entry, pin to Home, add to report, export this metric, ask AI).

This template is the single largest engineering-UX investment and the single largest coherence win: learn one screen, understand three hundred. Engineering consequence: the template is **registry-driven** — `MetricDetailScreen` takes only a `metricId`; everything else (unit, formatter, chart family, band availability, resources) resolves through `core-registry`. Adding a registry entry yields a working detail screen with zero UI code (E-01.3 acceptance).

### 8.6 Connective tissue systems (anti-fragmentation) — specified

1. **Unified Timeline.** One chronological stream of typed events across all pillars. *Owning module:* `core/core-db` (view + DAO) with feature UI in `Features/Journey/`. *Data contract:* SQLDelight view `timeline_feed` unions the event-bearing tables into one row shape `(event_id, kind, occurred_at, tz_offset_min, day_key, title_key, value_num, value_unit, badge_kind, badge_value, source_ref, native_ref)`:

```sql
-- core/core-db/src/commonMain/sqldelight/net/badan/db/timeline.sq
CREATE VIEW timeline_feed AS
SELECT id AS event_id, 'session.' || session_type AS kind, start_at AS occurred_at,
       tz_offset_min, day_key, title_key, primary_value AS value_num, primary_unit AS value_unit,
       'score' AS badge_kind, score AS badge_value, source_connection_id AS source_ref,
       'sessions/' || id AS native_ref
FROM sessions                       -- sleep + workout sessions
UNION ALL
SELECT id, 'event.' || event_type, occurred_at, tz_offset_min, day_key, title_key,
       value_num, value_unit, badge_taxonomy, badge_value, source_connection_id,
       event_type || '/' || id
FROM event_records                  -- meals, symptoms, med taken/skip, notes, mood,
                                    -- status start/end, lab results, sync markers
ORDER BY occurred_at DESC;
```

  `event_records.event_type ∈ {meal, symptom, med_taken, med_skipped, mood, note, status_start, status_end, lab_result, measurement, water, caffeine, alcohol, sync_marker}` (enum frozen in `contracts/events/domain-events.yaml`). `day_key` is precomputed by the timezone resolution engine (§9.10) so day grouping is stable across DST/travel. Filter chips map 1:1 to `kind` prefixes; every row's `native_ref` resolves through the route manifest (§8.5).
2. **Cross-pillar insight cards.** Insights explicitly cite two+ pillars ("Recovery dipped on the 3 days after late meals this month") and deep-link both ways. *Owning module:* `core/core-insight/` — `InsightCandidate` DTO carries `citedMetricIds: List<MetricId>` (≥2 for cross-pillar class) and `evidenceWindow`; renderer builds the two deep links from the citations. Verified by `core-insight`'s claim verifier before persistence to `insights`.
3. **The Narrative spine.** Daily/weekly/monthly narratives are generated from the same insight graph (`insights` table filtered by horizon), so the story is consistent at all zoom levels — no "sleep tab says great, recovery tab says terrible" whiplash without the narrative addressing it. *Owning modules:* `core-insight` (selection) + `core-phrasing` (surface realization, tone policy, EN/AR).
4. **Global search** (§35) across metrics, foods, symptoms, meds, settings, education. *Owning module:* `core/core-search/` (FTS5 index over registry names/synonyms, food names, symptom dictionary, settings keys, education titles).
5. **Statuses and annotations render on every chart.** *Owning module:* `DesignSystem/BandChart` accepts an `annotations: List<ChartAnnotation>` layer; the annotation query (`GetChartAnnotationsQuery(metricId, window)`) assembles med regimen changes, `StatusInterval` spans, cycle phase bands, and user notes; `PresentationPolicy.annotations` decides which classes render at the user's depth.

### 8.7 The presentation-policy object

The depth dial (§8.8) compiles into a single injected value — the one authority for density, labels, and annotation richness (enforcement: P10 lint). Defined in `core/core-model/presentation/PresentationPolicy.kt`; resolved by `PresentationPolicyResolver` (reads `customization_profiles` via `CustomizationRepository` in `core-db`, exposed as a cold-start-cached `Flow<PresentationPolicy>`).

```kotlin
// core/core-model/presentation/PresentationPolicy.kt
enum class DepthLevel { CASUAL, BALANCED, POWER }
enum class TermStyle { PLAIN, TECHNICAL }          // "Readiness" vs "HRV-weighted recovery composite"
enum class AnnotationRichness { MINIMAL, STANDARD, FULL }

data class PresentationPolicy(
    val depth: DepthLevel,
    val surfaceOverrides: Map<SurfaceId, DepthLevel>,   // e.g. Balanced overall, POWER on Sleep
    val labels: LabelPolicy,
    val density: DensityPolicy,
    val annotations: AnnotationPolicy,
) {
    data class LabelPolicy(
        val termStyle: TermStyle,
        val showUnitsInline: Boolean,
        val numberPrecisionBoost: Boolean,              // POWER: extra decimal + delta vs baseline
    )
    data class DensityPolicy(
        val todayModuleBudget: Int,                     // CASUAL 5, BALANCED 7, POWER 9
        val showTrendsTables: Boolean,                  // rolling-delta tables ambient vs on-demand
        val heroShowsTopDriver: Boolean,                // ring subtitle shows driving input word
        val timelinePreviewCount: Int,
    )
    data class AnnotationPolicy(
        val richness: AnnotationRichness,
        val showStatusSpans: Boolean,
        val showMedChanges: Boolean,
        val showCyclePhase: Boolean,                    // also gated by module visibility + consent class
        val showUserNotes: Boolean,
    )
    fun depthFor(surface: SurfaceId): DepthLevel = surfaceOverrides[surface] ?: depth
}
```

*Injection:* iOS — `@Environment(\.presentationPolicy)` set at `BadanApp.swift` scene root from the shared resolver (via SKIE flow bridging); Android — `CompositionLocalProvider(LocalPresentationPolicy provides policy)` at the activity root in `navigation/`. Non-UI consumers: `core-notify` (notification analytical depth), `core-insight` (narrative verbosity hint), widget snapshot builders (L0 density). The policy never gates data access or navigation topology (§8.8 invariants) — only rendering parameters.

### 8.8 Mode architecture (the recurring tension, resolved structurally)

- **Depth dial, not mode fork:** a per-user rendering level (Casual / Balanced / Power) set by onboarding archetype, adjustable anytime in one switch, with per-surface overrides (Balanced overall but Power on Sleep) — exactly the `surfaceOverrides` field above.
- What the dial changes: module density defaults, chart annotation richness, table visibility, terminology verbosity, notification analytical depth — i.e., precisely the fields of `PresentationPolicy` and nothing else.
- What the dial never changes: the data collected, the truth of statements, navigation topology (help content and muscle memory stay valid), or access to any screen (Power surfaces reachable from Casual via explicit links — just not ambient). CI: route manifest tests run under all three depth fixtures and assert identical route sets.

### 8.9 First-run experience arc

Connect → backfill → provisional insight *within the first session* ("From your last 90 days of watch data: your typical sleep is 6h50m; RHR trending −2 bpm since spring") → archetype-light onboarding (3 questions max: goal, depth appetite, modules — S-13 maps answers to a preset that seeds `PresentationPolicy` + module visibility) → Today screen already alive. Full onboarding spec in §16.2; education ramp in §27. The P4 integration test (§7.2) is this arc's contract.

### 8.10 iOS/Android divergence at the experience layer

Identical: layers, templates, pillar grammar, depth dial, Today contract, route manifest. Divergent by design: L0 surfaces (WidgetKit/Live Activities/watchOS complications vs Glance widgets/Wear tiles), platform settings idioms (iOS grouped-list vs Material 3 preference panes), share-sheet vs intent flows, Shortcuts vs app-actions automation. Both platforms' users must be able to describe the app identically to each other — the parity CI suite (P6) is the mechanical form of that sentence.

```
│   ├── Symptoms dictionary → correlation inputs → physician PDF
│   ├── Food search/barcode → nutrition scores (E-12) → photo/describe AI
│   │   └── Glucose module meal-response binding (E-13) [order-independent retro-bind]
│   └── Strength builder (E-11.1) → strength progression + muscle radar
├── Insights/narrative v1 (E-07)  [needs baselines + phrasing + guardrails]
│   ├── One True Sentence on Today
│   ├── Cross-pillar insight cards (WP-07-04) [needs timeline + routes]
│   ├── Ask-BADAN chat + memory + check-ins (E-17)
│   └── Correlation Lab + Experiments (E-19)  [needs 90d+ data density]
├── Trust surfaces (E-08): consent, privacy dashboard, local-only, opt-out
│   └── Cloud sync E2E (needs crypto port + identity)  → multi-device + restore
├── Export v1 (E-09) → scheduled exports → personal API + SQLite/Parquet (E-22)
├── Notifications + widgets (E-10)  [needs decision engine + deep links]
│   └── Watch apps / Live Activities / Wear tiles (E-16)
├── Billing/entitlements (flags) → paywall surfaces → referrals
└── Bio Age (E-20)  [needs biology registry + labs + validation memo]
```

### 9.10 Hidden enabling features (invisible, load-bearing) — mini-specs

1. **Metric registry service.** *Purpose:* single source of truth for every metric's identity/unit/family/formatting — enables the universal template and registry-driven UI. *Interface:* `MetricRegistry` (`core/core-registry/`): `definition(id: MetricId): MetricDefinition`, `byPillar(pillar): List<MetricDefinition>`, `formatter(id): MetricFormatter`. *Consumers:* every feature screen, `core-export` (column naming), `core-search` (index seeds), `core-insight` (citation naming). *Acceptance:* (a) adding a YAML entry in `contracts/metrics/registry/` yields browser row + detail screen with zero UI code; (b) registry load validates against `registry.schema.json` at build time, malformed entry fails CI.
2. **Unit conversion service.** *Purpose:* one converter for every unit pair incl. mmol/L↔mg/dL, kg↔lb, per-metric user overrides. *Interface:* `UnitConverter` (`core-registry`): `convert(value, from, to)`, `preferredUnit(metricId, locale, overrides)`. *Consumers:* formatters, charts, exports, log keypads (unit-guarded), narrative phrasing. *Acceptance:* (a) round-trip conversion loss < display precision for all registry unit pairs; (b) glucose fixture renders correctly in both unit systems across UI, export, and narrative in the same session.
3. **Timezone/DST resolution engine.** *Purpose:* stable day attribution (sleep-day rules, travel, DST) — computes `day_key` used by `timeline_feed`, baselines, calendar. *Interface:* `DayAttributionEngine` (`core-ingest`): `dayKeyFor(instant, tzOffset, kind)`, `sleepDayFor(session)`. *Consumers:* `core-db` writes, `BaselineEngine`, calendar UI, digests. *Acceptance:* (a) DST-transition fixture assigns each sleep session to exactly one day with no gaps/dupes; (b) 10-timezone travel fixture keeps daily step totals stable on re-derivation.
4. **Reference-range library (labs).** *Purpose:* biomarker reference ranges with locale/lab variants, versioned, display-only wellness framing. *Interface:* `ReferenceRangeLibrary` (`core-registry`): `rangeFor(biomarkerId, sex, age, unit, sourceLab?)`. *Consumers:* Biology rows/status words (PB-45), lab entry validation, physician PDF. *Acceptance:* (a) every shipped biomarker has a range or an explicit `unranged` flag (CI); (b) range version stamped on rendered status and included in export manifest.
5. **Food DB abstraction.** *Purpose:* one interface over multiple providers (Open Food Facts + commercial + regional GCC/MENA) with provenance per item. *Interface:* `FoodDataPort` (`be/fooddata/` + client in `c-ingest`): `search(query, locale)`, `byBarcode(ean)`, `resolve(providerId, itemId)`. *Consumers:* food logging flows, recipe builder, nutrition scoring. *Acceptance:* (a) provider outage degrades to cached + secondary provider without user-visible error class change; (b) every returned item carries `provider`, `verified` flag, and license tag.
6. **Notification decision engine.** *Purpose:* throttling/quiet hours/priority budgets (§24.8) — every notification passes a value test. *Interface:* `NotificationDecisionEngine` (`core-notify`): `decide(candidate: NotificationCandidate, context): Decision(Deliver|Suppress|Defer)`. *Consumers:* narratives, anomalies, med reminders, trial reminders, check-ins. *Acceptance:* (a) flood fixture (20 candidates/day) delivers ≤ budget with priority ordering preserved; (b) quiet-hours fixture defers non-critical and never defers med reminders flagged `user_scheduled`.
7. **Insight deduplication memory.** *Purpose:* never repeat the same insight within N days; track fatigue. *Interface:* `InsightMemory` (`core-insight`): `isFresh(candidateFingerprint, window)`, `recordShown(insightId)`. *Consumers:* `InsightEngine` selection, digests, check-ins. *Acceptance:* (a) identical fingerprint suppressed within window in fixture run; (b) suppression logged with reason for QA inspection in decision journal.
8. **Schema migration framework.** *Purpose:* coordinated local-DB migrations on two platforms + cloud snapshot compatibility. *Interface:* SQLDelight migrations in `core-db` + `MigrationGuard`: `preflight(dbVersion, appVersion)`, `postMigrationAudit()`. *Consumers:* app startup both platforms, sync engine (oplog versioning), restore flows. *Acceptance:* (a) soak test migrates a 5-year fixture DB through every historical schema chain without data loss (row-count + checksum audit); (b) downgrade attempt fails safe with export-preserving path.
9. **Feature-flag & kill-switch system.** *Purpose:* local eval + remote config; per-feature kill without release. *Interface:* `FeatureFlagService` (`core-flags`): `isEnabled(ff_key, context)`, `entitlement(key)`. *Consumers:* all features, parity release checklist (P6), entitlement gates (P2). *Acceptance:* (a) kill-switch flip disables target surface within one cold start and hides its notifications; (b) flag evaluation works fully offline with last-known values.
10. **Algorithm-version stamping.** *Purpose:* every derived value re-derivable and attributable. *Interface:* `AlgorithmVersion` value class on `DerivedValue` (`core-model`), registry of versions in `core-scoring`. *Consumers:* Score Anatomy, exports, changelog page, method-switch re-derivation (PB-59). *Acceptance:* (a) method/config change produces new version stamp and re-derives affected windows; (b) export of any derived value includes its version and the version resolves to a changelog entry.

### 9.11 Feature interaction map (selected critical couplings)

- Statuses ⇄ scoring ⇄ phrasing engine (context changes numbers *and* words).
- Cycle engine ⇄ baselines ⇄ every band chart (bands must re-render per phase).
- Dedup ⇄ export (exports must state the dedup policy applied; raw exports include suppressed duplicates flagged, not deleted).
- Meds logging ⇄ chart annotations ⇄ correlation lab (regimen changes are first-class events in analysis).
- Food logging ⇄ glucose ingestion ⇄ meal-response cards (arrival-order independence: meal logged after CGM data must retro-bind).
- Depth dial ⇄ notifications ⇄ AI verbosity (one preference — `PresentationPolicy` — many surfaces).
- Import connectors ⇄ dedup (imported archives overlap live syncs by design; idempotency required).

### 9.12 Anti-features (explicitly rejected) — with detection

1. Public leaderboards on health scores (shame dynamics; scores aren't comparable across bodies).
2. Ads or data monetization of any kind (Law 1; report: table stakes).
3. Diagnosis-flavored outputs ("you may have X") — hard wording firewall.
4. Punitive streaks (loss aversion on health data breeds anxiety and churn).
5. Dark-pattern paywalls (obfuscated numbers the user "already has"; fake urgency timers).
6. Auto-posting to social networks; any default-public anything.
7. Notification spam as engagement lever (every notification passes the decision engine's value test).
8. Infinite configurable chaos: no user-defined arbitrary formula metrics in v1 (deferred to Workbench-era with sandboxing, §45) — customization is curation, not programming, until the foundation is stable.

| # | How CI/review detects an attempt |
|---|---|
| 1 | Analytics-schema review: any event/property comparing scores across users rejected; no ranking endpoint permitted in `contracts/api/`; community specs (E-23) reviewed against "effort-only challenges" rule |
| 2 | Dependency audit in `tooling/ci/`: ad/attribution SDK denylist fails build; `contracts/events/analytics-events.yaml` schema validation rejects any health-value property (only enums/shapes allowed) |
| 3 | `PhrasingLinter` (`core-phrasing`) with `contracts/phrasing/guardrails.yaml`: banned diagnosis patterns block CI on templates and fail runtime verification on generated text; AI outputs pass the same linter before render |
| 4 | Design-review checklist: streak specs must show freeze mechanics + opt-in; lint bans "streak lost/broken" strings; notification candidates of class `streak` capped by decision-engine budget |
| 5 | UI-test assertion: no obfuscation/blur modifier in any paywalled view tree (PB-43/PB-78); paywall analytics `source` enum excludes `interstitial`; countdown-timer components disallowed in `DesignSystem` |
| 6 | Static check: no social SDK share calls outside the explicit `feat Share` flow; share-card generator defaults every field to privacy-safe preset; any `public` default in a config schema fails contract review |
| 7 | `NotificationDecisionEngine` is the only path to the OS notification APIs (arch test: direct `UNUserNotificationCenter`/`NotificationManager` usage outside `port-push` actuals fails CI); budget KPI dashboard reviewed per train |
| 8 | Registry schema has no user-formula type; PRs adding expression evaluators to `core-registry`/`core-scoring` require ADR; §45 tracks the sandboxed future explicitly |

## 10. Health metric ontology

This section is the **data heart** of BADAN: the canonical registry that every screen (§16A/B), every score (`core-scoring`), every export column (§20), and every AI claim (§23) resolves against. v1 §10 defined the 18 metric families as prose; here each family becomes a structured, machine-checkable block. The registry itself lives at `contracts/metrics/registry/*.yaml` (one file per family), is validated in CI against `contracts/metrics/registry.schema.json`, and is loaded at runtime by `core-registry/MetricRegistry.kt`. Rationale and altitude decisions belong to v1 §10 and §30; this section owns the **entity mapping, metric ids, computation homes, and edge-case policies**. File layout for the modules named here is owned by §47–66.

### 10.0 Canonical representation vocabulary (used by every family below)

Every metric normalizes into exactly one of five canonical entities from `core-model` (types per CONVENTIONS §3; entity map per v1 §30.1):

| Entity | Kotlin type | Shape | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Instant sample | `Sample` | `(metricId, valueSI, unit, at: Instant, tz, Provenance, QualityFlags)` | HR, SpO₂ spot, glucose point, weight |
| Interval aggregate | `IntervalRecord` | `(metricId, valueSI, unit, start, end, tz, aggregation, Provenance, QualityFlags)` | steps/hr, active energy, sleep-window RR |
| Session | `Session` (`SleepSession`/`WorkoutSession`) | `(id, type, start, end, segments[], seriesRefs[], Provenance)` | sleep nights, workouts |
| Event | `EventRecord` (closed union) | `(kind, at, payload, tz, Provenance)` | meal, symptom, med adherence, status, lab, cycle, measurement |
| Derived value | `DerivedValue` | `(metricId, value, algorithmId, algoVersion, InputManifest, at, Confidence)` | scores, indices, deltas, baselines |

Each family block below states which of these it lands in, the exact metric ids (dot-namespaced, CONVENTIONS §3), the computation home module, baseline/covariate policy, edge cases, source-disagreement policy, Score Anatomy outputs (§22.5), export representation (§20), confidence/provenance behavior (v1 §10.18), and raw source types.

### 10.1 Vitals & cardiovascular

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit `HKQuantityTypeIdentifier.heartRate`, `.restingHeartRate`, `.heartRateVariabilitySDNN`, `.walkingHeartRateAverage`, raw beat-to-beat series (`HKHeartbeatSeriesType`), `.bloodPressureSystolic/.bloodPressureDiastolic`, `.oxygenSaturation`, `.respiratoryRate`, `.vo2Max`; Health Connect `HeartRateRecord`, `RestingHeartRateRecord`, `HeartRateVariabilityRmssdRecord`, `BloodPressureRecord`, `OxygenSaturationRecord`, `RespiratoryRateRecord`, `Vo2MaxRecord`; vendor (Garmin/Oura) rMSSD; manual BP/HR entries.
- **Normalized representation:** `Sample` for HR/SpO₂/RR/BP components; `IntervalRecord` for windowed resting/sleeping HR; `DerivedValue` for HRV baseline, RHR baseline, HRR, VO₂Max-trend.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `vitals.rhr`, `vitals.rhr_baseline`, `vitals.hrv_rmssd`, `vitals.hrv_sdnn`, `vitals.hrv_baseline`, `vitals.hr_max`, `vitals.hr_sleeping`, `vitals.spo2_sleep`, `vitals.rr_sleep`, `vitals.bp_systolic`, `vitals.bp_diastolic`, `vitals.vo2max`, `vitals.hrr_1min`, `vitals.hrr_2min`.
- **Baseline window + covariate eligibility:** HRV/RHR — 28-day robust median + MAD band, phase-conditioned (cycle) and status-conditioned (sick/travel). VO₂Max — 90-day trend, no phase conditioning. BP — no rolling baseline (manual authority; show last + 7-day mean).
- **Edge cases:** (1) rMSSD-from-raw-beats vs platform SDNN field disagree → store both, user method switch (`vitals.hrv_rmssd` is canonical for scoring). (2) sleeping-HR window empty (no sleep session) → fall back to lowest 30-min rolling mean, flag `derived_window_fallback`. (3) BP entered without pulse → pulse null, not zero. (4) VO₂Max step-change on new device → provenance split, do not blend across sources in one trend line. (5) HR series with <60% coverage over workout → suppress HRR, flag `insufficient_coverage`.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** dedup priority dedicated-wearable > phone > third-party app > manual (except BP: manual wins). Conflicting HRV methods never averaged — canonical method per user setting.
- **Explainability (Score Anatomy):** shows contributing sample count ("HRV from 43 beats-to-beat samples"), baseline value + band, deviation in σ, method label.
- **Export representation:** CSV `samples.csv` rows (metric_id, value_si, unit, measured_at, tz, source_device, source_app, quality_flags); JSON `vitals.hrv_rmssd` under `derived[]` with `input_manifest`.
- **Confidence/provenance:** confidence scales with sample coverage; provisional flag until 14 nights.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/vitals/VitalsDerivationEngine.kt`, HRR in `core-scoring/vitals/HrrCalculator.kt`, baselines in `core-baseline/BaselineEngine.kt`.

### 10.2 Sleep

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit `HKCategoryTypeIdentifier.sleepAnalysis` (values `.asleepCore/.asleepDeep/.asleepREM/.awake/.inBed`), `.appleSleepingWristTemperature`, overlapping HR/RR/SpO₂ samples; Health Connect `SleepSessionRecord` (with `Stage` list), `SkinTemperatureRecord`; vendor sleep sessions (Oura/Garmin).
- **Normalized representation:** `SleepSession` (segments = staged intervals); nightly aggregates as `IntervalRecord`; scores as `DerivedValue`.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `sleep.time_in_bed`, `sleep.time_asleep`, `sleep.deep`, `sleep.rem`, `sleep.light`, `sleep.awake`, `sleep.latency`, `sleep.efficiency`, `sleep.continuity_index`, `sleep.hr_dip_pct`, `sleep.midpoint`, `sleep.social_jetlag`, `sleep.debt`, `sleep.bank_balance`, `sleep.need`, `sleep.score`, `sleep.wristtemp_deviation`.
- **Baseline window:** sleep duration/need — 28-day adaptive personal need; timing/social-jetlag — separate workday vs free-day midpoints; all phase- and status-conditioned.
- **Edge cases:** (1) two sources cover same night → `SleepSessionMergeRule` picks ranked primary, others suppressed not deleted. (2) nap vs primary → classify by duration/time-of-day (`SessionAssembler` rules). (3) shift-worker daytime sleep → sleep-day attribution by 18:00 anchor, not midnight. (4) manual "merge-manual-sleep" toggle on → stitch adjacent manual + auto. (5) missing stages (in-bed-only source) → duration only, stages null, flag `stages_unavailable`. (6) wrist-temp absolute value de-emphasized — only deviation stored.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** `SleepSessionMergeRule` — highest-ranked source wins the session boundary; sub-metrics (HR dip, RR) joined from best-covered overlapping series.
- **Explainability:** Score Anatomy lists inputs (duration vs need, continuity, HR dip, timing consistency), each with contribution direction; shows which source provided the session.
- **Export:** `sessions.csv` (session_id, type, start, end, primary_source) + `sleep_stages.csv` (segment rows); derived nightly metrics in `derived[]`.
- **Confidence/provenance:** low confidence if stages absent or single fragmented source; provisional until 14 nights.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/sleep/SleepScoreCalculator.kt`, session stitching in `core-ingest/session/SleepSessionAssembler.kt`, bank ledger in `core-scoring/sleep/SleepBankLedger.kt`.

### 10.3 Recovery & readiness

- **Raw inputs:** derived from `vitals.*` (HRV, RHR, RR, temp), `sleep.score`, prior-day `strain.score`, active statuses (§10.13), cycle phase (§10.11).
- **Normalized representation:** `DerivedValue` only (composite score) + sub-state `DerivedValue`s.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `recovery.score`, `recovery.readiness_state`, `recovery.stress_score`, `recovery.energy_battery`, `recovery.strain_balance`.
- **Baseline window:** each input carries its own phase-conditioned baseline; recovery score compared to personal 28-day distribution for status wording.
- **Edge cases:** (1) luteal-phase HRV suppression → phase-conditioned baseline prevents false "sick" (the WHOOP failure, v1 §3.10). (2) missing sleep → recovery computed with reduced-input flag + wider confidence. (3) `Sick`/`Injured` status → suppress "push harder" phrasing, re-base targets (§23.9). (4) travel timezone shift → status covariate widens band. (5) all inputs provisional → recovery itself provisional.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** inherits per-input dedup; no independent source (fully derived).
- **Explainability:** Anatomy shows each input's deviation and weight (qualitative), plus active covariates ("computed against your luteal-phase norm").
- **Export:** `derived[]` with full `input_manifest` referencing the contributing sample/session ids and their algorithm versions.
- **Confidence/provenance:** confidence = min over inputs; every recompute appends new `DerivedValue` (never overwrites, v1 §30.1).
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/recovery/RecoveryScoreCalculator.kt`, stress in `core-scoring/recovery/StressCalculator.kt`, battery in `core-scoring/recovery/EnergyBatteryModel.kt`.

### 10.4 Activity & movement

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit `.stepCount`, `.distanceWalkingRunning/.distanceCycling/.distanceSwimming`, `.flightsClimbed`, `.activeEnergyBurned`, `.basalEnergyBurned`, `.appleExerciseTime`, `.appleStandTime`, `.walkingSpeed/.walkingSteadiness/.walkingAsymmetryPercentage`; Health Connect `StepsRecord`, `DistanceRecord`, `FloorsClimbedRecord`, `ActiveCaloriesBurnedRecord`, `TotalCaloriesBurnedRecord`, `ExerciseSessionRecord`, `SpeedRecord`.
- **Normalized representation:** `IntervalRecord` (all counts/energy over windows); walking-quality metrics as `Sample`.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `activity.steps`, `activity.distance`, `activity.floors`, `activity.active_energy`, `activity.resting_energy`, `activity.exercise_minutes`, `activity.met_minutes`, `activity.movement_consistency`, `activity.walking_speed`, `activity.walking_steadiness`.
- **Baseline window:** 28-day day-of-week-aware baseline (weekends differ); no phase conditioning by default.
- **Edge cases:** (1) phone + watch both report steps → `StepOverlapRule` de-overlaps by interval intersection (the report's #1 dedup case). (2) manual "add steps" overlapping auto → prefer device, flag manual as supplement. (3) energy double-count across sources → attribute to single ranked source per interval. (4) treadmill distance vs GPS distance divergence → keep per-source, do not sum. (5) midnight-straddling walk → split interval at local midnight for daily aggregates.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** `StepOverlapRule` + `EnergyAttributionRule`; dedicated-wearable wins overlapping windows.
- **Explainability:** Anatomy for daily total shows per-source contribution and any suppressed overlap.
- **Export:** `interval_records.csv` (metric_id, value_si, unit, start, end, aggregation, source_*).
- **Confidence/provenance:** high; overlap-suppressed records retained with `suppressed_by`.
- **Computation home:** `core-ingest/dedup/StepOverlapRule.kt`, aggregation in `core-ingest/aggregate/AggregateComputer.kt`.

### 10.5 Workouts & training

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit `HKWorkoutType` (+ `HKWorkoutActivityType` taxonomy), `HKWorkoutRoute`, segment/lap events, `.cyclingPower/.runningPower/.cyclingCadence`; Health Connect `ExerciseSessionRecord` (+ `ExerciseSegment`, `ExerciseLap`), `PowerRecord`, `CyclingPedalingCadenceRecord`; vendor workout files (Garmin FIT, laps/power); **BADAN Strength Builder** manual sets (system of record — no platform strength type exists, §12.3).
- **Normalized representation:** `WorkoutSession` (segments, series refs); strength sets as structured payload on the session; training-load metrics as `DerivedValue`.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `workout.duration`, `workout.zone_minutes`, `strain.score`, `strain.target`, `strain.deviation_pct`, `strength.volume`, `strength.e1rm`, `strength.total_reps`, `strength.muscle_load`, `cardio.load_acute`, `cardio.load_chronic`, `cardio.load_ratio`, `cardio.load_status`, `cardio.focus_distribution`, `cardio.hrr`.
- **Baseline window:** acute = 7-day EWMA, chronic = 28-day EWMA (ACWR, v1 §10.5); muscle volume 28-day per group; status machine states Calibrating/Detraining/Maintaining/Productive/Fatigued/Peaking/Overtraining.
- **Edge cases:** (1) Garmin + Watch both log the same run → `WorkoutOverlapRule`, Garmin-direct wins workouts by default (§13.2). (2) strength "leg day" invisible to cardio load → separate `strength.muscle_load` channel (v1 §3.7). (3) post-surgical `Injured` status → suppress "Detraining" wording (v1 §3.13). (4) HR series gaps → zone minutes flagged partial. (5) manual workout with no HR → strain from duration/METs heuristic, low confidence. (6) supersets → grouped in payload, volume attributed per exercise.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** `WorkoutOverlapRule` (boundary + type + magnitude similarity); direct-vendor > platform for workouts.
- **Explainability:** strain Anatomy shows zone distribution, duration, HR reserve used; cardio-load Anatomy shows acute/chronic curve and ratio.
- **Export:** `sessions.csv` + `workout_sets.csv` (session_id, exercise_id, set_index, reps, weight_kg, rpe) + derived.
- **Confidence/provenance:** heuristic muscular-load explicitly labeled; e1RM formula id stamped.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/strain/StrainScoreCalculator.kt`, `core-scoring/cardio/CardioLoadEngine.kt`, `core-scoring/strength/StrengthProgressionCalculator.kt`, dedup `core-ingest/dedup/WorkoutOverlapRule.kt`.

### 10.6 Body composition & anthropometrics

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit `.bodyMass`, `.bodyFatPercentage`, `.leanBodyMass`, `.height`, `.bodyMassIndex`, `.waistCircumference`; Health Connect `WeightRecord`, `BodyFatRecord`, `LeanBodyMassRecord`, `HeightRecord`, `BodyWaterMassRecord`, `BoneMassRecord`; smart-scale writes; manual circumferences.
- **Normalized representation:** `Sample` for each measurement; BMI as `DerivedValue`.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `body.weight`, `body.fat_pct`, `body.lean_mass`, `body.bmi`, `body.waist`, `body.hip`, `body.water_pct`, `body.visceral_rating`.
- **Baseline window:** 28-day trend with outlier rejection (single spurious scale reading suppressed).
- **Edge cases:** (1) daily weight noise → show smoothed trend line + raw dots. (2) impedance-derived water/bone/visceral → quality-flag `estimate`, de-emphasize. (3) unit mismatch (lb vs kg) → normalize to kg SI, render per locale. (4) two scales with offset → per-source trends, warn on merge. (5) manual weight wins over scale on same day if user edits.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** manual always wins (deliberate human authority, v1 §11.4).
- **Explainability:** trend Anatomy shows smoothing window and rejected outliers.
- **Export:** `samples.csv`; BMI in `derived[]`.
- **Confidence/provenance:** impedance extras carry lower confidence.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/body/BodyCompositionEngine.kt`, trend smoothing in `core-baseline/RobustTrend.kt`.

### 10.7 Temperature

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit `.appleSleepingWristTemperature`, `.bodyTemperature`, `.basalBodyTemperature`; Health Connect `SkinTemperatureRecord`, `BodyTemperatureRecord`, `BasalBodyTemperatureRecord`.
- **Normalized representation:** wrist/skin as nightly `DerivedValue` deviation; manual body temp as `Sample`.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `temp.wrist_deviation`, `temp.body`, `temp.basal`, `temp.cycle_shift`.
- **Baseline window:** wrist deviation baselined per-user 28-day, phase-conditioned; absolute values never merged across wrist vs oral.
- **Edge cases:** (1) wrist temp offset 1–2°C from core → only deviation surfaced (v1 §10.7). (2) fever manual entry → distinct `temp.body`, never fed to cycle model. (3) ovulatory shift detection → feeds cycle engine only when cycle module enabled. (4) sensor gap night → deviation null, no interpolation.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** wrist and manual are distinct metrics, never reconciled.
- **Explainability:** deviation Anatomy shows baseline and nightly delta in °C.
- **Export:** `derived[]` (deviation) + `samples.csv` (manual body temp).
- **Confidence/provenance:** device-dependent; flagged per source capability.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/temperature/WristTempDeviationEngine.kt`, cycle-shift feed via `core-scoring/cycle/PhaseInferenceEngine.kt`.

### 10.8 Respiratory & oxygenation

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit `.respiratoryRate`, `.oxygenSaturation`; Health Connect `RespiratoryRateRecord`, `OxygenSaturationRecord`.
- **Normalized representation:** `Sample` (spot) + `IntervalRecord` (sleep aggregate).
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `respiratory.rr_sleep`, `respiratory.spo2_sleep`, `respiratory.spo2_spot`.
- **Baseline window:** 28-day nightly baseline; altitude/travel covariate flag.
- **Edge cases:** (1) SpO₂ dip at altitude → context flag, no alarm (v1 §10.8). (2) single low spot reading → not baselined, shown raw. (3) sleep RR without sleep session → attributed to lowest-motion window, flagged.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** dedicated-wearable > phone; spot vs continuous kept distinct.
- **Explainability:** Anatomy shows sample count and altitude covariate if active.
- **Export:** `samples.csv` + `interval_records.csv`.
- **Confidence/provenance:** altitude flag stored as covariate on baseline.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/respiratory/RespiratoryAggregator.kt`.

### 10.9 Glucose (wellness-framed)

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit `.bloodGlucose` (Dexcom/Libre writes), `HKInsulinDeliveryReason` (display-only); Health Connect `BloodGlucoseRecord`; vendor APIs (Dexcom, Libre/Lingo, §13.5); manual fingerstick.
- **Normalized representation:** CGM series as `Sample` stream; derived stats as `DerivedValue`; meal-response as `DerivedValue` bound to meal `EventRecord`.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `glucose.avg`, `glucose.fasting_morning`, `glucose.variability_cv`, `glucose.time_in_band`, `glucose.meal_response_peak`, `glucose.meal_response_ttb`.
- **Baseline window:** 14-day rolling for average/variability; user-set band thresholds (default 3.9–7.8 mmol/L, editable, unit-localized).
- **Edge cases:** (1) compression low overnight → `CompressionLowClassifier` flags artifact, excludes from stats (v1 §37). (2) sensor warm-up gap → excluded, not interpolated. (3) fingerstick vs CGM offset → distinct source class, not merged. (4) meal logged after CGM data arrives → `MealResponseBinder` retro-binds (order-independence, v1 §9.9). (5) unit confusion → SI mmol/L canonical, mg/dL render per locale + override everywhere incl. export.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** CGM stream is primary; fingerstick flagged separate; never dosing/insulin math.
- **Explainability:** meal-response card cites Δpeak, time-to-baseline, and the bound meal.
- **Export:** `samples.csv` (glucose points with unit) + `derived[]`.
- **Confidence/provenance:** artifact-flagged points excluded from derived, retained in raw.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/glucose/GlucoseStatsEngine.kt`, `core-scoring/glucose/MealResponseBinder.kt`, `core-ingest/quality/CompressionLowClassifier.kt`.

### 10.10 Nutrition & hydration

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit dietary types (`.dietaryEnergyConsumed`, `.dietaryProtein/.dietaryCarbohydrates/.dietaryFatTotal`, fiber/sugar/sat-fat, vitamin/mineral set, `.dietaryWater`, `.dietaryCaffeine`, `.numberOfAlcoholicBeverages`); Health Connect `NutritionRecord` (broad field set), `HydrationRecord`; manual food entries (photo AI/description/barcode/search, §21).
- **Normalized representation:** meal as `EventRecord` (kind=meal, payload=foods+nutrients); aggregates as `IntervalRecord`; scores as `DerivedValue`.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `nutrition.energy_in`, `nutrition.protein`, `nutrition.carbs`, `nutrition.fat`, `nutrition.fiber`, `nutrition.water`, `nutrition.caffeine`, `nutrition.alcohol_units`, `nutrition.food_quality_score`, `nutrition.macro_balance`, `nutrition.net_energy`.
- **Baseline window:** 28-day for typical intake; net energy = energy_in − active_energy − resting_energy per day.
- **Edge cases:** (1) AI portion uncertainty → `estimate` quality flag + range shown (v1 §3.15). (2) partial day logging → passive value shown, never "0g" shame rows (P5). (3) alcohol timing → stored as sleep covariate. (4) duplicate barcode + photo of same meal → user-confirmed merge. (5) micronutrient gaps → dot-matrix shows unknown, not zero.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** manual logs authoritative; platform write-back mirrors, never re-ingested (self-source filter, v1 §11.5).
- **Explainability:** food-quality score shows visible rubric (vs Bevel opacity, v1 §3.15); net energy shows in vs out components.
- **Export:** `event_records.csv` (meal events) + `nutrition_nutrients.csv` (per-nutrient rows) + `derived[]`.
- **Confidence/provenance:** AI-estimated portions flagged; database source recorded.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/nutrition/FoodQualityScorer.kt`, `core-scoring/nutrition/NetEnergyCalculator.kt`.

### 10.11 Cycle

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit `HKCategoryTypeIdentifier.menstrualFlow`, `.intermenstrualBleeding`, `.ovulationTestResult`, `.basalBodyTemperature`, cervical mucus; Health Connect `MenstruationFlowRecord`, `MenstruationPeriodRecord`, `OvulationTestRecord`, `IntermenstrualBleedingRecord`; manual period/flow/symptom logs; passive temperature inference (§10.7).
- **Normalized representation:** cycle events as `EventRecord` (kind=cycleEvent); phase as `DerivedValue`; phase-conditioned baselines stored as `Baseline` entities keyed by covariate context.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `cycle.phase`, `cycle.length`, `cycle.period_length`, `cycle.phase_confidence`, `cycle.predicted_next`.
- **Baseline window:** cycle-length stats over last 6 cycles; phase model drives phase-conditioned baselines for `vitals.hrv`, `vitals.rhr`, `sleep.*`, `recovery.*`, `temp.*`.
- **Edge cases:** (1) irregular cycles → wider prediction interval, honest "prediction paused" not wrong guess (v1 §10.11). (2) pregnancy/postpartum/contraception → model flags pause predictions. (3) passive-only inference low quality → phase confidence low, not asserted. (4) reproductive-data privacy → strictest storage class, on-device by default, excluded from cloud AI (v1 §28.7). (5) module hidden → phase covariate disabled, baselines revert to unconditioned.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** logged period authoritative over inferred; inference only fills gaps.
- **Explainability:** any band chart shows phase overlay; Anatomy states "computed against luteal-phase norm."
- **Export:** `event_records.csv` (cycle events) + `derived[]` (phase, gated by sensitive-class export consent).
- **Confidence/provenance:** phase confidence surfaced; sensitive-class provenance tag.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/cycle/PhaseInferenceEngine.kt`, phase-conditioning consumed by `core-baseline/BaselineEngine.kt`.

### 10.12 Biomarkers & labs

- **Raw inputs:** manual lab entry, PDF import (on-device extraction, §13.6), HealthKit Clinical Records (FHIR, US-centric, 🔶), wearable-derived registry members (VO₂Max, HRV/RHR baselines, body comp fold in as registry entries).
- **Normalized representation:** each result as `EventRecord` (kind=labResult, payload=`LabResult`); trend per biomarker as queryable metric.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `biology.apob`, `biology.ldl`, `biology.hdl`, `biology.triglycerides`, `biology.lpa`, `biology.hba1c`, `biology.fasting_insulin`, `biology.homa_ir`, `biology.hscrp`, `biology.homocysteine`, `biology.testosterone_total`, `biology.testosterone_free`, `biology.shbg`, `biology.dheas`, `biology.cortisol`, `biology.igf1`, `biology.tsh`, `biology.ferritin`, `biology.vitamin_d`, `biology.b12`, `biology.egfr`, `biology.creatinine`, `biology.bun`, `biology.alt`, `biology.ast`, `biology.wbc`, `biology.rbc`, `biology.hemoglobin`, `biology.mcv`, `biology.rdw`, `biology.magnesium`, `biology.sodium`, `biology.mercury`, `biology.bio_age` … (~390+ catalog, one registry entry each).
- **Baseline window:** no rolling baseline — reference ranges (locale/lab-aware, overridable per uploaded result) + longitudinal trend across all entries.
- **Edge cases:** (1) unit variants (mg/dL vs mmol/L for lipids) → per-biomarker unit variant table. (2) reference range differs by lab/sex/age → range attached per result, overridable. (3) fasted vs non-fasted → sampling metadata flag. (4) specimen date vs entry date distinct. (5) PDF extraction never silent → human-confirmed field mapping (v1 §9.1). (6) bio-age needs confidence interval, no two-decimal pseudo-precision (v1 §3.9).
- **Source-disagreement policy:** each lab result is authoritative for its specimen; no cross-lab merge.
- **Explainability:** bio-age Anatomy shows input biomarkers and weights (free coarse band + paid full decomposition, v1 §9.2); each biomarker shows status vs range.
- **Export:** `lab_results.csv` (biomarker_id, value, unit, ref_low, ref_high, specimen_date, lab_name, fasted).
- **Confidence/provenance:** LOINC-style stable id; lab name + specimen date as provenance.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/biology/BiologicalAgeModel.kt`, reference ranges in `core-registry/ReferenceRangeLibrary.kt`, PDF assist in `backend/services/fooddata`-adjacent `core-ingest/import/LabPdfExtractor.kt`.

### 10.13 Context & status (first-class family)

- **Raw inputs:** manual status set (Active/Sick/Injured/On-a-Break), auto-suggested Traveling (timezone shift), auto Fasting window, auto Menstrual phase (§10.11), auto Medication change (from med log), manual High-stress, custom.
- **Normalized representation:** `EventRecord` (kind=status) as **interval events** (`StatusInterval`).
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `context.status_active` (interval presence), `context.status_sick`, `context.status_injured`, `context.status_travel`, `context.status_fasting`, `context.status_med_change`.
- **Baseline window:** statuses are covariate inputs to *other* baselines, not baselined themselves.
- **Edge cases:** (1) retroactive apply (Bevel parity) → propagates to recompute of overlapping scores. (2) overlapping statuses → all active simultaneously, all enter covariate set. (3) auto-suggested travel declined → not applied. (4) status spanning midnight → interval retained whole.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** user statuses authoritative; auto-suggestions require confirmation.
- **Explainability:** every chart renders status spans; Anatomy names active covariates.
- **Export:** `event_records.csv` (status intervals with start/end).
- **Confidence/provenance:** manual = full confidence; auto-suggested flagged until confirmed.
- **Computation home:** covariate resolution in `core-baseline/CovariateContextResolver.kt`, phrasing gating in `core-phrasing/StatusPhrasingPolicy.kt`.

### 10.14 Subjective wellness

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit `.stateOfMind` (State of Mind, iOS 17+); Health Connect (🔶); in-app mood/energy/soreness/perceived-quality check-ins.
- **Normalized representation:** `EventRecord` (kind=subjective).
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `subjective.mood`, `subjective.energy`, `subjective.soreness`, `subjective.perceived_stress`, `subjective.perceived_sleep`.
- **Baseline window:** 28-day for typical valence; perceived-vs-objective gap tracked as calibration instrument.
- **Edge cases:** (1) perceived sleep vs objective divergence → surfaces "algorithm disagrees" honestly (v1 Law 2). (2) asked rarely to avoid fatigue. (3) free-text feelings → journal, not scored. (4) per-region soreness maps to body map.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** subjective is authoritative for itself, compared not merged with objective.
- **Explainability:** used to explain calibration ("you felt rested though HRV was low").
- **Export:** `event_records.csv` (subjective events).
- **Confidence/provenance:** self-report source class.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/subjective/SubjectiveGapAnalyzer.kt`.

### 10.15 Symptoms, medications, conditions

- **Raw inputs:** HealthKit symptom category types (subset, iOS), HealthKit medications (iOS 16+, read); Health Connect (no med/symptom types today → internal system of record, §12.5); in-app canonical symptom dictionary + user synonyms; med regimen setup.
- **Normalized representation:** symptom as `EventRecord` (kind=symptom, `SymptomEvent`); medication as `MedicationRegimen` + `AdherenceEvent`; condition as `Condition` linking entity.
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `symptoms.count`, `symptoms.severity_avg`, `symptoms.recurrence`, `meds.adherence_rate`, `meds.regimen_change` (annotation event).
- **Baseline window:** symptom recurrence over rolling window; adherence rate per regimen per period.
- **Edge cases:** (1) vocabulary chaos → canonical dictionary + synonyms (v1 §21.6). (2) skip-with-reason, never red X (v1 §3.12). (3) regimen change → vertical annotation on all charts. (4) prn vs scheduled distinct. (5) no dosing advice ever — record and reflect only. (6) condition is user-declared, never inferred by app.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** internal canonical dictionary richer than platform; HK symptoms mapped in, HK meds read-only.
- **Explainability:** symptom↔metric correlation shows association-not-cause framing (v1 §3.11); adherence shown without shame.
- **Export:** `event_records.csv` (symptoms) + `medication_regimens.csv` + `adherence_events.csv`.
- **Confidence/provenance:** manual source class; regimen-change events feed correlation lab.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/symptoms/RecurrenceDetector.kt`, adherence in `core-scoring/meds/AdherenceCalculator.kt`, dictionary in `core-registry/SymptomDictionary.kt`.

### 10.16 Behavior & adherence

- **Raw inputs:** in-app logging events, goal definitions, insight/report engagement (local-first).
- **Normalized representation:** `DerivedValue` (consistency/adherence metrics).
- **Derived metrics (ids):** `behavior.logging_consistency`, `behavior.goal_adherence`, `behavior.streak_length`, `behavior.engagement_score`.
- **Baseline window:** rolling per goal; streaks opt-in with freezes (v1 §3.2).
- **Edge cases:** (1) streaks never punitive (anti-feature v1 §9.10). (2) engagement inputs stay local-first for personalization. (3) missed log → streak freeze, not break, if configured.
- **Source-disagreement policy:** derived from own events only.
- **Explainability:** goal adherence shown as progress, not deficit.
- **Export:** `derived[]`.
- **Confidence/provenance:** local-only by default.
- **Computation home:** `core-scoring/behavior/AdherenceEngine.kt`.

### 10.17 Derived/composite registry

Every score/index above is itself a registered metric (score history queryable/exportable like any metric — Bevel does this in All Categories, BADAN guarantees it structurally, v1 §10.17). Each carries `algorithm_id` + `algo_version` + `input_manifest` reference. Registry entries for composites set `type: derived` and populate the `derivation` block. **Computation home:** all composites route through `core-scoring/ScoringEngine.kt`, which reads `MetricDefinition.derivation` to select the calculator.

### 10.18 Confidence, quality, provenance metadata (all families)

Per value: source chain (device→app→platform→BADAN), measured-at vs recorded-at, tz, quality flags (`gap_filled`, `artifact_suspected`, `user_corrected`, `provisional_baseline`, `estimate`, `insufficient_coverage`, `stages_unavailable`, `derived_window_fallback`), coverage count, and (derived) input manifest. Rendering: casual = subtle green/amber dot + plain tooltip; power = full chain (v1 §10.18). Home: `core-model/Provenance.kt`, `core-model/QualityFlags.kt`; rendering policy `core-phrasing/ConfidencePhrasing.kt`.

### 10.19 Registry YAML fragment (one full metric definition)

Conforms to `contracts/metrics/registry.schema.json`; lives in `contracts/metrics/registry/sleep.yaml`:

```yaml
- id: sleep.score
  family: sleep
  type: derived                       # instant|interval|session|event|derived
  names:
    en: { casual: "Sleep", power: "Sleep quality composite" }
    ar: { casual: "النوم", power: "مؤشر جودة النوم المركّب" }
  unit: { canonical: score_0_100, display: percent, variants: [] }
  source_classes: [derived]
  derivation:
    algorithm_id: sleep_score
    version: 3                        # bumped -> re-derivation, history retained
    inputs:
      - { metric: sleep.time_asleep, role: duration_vs_need }
      - { metric: sleep.continuity_index, role: continuity }
      - { metric: sleep.hr_dip_pct, role: autonomic_recovery }
      - { metric: sleep.midpoint, role: timing_consistency }
    calculator: core-scoring/sleep/SleepScoreCalculator.kt
  baseline:
    window_days: 28
    method: robust_median_mad
    phase_conditioned: true           # cycle covariate eligible
    status_conditioned: true          # sick/injured/travel covariates
  quality:
    provisional_until_nights: 14
    flags_possible: [stages_unavailable, insufficient_coverage, provisional_baseline]
  rendering: { chart: band, casual_dot: true }
  export: { csv: derived, json_key: "sleep.score", include_input_manifest: true }
```

### 10.20 Registry entry field reference

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (dot-namespaced) | canonical metric id (CONVENTIONS §3) |
| `family` | enum (18 families) | ontology family (§10.1–10.18) |
| `type` | enum instant\|interval\|session\|event\|derived | canonical entity mapping (§10.0) |
| `names.{locale}.{casual,power}` | string | localized labels per depth altitude |
| `unit.canonical` | string | SI-canonical unit id |
| `unit.display` | string | default display unit |
| `unit.variants` | string[] | allowed display alternates (mmol/L↔mg/dL) |
| `source_classes` | enum[] device\|platform\|manual\|derived\|vendor | permitted source types |
| `derivation.algorithm_id` | string | stable algorithm identity (derived only) |
| `derivation.version` | int | algorithm version (bump ⇒ re-derive) |
| `derivation.inputs[]` | object[] | `{metric, role}` input references |
| `derivation.calculator` | path | computation home module |
| `baseline.window_days` | int | rolling baseline window |
| `baseline.method` | enum | robust_median_mad\|ewma\|none |
| `baseline.phase_conditioned` | bool | cycle covariate eligibility |
| `baseline.status_conditioned` | bool | status covariate eligibility |
| `quality.provisional_until_nights` | int | calibration countdown |
| `quality.flags_possible` | enum[] | quality flags this metric may carry |
| `rendering.chart` | enum band\|line\|bar\|dotmatrix\|clock | detail chart type |
| `rendering.casual_dot` | bool | show confidence dot in casual mode |
| `export.csv` | enum samples\|interval\|sessions\|event\|derived\|labs | export table target |
| `export.json_key` | string | JSON bundle key |
| `export.include_input_manifest` | bool | emit derivation manifest in export |

### 10.21 Unit canonicalization table (SI-canonical store + display variants)

`UnitNormalizer` (§11.3) converts every value to the canonical SI unit and retains the original; `core-model/UnitConverter.kt` renders display per locale + user override. Both are stored (never lossy).

| Family | Canonical (stored) | Display variants | Locale default rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| vitals HR/RHR | bpm | bpm | universal |
| vitals HRV | ms | ms | universal |
| glucose | mmol/L | mmol/L, mg/dL | mg/dL for US locale, else mmol/L; per-metric override |
| body weight | kg | kg, lb, st | lb for US, st for UK, else kg |
| temperature | °C | °C, °F | °F for US, else °C |
| distance | m | km, mi | mi for US/UK, else km |
| energy | kJ | kcal, kJ | kcal default everywhere (health convention) |
| nutrition mass | g | g, oz | g default; oz optional |
| BP | mmHg | mmHg | universal |

Rule: exports carry both `value_si`+`unit` and a `display_unit` hint; the data dictionary (§20) documents canonical units so downstream analysis is unambiguous.

### 10.22 Cross-family derivation dependency graph

Recompute ordering is topological (enforced by `core-scoring/ScoringEngine.kt` reading `derivation.inputs`): a change to an upstream metric triggers downstream recompute in order. Critical edges:

```
vitals.hrv_rmssd, vitals.rhr, temp.wrist_deviation, respiratory.rr_sleep ─┐
sleep.score ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─> recovery.score ─> recovery.energy_battery
cardio.load_acute/chronic (prior-day) ─────────────────────────────────────┘
cycle.phase ─> (phase-conditions) ─> all Baseline entities ─> every band chart
context.status_* ─> (covariate) ─> Baseline + phrasing selection
workout sessions ─> strain.score, cardio.load_*, strength.* (independent branches)
nutrition.energy_in + activity.*_energy ─> nutrition.net_energy
glucose points + meal EventRecord ─> glucose.meal_response_* (retro-bind)
```

Consequence: cycle-phase or status edits fan out to baseline re-materialization then score recompute; the pipeline emits `ScoresRecomputed` so UI invalidates cached bands (v1 §9.9 cycle⇄baseline⇄every-band coupling).

### 10.23 Score Anatomy output contract (the glass-box shape)

Every family's "Explainability" line above resolves to one structured DTO rendered by the universal Score Anatomy sheet (v1 §22.5, P3 glass-box). Owned by §16 for layout; the data contract is defined here so calculators emit it uniformly:

```kotlin
data class ScoreAnatomy(
    val metricId: String,               // e.g. "recovery.score"
    val value: Double, val displayValue: String,
    val algorithmId: String, val algoVersion: Int,
    val inputs: List<AnatomyInput>,     // ordered by contribution magnitude
    val baseline: BaselineRef?,         // value + band + phase/status context label
    val activeCovariates: List<String>, // ["luteal phase", "traveling"]
    val confidence: Confidence,         // provisional? coverage counts
    val whatWouldMoveThis: List<String> // qualitative levers
)
data class AnatomyInput(
    val metricId: String, val role: String,      // from registry derivation.inputs
    val contribution: Direction,                 // raised | lowered | neutral
    val coverageNote: String                     // "HRV from 43 samples"
)
```

Rule: no derived metric may render a value without a resolvable `ScoreAnatomy` (a free-tier guarantee, v1 §7 P2 — "a free user is never left with a naked number"). Home: each calculator returns `(DerivedValue, ScoreAnatomy)`; assembled by `core-scoring/anatomy/AnatomyAssembler.kt`.

### 10.24 Export representation summary (per canonical entity)

Consolidates the per-family "Export" lines into the CSV/JSON target map (schema `contracts/export/schema/v1/*`, owned by §20):

| Canonical entity | CSV file | Key JSON path | Always-present columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Sample` | `samples.csv` | `samples[]` | metric_id, value_si, unit, measured_at, tz, source_device, source_app, path, quality_flags |
| `IntervalRecord` | `interval_records.csv` | `intervals[]` | + start, end, aggregation, suppressed_by |
| `Session` | `sessions.csv` (+ `sleep_stages.csv`/`workout_sets.csv`) | `sessions[]` | session_id, type, start, end, primary_source |
| `EventRecord` | `event_records.csv` (+ nutrient/subtype files) | `events[]` | kind, at, tz, payload_json, source |
| `DerivedValue` | `derived_values.csv` | `derived[]` | metric_id, value, algorithm_id, algo_version, input_manifest_ref, confidence |
| `LabResult` | `lab_results.csv` | `labs[]` | biomarker_id, value, unit, ref_low, ref_high, specimen_date, lab_name, fasted |

Every export states the dedup policy applied and includes suppressed duplicates flagged (not deleted) — Law 5, v1 §9.9.

## 11. Data ingestion and interoperability

v1 §11 defined five ingestion paths and a normalization pipeline as prose; this section makes them **adapter specs and pipeline classes**. Rationale stays in v1 §11/§30; file layout in §47–66. All paths land in one deterministic, replayable pipeline (`core-ingest/NormalizationPipeline.kt`) — no path bypasses provenance (Law 5).

### 11.1 Adapter interfaces (the five paths as contracts)

Each ingestion path implements one of three port interfaces. Platform stores and vendor clouds are ports (KMP expect/actual in `adapters/`); archive import is a core service.

```kotlin
// adapters/port-health/  — implemented by port-health-ios (HealthKit) & port-health-android (Health Connect)
interface HealthStorePort {
    suspend fun capabilities(): HealthCapabilityDescriptor          // which HK/HC types exist on this device
    suspend fun requestPermissions(bundle: PermissionBundle): PermissionResult
    suspend fun readSamples(type: OntologyType, range: TimeRange): Flow<RawSamplePayload>
    suspend fun readSessions(type: SessionType, range: TimeRange): Flow<RawSessionPayload>
    fun observe(types: Set<OntologyType>): Flow<ChangeToken>        // observer queries / HC background reads
    suspend fun write(record: WriteableRecord): WriteReceipt        // write-back, self-source tagged
    suspend fun historicalWindow(): TimeRange                       // max backfill range this platform allows
}

// core-ingest/vendor/  — Garmin, Oura, Dexcom, Fitbit, Whoop, broker
interface VendorApiAdapter {
    val sourceId: SourceId
    val authType: AuthType                                          // OAUTH2 | API_KEY | PARTNER
    suspend fun connect(authGrant: AuthGrant): SourceConnection
    suspend fun backfill(range: TimeRange): Flow<RawVendorPayload>  // one-shot deep history
    suspend fun poll(since: SyncCursor): RawBatch                   // incremental pull
    fun webhookRoutes(): List<WebhookRoute>                         // push endpoints (Garmin ping, Dexcom)
    suspend fun refreshToken(conn: SourceConnection): SourceConnection
}

// core-ingest/import/  — Apple Health ZIP, Google Takeout, Garmin/Oura/Fitbit archives, CSV
interface ArchiveImporter {
    val format: ArchiveFormat
    suspend fun probe(file: FileHandle): ArchiveManifest            // detect format + counts + date span
    fun stream(file: FileHandle): Flow<RawArchiveEntry>             // streaming parse, bounded memory
    fun entityMapping(): EntityMappingTable                         // source element -> ontology type
    suspend fun importBatch(entries: Flow<RawArchiveEntry>): ImportBatch  // idempotent, batch-id tagged
}
```

Manual entry (path 4) is not a port — it constructs canonical entities directly via `core-ingest/manual/ManualEntryGateway.kt` and enters the pipeline at the QualityFlagger stage (it skips SourceTagger/UnitNormalizer since it is already canonical + user-authored).

### 11.2 Path → adapter mapping

| Path (v1 §11.2) | Adapter interface | Concrete impls | Entry stage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Platform store | `HealthStorePort` | `HealthKitStore` (iOS), `HealthConnectStore` (Android) | SourceTagger |
| Vendor cloud API | `VendorApiAdapter` | `GarminAdapter`, `OuraAdapter`, `DexcomAdapter`, `FitbitAdapter`, `WhoopAdapter` | SourceTagger |
| Broker/aggregator | `VendorApiAdapter` | `TerraBrokerAdapter` (multiplexes many `sourceId`) | SourceTagger |
| Manual entry | `ManualEntryGateway` (not a port) | in-app forms, Shortcuts/intents | QualityFlagger |
| Archive import | `ArchiveImporter` | `AppleHealthZipImporter`, `GoogleTakeoutImporter`, `GarminArchiveImporter`, `OuraArchiveImporter`, `FitbitArchiveImporter`, `CsvMappingImporter` | SourceTagger |

### 11.3 Pipeline stages (as classes)

Each stage is a class in `core-ingest/pipeline/` with explicit input/output types; the pipeline is deterministic and replayable (raw payloads retained per retention policy) so algorithm upgrades re-derive history (v1 §11.3). Every stage stamps its version.

| # | Stage class | Input type | Output type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `SourceTagger` | `RawPayload` | `TaggedPayload` | attach `SourceConnection` id, device, ingestion path, batch id |
| 2 | `UnitNormalizer` | `TaggedPayload` | `NormalizedPayload` | convert to SI-canonical, retain original unit + value |
| 3 | `TimezoneResolver` | `NormalizedPayload` | `TzResolvedPayload` | capture event tz, set UTC canonical, apply sleep-day 18:00 anchor |
| 4 | `TypeMapper` | `TzResolvedPayload` | `TypedRecord` | map source type → ontology metric id via registry |
| 5 | `QualityFlagger` | `TypedRecord` | `FlaggedRecord` | physiologic bounds checks, artifact flags (compression low, coverage) |
| 6 | `DedupEngine` | `FlaggedRecord` | `DedupedRecord` (+ `suppressed_by`) | run per-family rule classes (§11.4) |
| 7 | `SessionAssembler` | `DedupedRecord` | `Session` / passthrough | stitch sleep/workout sessions from samples+segments |
| 8 | `AggregateComputer` | `DedupedRecord`/`Session` | `IntervalRecord`/aggregates | daily/weekly rollups, decimation tiers |
| — | (emit) | aggregates | `IngestBatchCompleted` event | triggers `core-baseline`/`core-scoring` recompute + insight engine |

Pipeline entry: `NormalizationPipeline.process(batch: RawBatch): IngestResult`. Emits `IngestBatchCompleted` (domain event, CONVENTIONS §3) consumed by `ScoringEngine` and `InsightEngine`.

### 11.4 Idempotency rules

- **Deterministic identity:** platform records keyed by `(source_uuid, ontology_type)` (v1 §30.5); re-sync of the same record is a no-op upsert.
- **Import batches:** carry a `batch_id` (ULID); re-importing the same archive detects prior batch via content hash → offers "skip / re-run" (never silent duplication). One-tap undo removes the whole batch.
- **Vendor poll cursors:** `SyncCursor` persisted per `SourceConnection`; webhook + poll converge on the same dedup keys so overlap is suppressed, not duplicated (v1 §9.9 import⇄dedup coupling).
- **Manual entries:** ULID at creation; edits append `user_corrected` version, never mutate in place.
- **Replay safety:** re-running the pipeline over retained raw payloads with a bumped algorithm version produces new `DerivedValue` versions, never duplicate raw records.

### 11.5 Dedup rule classes (per-family)

DedupEngine dispatches to named rule classes in `core-ingest/dedup/`. Each rule has a trigger condition and writes a **decision-journal record**. Nothing is deleted — suppressed records keep a `suppressed_by` pointer (Law 5).

| Rule class | Family | Trigger condition | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| `StepOverlapRule` | activity | two step `IntervalRecord`s with intersecting windows + same-ish magnitude | keep ranked source for the intersection, suppress other |
| `EnergyAttributionRule` | activity | active/basal energy from multiple sources over same interval | attribute to single ranked source |
| `SleepSessionMergeRule` | sleep | ≥2 sessions overlapping same night | pick ranked primary session; sub-metrics joined from best-covered series |
| `WorkoutOverlapRule` | workouts | sessions with boundary+type+magnitude similarity | direct-vendor wins; suppress platform duplicate |
| `HrSampleDedupRule` | vitals | identical HR samples from watch echoed via phone | hash-dedup exact duplicates |
| `WeightOutlierRule` | body | scale reading >N σ from trend | flag outlier; manual wins |
| `GlucosePointDedupRule` | glucose | CGM point present from both store and vendor API | prefer store; suppress vendor dup |
| `ImportOverlapRule` | all | imported record matches live-synced record (deterministic id or hash) | suppress import copy, flag `import_over_live` |
| `NutritionMergeRule` | nutrition | same meal via barcode + photo within window | user-confirmed merge |

**Decision-journal record shape** (`core-db` table `dedup_decisions`, exposed in the reconciliation debug view, v1 §11.3):

```kotlin
data class DedupDecision(
    val id: Ulid,
    val ruleId: String,               // "StepOverlapRule"
    val family: String,               // "activity"
    val trigger: String,              // human-readable condition that fired
    val recordsTouched: List<Ulid>,   // all record ids considered
    val kept: Ulid,                   // winner
    val suppressed: List<Ulid>,       // losers (retain suppressed_by -> kept)
    val reversible: Boolean,          // true; user can override
    val thresholdSnapshot: Map<String, Double>, // server-config thresholds at decision time
    val at: Instant, val pipelineVersion: String
)
```

Thresholds ship as server-side config (fixable without release, v1 §30.6); a CI conformance suite (`core-testing/conformance/dedup/`) runs ≥40 real-world overlap fixtures and blocks release on accuracy regression (v1 §30.6, E-03.2).

### 11.6 Retention & replay policy

The pipeline is replayable because raw payloads are retained (`core-db` table `import_batches` + raw payload store). Policy:

| Data | Retention | Replay use |
|---|---|---|
| Raw platform payloads | 90 days rolling (config) | re-derive after QualityFlagger/Dedup version bump |
| Import archive raw entries | until batch undone | full re-import on algorithm upgrade |
| Vendor poll batches | 30 days | reconcile webhook/poll overlap |
| `DerivedValue` versions | permanent (append-only) | audit + "your scores were re-derived" notice |
| `DedupDecision` journal | permanent | reconciliation debug view, user overrides |

Replay entrypoint: `NormalizationPipeline.replay(range, fromStage)` re-runs from a chosen stage (e.g., re-dedup only) without re-fetching from platforms. Each `DerivedValue` re-derivation appends a new version (never overwrites, v1 §30.1) and stamps `algo_version` + `pipelineVersion`.

### 11.7 Pipeline worked example (phone+watch steps, one day)

1. `SourceTagger`: two `RawPayload`s — watch steps (source=AppleWatch), phone steps (source=iPhone) — tagged with `SourceConnection` ids + path=platform.
2. `UnitNormalizer`: both already count units → canonical `count`, original retained.
3. `TimezoneResolver`: event tz = device local; UTC canonical; midnight-straddling interval split at local midnight.
4. `TypeMapper`: both → `activity.steps` `IntervalRecord`.
5. `QualityFlagger`: bounds check (0–60k/day) pass.
6. `DedupEngine`: `StepOverlapRule` fires on intersecting windows → watch kept (dedicated-wearable rank), phone suppressed with `suppressed_by → watch record`; `DedupDecision` journaled.
7. `SessionAssembler`: passthrough (no session for steps).
8. `AggregateComputer`: daily total from kept records; decimation tiers updated.
9. Emit `IngestBatchCompleted` → `activity.steps` daily aggregate baseline recompute → Today module invalidated.

### 11.8 Manual-entry guarded inputs

`ManualEntryGateway` (§11.1) enforces guarded inputs before constructing canonical entities: physiologic bounds per metric (registry `quality.bounds`), unit-explicit forms (never ambiguous kg/lb), timestamp with tz picker (default now), and `user_corrected` versioning on edits. Manual entries enter at QualityFlagger (skip SourceTagger/UnitNormalizer — already canonical + authored). Manual wins for weight/BP/labs per dedup priority (v1 §11.4).

### 11.9 Timezone & sleep-day attribution rules

`TimezoneResolver` (stage 3) is the hidden load-bearing engine (v1 §9.8). Rules:

- **Capture, don't assume:** every record stores its event tz (from source or device); UTC is canonical; local tz retained for display and day-bucketing.
- **Sleep-day anchor:** a sleep session is attributed to the calendar day it *ends* (wake day) using an 18:00 local cutoff — a nap before 18:00 belongs to that day; sleep started 23:00 belongs to the next wake-day (v1 §10.2 shift-work case).
- **DST transitions:** intervals spanning a DST change use wall-clock-aware duration (a 25-hour "night" during fall-back computes true elapsed time, not naive subtraction).
- **Travel:** timezone jump >3h auto-suggests `context.status_travel`; day boundaries follow the new tz once confirmed; sleep straddling the jump attributed by wake-tz.
- **Manual backdating:** user picks date+tz explicitly; retroactive entries re-bucket and trigger recompute of affected days.
- Home: `core-ingest/pipeline/TimezoneResolver.kt` + `core-ingest/SleepDayAttributor.kt`.

### 11.10 Domain events emitted by ingestion

| Event (PascalCase, CONVENTIONS §3) | Emitted when | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `IngestBatchCompleted` | pipeline finishes a batch | `BaselineEngine`, `ScoringEngine`, `InsightEngine` |
| `ScoresRecomputed` | derived values re-appended | UI cache invalidation, `core-notify` |
| `SyncConflictDetected` | dedup finds unresolvable multi-source conflict | reconciliation UI |
| `PermissionRevoked` | platform grant lost | affected modules → denied-state |
| `SourceConnectionDegraded` | auth-health failure (§13.5) | re-auth banner |

### 11.11 Write-back, outbound, cold-start

- **Write-back** (`HealthStorePort.write`): mirrors Bevel's granular toggles (food macros/micros/water/caffeine/alcohol, workouts, body, mood). Rules: never write derived scores; self-source filtering prevents re-ingestion; symptoms/meds write-back off by default on Android until HC type support verified per version (v1 §11.5, §12.5).
- **Outbound** is a peer of inbound: Export Center (§20), personal API (P3), Shortcuts/intents, share-cards. "No dead-end repository" rule (v1 §11.6).
- **Cold-start backfill** (`HealthStorePort.historicalWindow`): request maximal window (HealthKit full history; HC 30-day default → request extended range where available, else prompt archive import); compute provisional baselines immediately, label until 14 nights confirm (v1 §11.7). KPI ≥80% of new users see a personalized insight in session 1.

Bundles are declared in `core-registry/PermissionBundles.kt`, requested via `HealthStorePort.requestPermissions(bundle)`. Staged: Core at onboarding; others on module activation (v1 §12.6).

| `BACKGROUND` (Android) | HC background-read permission + battery-optimization exemption | after Core granted, before first sync completes |

### 12.6 Denied-state fallback matrix (permission × module → UI behavior + retry)

Maintained as a living QA artifact (v1 §12.6, seeded §37.3). No denied state is a dead screen. Retry path always present.

| Permission denied | Module | UI behavior | Retry path |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CORE` (sleep) | Sleep pillar | Education card + manual sleep-log CTA + "why we ask" | Settings→Data→Permissions deep link |
| `CORE` (HR/HRV) | Recovery/Today | Recovery shows "connect a source" empty state, manual RHR entry offered | re-request sheet from Recovery hero |
| `FITNESS` | Fitness pillar | Strength Builder still works (manual); cardio-load shows "needs workout data" | per-card re-request |
| `NUTRITION` | Nutrition | Manual logging fully available; write-back toggle greyed with tooltip | toggle tap → permission sheet |
| `GLUCOSE` | Glucose | Manual fingerstick + vendor-connect CTA; day-strip hidden not broken | "Manage CGM" flow |
| `CYCLE` | Cycle | Manual period logging works; passive inference disabled; sensitive-class notice | consent gate re-entry |
| `BACKGROUND` (Android) | all sync | Foreground-refresh mode banner ("open app to sync"); not silent staleness | banner → battery-optimization guided setup |
| any (revoked mid-use) | affected | `PermissionRevoked` domain event → module shows revoked banner + last-synced timestamp | one-tap re-grant |

### 12.7 Version-dependency matrix (the 🔶 rows made precise)

`HealthStorePort.capabilities()` reads OS/HC version at runtime and downgrades gracefully; these are the exact gates:

| Capability | Gate | Below-gate behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Sleep stages (HK) | iOS 16+ | in-bed/asleep only; `stages_unavailable` flag |
| State of Mind (mood) | iOS 17+ | internal mood check-in only |
| Alcohol count (HK) | iOS 18 | internal log; write-back off |
| Cycling/running power (HK) | iOS 17+ | derive from vendor FIT (🔌) or omit |
| HC background reads | Android 14 / HC version-dependent | foreground-refresh mode banner |
| HC skin temperature | device + HC version | vendor path or omit deviation |
| HC HRV RMSSD | HC version | SDNN unavailable on HC → RMSSD canonical |
| HK medications read | iOS 16+ | internal system of record |

### 12.8 Onboarding permission sequence

`CORE` requested after 3 archetype questions (v1 §8.7) → on grant, cold-start backfill starts and a provisional insight renders in session 1. Module bundles (`FITNESS`/`NUTRITION`/`GLUCOSE`/`CYCLE`/`BODY`/`TEMPERATURE`) requested lazily on first module touch. Android inserts `BACKGROUND` after `CORE` grant, before first sync completes. Each request screen states value + denied-consequence (matrix §12.6). Never a bulk "grant everything" wall.

### 12.9 Practical vs theoretical

Practical now: all ✅/✍️ rows; CGM via stores; HK medications read. Deferred: HC medications/symptoms (watch releases), cross-platform clinical records, BLE-direct sensors (BADAN builds no BLE stack in v1 — stores + vendor bridges cover it, v1 §12.7).
