## 23. AI and interpretation layer

### 23.1 Role definition and capability ladder (carried, binding)
The AI is a **data analyst and translator, never an oracle or clinician**: it explains BADAN's deterministic outputs, answers questions grounded in the user's data, drafts narratives, and assists logging. Scores and stats come from the deterministic engine (§22); the LLM renders and converses about them. This division is architectural, not stylistic — **the LLM cannot emit a number the engine didn't compute** (enforced by the verifier, §23.4). Capability ladder unchanged from v1 §23.2: **Tier 1 (launch)** template-based narratives with LLM smoothing, Ask-BADAN over summarized windows, AI food parsing — cloud LLM with zero-retention agreement + strict minimization; **Tier 2 (P2–3)** user-visible/editable memory, proactive check-ins, RAG over curated literature (PH-LLM-informed), chart generation, fine-tuned small model; **Tier 3 (P3–4)** on-device inference (Apple Foundation Models / Gemma-class via LiteRT) for narratives + basic Q&A fully locally — the "nothing leaves the phone" truth; cloud remains opt-in for deep analysis.

### 23.2 Context-builder pipeline
Stages in `core-insight/ai/` (client) + `backend/services/ai-gateway/` (cloud routing only — the gateway never stores payloads):

1. `AiRequestClassifier` → `AiRequestKind` (DAILY_NARRATIVE, ASK_QUICK, ASK_DEEP, FOOD_PARSE, CHECKIN, REPORT_SECTION).
2. `AiContextAssembler` builds the bundle — pre-aggregated, token-efficient (the report's Terra-AI lesson: never inject raw sensor JSON):

```kotlin
data class AiContextBundle(
    val requestKind: AiRequestKind,
    val engineFacts: List<EngineFact>,           // factId, metricId, value, unit, period, provenanceRef — the ONLY numbers allowed downstream
    val windowSummaries: List<WindowSummaryDto>, // pre-aggregated stat blocks per metric×period
    val memory: List<MemoryItemDto>,             // Tier 2: user-visible/editable items only
    val tonePolicy: TonePolicy,                  // §23.5
    val locale: String,                          // generation language, never post-hoc translation
    val guardrailProfileId: String,              // phrasing profile per request kind
    val tokenBudget: Int
)
```
3. `PromptComposer` binds the bundle into the registered template (§23.3), slot-typed — a template slot can only bind an `EngineFact` field, never free numbers.
4. Routed model call (§23.6) → 5. `ClaimVerifier` (§23.4) → 6. `PhrasingLinter` (`core-phrasing`, rules from `contracts/phrasing/guardrails.yaml`) → 7. render with "data used" footnote (fact list) + payload-log write (§23.7).

### 23.3 Prompt/insight template registry
File layout (content-CMS versioned, reviewable, updatable without app release):

```
content/insight-templates/
├── registry.yaml                     # index: id → file, status(active|killed), owner, review_level
├── daily/dn_sleep_short.yaml         # one file per template
├── daily/dn_readiness_low.yaml
├── weekly/wd_focus.yaml
├── checkins/ci_hrv_trend.yaml
├── ask/system_prompts/{quick,deep}.yaml
└── report/rs_physician_vitals.yaml
```

Template YAML fields: `id, version, kind, trigger` (rule expression over engine outputs, e.g. `sleep.time_asleep.z <= -1.0 && coverage >= 0.8`), `evidence_requirements` (min facts + freshness), `cooldown_days`, `depth_variants {casual, power}` × `lang {en, ar}`, `slots` (typed placeholders → `EngineFact` bindings), `phrasing_class` (drives review level: any template touching symptoms/meds/glucose/cycle requires human review), `kill_switch` (remote — ops can retire a misfiring insight class in minutes, v1 §23.7). Runtime loading + trigger evaluation in `core-insight/InsightEngine.kt`; dedup memory (no repeats within cooldown) and 👍/👎 per-user template weights carried from v1 §23.7.

### 23.4 Verifier pass algorithm
`core-insight/ai/ClaimVerifier.kt`, runs on every generated text before display:

1. **Extract numeric claims:** regex + unit lexicon over the output — numbers adjacent to units/percent/score words/dates/durations; comparative phrases ("higher/lower than", "improved by") extracted as signed claims.
2. **Match to `engineFacts`:** each claim must match a fact within tolerance — exact for integers; ±0.5 of displayed rounding for one-decimal values; ±1 point for percentages after rounding; date claims must match fact periods.
3. **Sign check:** comparative claims validated against the sign of the referenced fact's z-score or delta.
4. **Drop rule:** any sentence containing an unmatched or sign-contradicted claim is dropped whole. If >30% of sentences drop, discard the generation and fall back to the deterministic template render (templates work un-smoothed — v1 §23.5).
5. **Telemetry:** per-template drop-rate recorded (shape-only) — sustained drop-rate >5% flags the template for revision. Target: ≥99% numeric-claim precision on the eval set (E-17 acceptance).

### 23.5 Tone policy object
`core-phrasing/TonePolicy.kt`, stored under `customization_profiles` key `ai.tone_policy` (§19.4):

```kotlin
data class TonePolicy(
    val length: Length,               // CONCISE, STANDARD, DETAILED
    val warmth: Warmth,               // WARM, NEUTRAL
    val language: String,             // BCP-47; narratives GENERATED in UI language
    val readingLevel: ReadingLevel,   // B1_PLAIN (casual default), TECHNICAL (power)
    val nameUsePerDay: Int = 1,       // the user's name never overused
    val fakeEnthusiasm: Boolean = false   // hard false; not user-settable — no fake enthusiasm, ever
)
```
Defaults warm+concise; power mode may use technical vocabulary; reading-level linting in content CI (§27.6).

### 23.6 On-device / cloud routing table
`core-insight/ai/AiRouter.kt`; rows remote-configurable per flag:

| Workload | Default route | Fallback | Gate/flag | Rationale (v1 carried) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Food photo/description parse | Cloud (Tier 1) → hybrid | search UI with draft retained | `ff_nutrition_photo_ai` | accuracy-critical; on-device for simple items later |
| Daily narrative | Templated+LLM cloud → on-device (Tier 3) | deterministic template | `ff_ai_narrative_ondevice` | daily cost + privacy showcase |
| Ask-BADAN quick answers | Cloud minimal-context → on-device option | canned "AI unavailable" + data links | — | latency + privacy |
| Deep analysis / chart gen | Cloud (Pro) | — | Pro entitlement | capability-bound |
| Memory storage | On-device + E2E sync only | — | — | it's user data |
| Cycle-related AI context | EXCLUDED from cloud by default; on-device only unless explicit opt-in | cycle facts stripped from bundle | consent record (§28.7) | sensitive class |

Privacy engineering carried in full (v1 §23.5): minimum-necessary context per query type; pseudonymous sessions (no account identifiers to the LLM vendor); no training on user data (contractual + stated); global "AI off" switch removes all AI surfaces cleanly — deterministic narratives remain.

### 23.7 Per-request payload log
Table `ai_request_logs` (`core-db`; local-only class, powers the Privacy-dashboard "what was sent" view — v1 §23.5):

```sql
CREATE TABLE ai_request_logs (
  request_id       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  at               INTEGER NOT NULL,
  request_kind     TEXT NOT NULL,
  route            TEXT NOT NULL,            -- 'on_device' | 'cloud'
  model_id         TEXT, model_version TEXT,
  payload_summary_json TEXT NOT NULL,        -- field names, fact counts, metric ids, date ranges — no values
  payload_full_ref TEXT,                     -- encrypted local blob, 30-day TTL; power users open exact payload summaries
  token_in INTEGER, token_out INTEGER,
  verifier_dropped INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  guardrail_hits   TEXT                      -- rule ids fired, if any
);
```

### 23.8 Wording guardrails (the non-negotiables — v1 §23.9 carried in full, mechanized)
- **Banned frames:** diagnosis ("you may have…"), treatment ("increase your dose," "take X"), fear ("dangerous," "alarming"), moral judgment ("you failed," "bad day").
- **Required frames:** possibility + evidence ("often associated with…", "in your data, X tends to follow Y"); confidence qualifiers scaled to data quality; status-aware phrasing (Injured/Sick suppress performance-critique templates — the Karim safeguard); persistent-deviation language routes to neutral "worth discussing with a professional if it persists" ONLY via a reviewed template with strict triggers.
- **Enforcement:** phrasing linter on the template registry + verifier-pass regexes + human review for any template touching symptoms/meds/glucose/cycle; red-team suite in CI (§23.9).

Rules live in `contracts/phrasing/guardrails.yaml`, evaluated by `core-phrasing/PhrasingLinter.kt` at template-review time AND at generation time (stage 6, §23.2). Concrete rule examples:

```yaml
version: 3
rules:
  - id: GR-DIAG-01
    type: banned_regex
    applies_to: [all]
    pattern: "\\byou (may|might|could) have\\b"
    severity: block
    rationale: diagnosis frame
  - id: GR-TREAT-01
    type: banned_regex
    applies_to: [all]
    pattern: "\\b(increase|decrease|adjust|double|halve|stop|start) (your )?(dose|dosage|medication|meds)\\b"
    severity: block
    rationale: treatment/dosing advice
  - id: GR-FEAR-01
    type: banned_lexicon
    applies_to: [all]
    lexicon: [dangerous, alarming, "at risk", worrying, scary]
    severity: block
  - id: GR-MORAL-01
    type: banned_lexicon
    applies_to: [all]
    lexicon: ["you failed", "bad day", "lazy", "cheat day", "guilty"]
    severity: block
  - id: GR-CAUSAL-01
    type: banned_regex
    applies_to: [correlation, experiment, insight]
    pattern: "\\b(causes?|caused by|because of your|proves?)\\b"
    severity: block
    allowed_alternatives: ["associated with", "tends to follow", "in your data"]
  - id: GR-CONF-01
    type: required_pattern
    applies_to: [insight, narrative]
    when: "fact.confidence < 0.7 || fact.provisional == true"
    require_one_of: ["may", "tends to", "in your data", "so far"]
    severity: block
  - id: GR-STATUS-01
    type: suppression
    when: "active_status in [SICK, INJURED]"
    suppress_phrasing_classes: [performance_critique]
    severity: block
  - id: GR-PERSIST-01
    type: routing
    when: "composite_deviation.persistence_days >= 5"
    only_template: "neutral_professional_mention"   # the single reviewed template allowed to say
    severity: block                                  # "worth discussing with a professional if it persists"
```
Localization rule: every regex/lexicon rule ships an AR-normalized counterpart in the same file (`pattern_ar`, `lexicon_ar`); linter runs both.

### 23.9 Red-team CI suite
`tooling/ci/ai-redteam/`: `prompts.yaml` — ≥200 adversarial prompts across classes (elicit diagnosis, elicit dosing, induce fear framing, extract cycle data into cloud context, jailbreak phrasings, EN + AR variants); `harness.py` runs each against the staging ai-gateway config AND the on-device model build, passing outputs through `PhrasingLinter` + `ClaimVerifier`. **Gate:** zero outputs of a banned class may pass the linter; any hit blocks release and files the transcript. Suite runs on every guardrails.yaml change, template registry change, model/version bump, and nightly.

### 23.10 Proactive system, insight quality, and trust affordances (carried)
**Check-ins (v1 §23.6):** user-configured cadences + AI-suggested moments gated by `core-notify`; every proactive message must cite a concrete trigger ("HRV 7-day trend −12%" — an `EngineFact`) and offer an action (view evidence / adjust / snooze topic); topic-level snooze is permanent-until-reenabled, honored forever. **Insight quality (v1 §23.7):** template registry with trigger conditions/evidence requirements/cooldowns/variants; dedup memory; 👍/👎 trains per-user template weights; per-template global kill-switch. **Trust affordances (v1 §23.10):** "Why am I seeing this" on every insight (trigger + evidence + template id in power mode); "AI-generated" labeling; correction loop ("that's wrong" → logged, cited data shown for user verification); model/version stamp in power mode.

## 24. Notifications, widgets, watch, and ambient experiences

### 24.1 Ambient philosophy and surface inventory
L0 surfaces deliver the daily contract without opening the app. Every ambient surface (a) answers exactly one question, (b) deep-links to its evidence screen, (c) passes through `core-notify/NotificationDecisionEngine` (widgets and complications pass through its *refresh* budget arm, notifications through its *delivery* arm), and (d) carries **references, not health values** in any payload that transits the backend push service (§31.2 — content is rendered on-device from local data). Ambient ≠ noisy: the default installed footprint is two notifications/day maximum and zero pre-placed widgets.

Surface inventory (each row implemented in this section):

| Surface | Platform | Data path | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Home-screen widgets | iOS WidgetKit / Android Glance | `WidgetSnapshotStore` (app-group JSON) | §24.2, §24.5 |
| Lock Screen / StandBy widgets | iOS | same snapshot store | §24.2 |
| Live Activities / Dynamic Island | iOS | local `ActivityKit` updates (no push token path in P1) | §24.3 |
| Watch app + complications | watchOS | WatchConnectivity snapshots + watch-local HealthKit for live workout | §24.4 |
| Wear OS tiles + ongoing activity | Android | `DataClient` snapshots + `OngoingActivity` API | §24.5 |
| Quick Settings tile, app shortcuts | Android | intent → deep link | §24.5 |
| Notifications (6 classes) | both | `NotificationDecisionEngine` → local scheduling; APNs/FCM only for server-originated triggers (export ready, integration webhook arrival) | §24.6–24.8 |

**The snapshot pattern (decision).** Widgets and watch surfaces never open the SQLCipher database directly (extension memory limits, key-availability-before-first-unlock, and cross-process locking all argue against it). Instead, after every `ScoresRecomputed` or `IngestBatchCompleted` domain event, `core-notify/AmbientSnapshotWriter.kt` serializes a bounded `AmbientSnapshotDto` (today's ring scores + driver words, One True Sentence string, meds-due list of `regimen_id`s + display names, last-night sleep summary, up to 6 Health Monitor tile states, staleness timestamp) to:
- iOS: `group.net.badan.shared/Library/Caches/ambient/today.json` (Data Protection class A-until-first-unlock exception handled by writing a redacted variant `today.locked.json` containing only non-sensitive fields);
- Android: app-private file surfaced to Glance via `GlanceStateDefinition` + to Wear via `DataClient` path `/badan/ambient/today`.
Snapshot writes are debounced (30 s) and versioned (`snapshot_schema_version`); widget code tolerates one version behind. Sensitive-plus families (§28.2) appear in snapshots **only** when the per-widget opt-in consent key `consent.widget.<family>` is granted.

"Refresh policy" combines `WidgetCenter.reloadTimelines(ofKind:)` calls fired by `Platform/WidgetReloader.swift` on domain events, plus scheduled timeline entries.

Deep links: every widget body is one `Link`/`widgetURL` to its evidence route (table in §24.6.1). Tests: `ios/BadanWidgetsTests/SnapshotDecodingTests.swift` (schema tolerance N-1), `WidgetDeepLinkTests.swift` (every widget id → resolvable `AppRouter` route), snapshot-render tests both themes × RTL.

### 24.3 Live Activities (iOS)

Four activities; attribute models live in `ios/BadanWidgets/LiveActivities/`. P1 ships WD + export; workout + CGM in P2 (E-16). All updates are local (`Activity.update`); push-token channel deferred until a server-originated need exists.

```swift
// LiveActivities/WorkoutActivityAttributes.swift
struct WorkoutActivityAttributes: ActivityAttributes {
  struct ContentState: Codable, Hashable {
    var elapsedSec: Int; var currentZone: Int          // 0–5
    var zoneSecondss: [Int]                            // per-zone accrual
    var strainSoFar: Double?; var hrBpm: Int?          // nil when watch not streaming
  }
  var workoutType: String; var startedAt: Date; var sessionRef: String  // session ULID, no values
}
// WindDownActivityAttributes.swift — ContentState: minutesToBedtime, phase(.approach/.inWindow/.past)
// MealResponseActivityAttributes.swift — ContentState: minutesSinceMeal(0–120), curvePointRefs (snapshot indices, rendered from local data), peakFlag: Bool; Attributes: mealEventRef
// ExportJobActivityAttributes.swift — ContentState: percent, stage(.querying/.writing/.packaging), etaSec; Attributes: exportJobRef, formatLabel
```

Dynamic Island: workout shows compact zone dot + elapsed; wind-down shows moon glyph + minutes; both expand to the full ContentState view. `MealResponseActivity` is opt-in per §13.5 wellness framing and gated by `ff_glucose_live_activity` + `consent.widget.glucose`. Lifecycle owner: `ios/BadanApp/Platform/LiveActivityCoordinator.swift` (start/stop keyed to domain events `WorkoutSessionStarted/Ended`, `WindDownWindowEntered`, `MealLogged` when CGM active, `ExportJobProgressed`).

### 24.4 watchOS app (`ios/BadanWatch/`)

**Data-sync decision.** The watch app is a *renderer of phone-computed truth* plus a *logger*: (1) `WatchConnectivity` `applicationContext` carries the same `AmbientSnapshotDto` (writer: `Platform/WatchSnapshotSync.swift`; receiver: `BadanWatch/Sync/SnapshotReceiver.swift`) — guaranteed-latest semantics fit snapshot data; (2) quick-logs travel phone-ward via `transferUserInfo` (queued, survives disconnection) as `LogEventDto`s replayed into the normal ingestion pipeline with `Provenance.ingestionPath = watchQuickLog`; (3) the only direct store reads on watch are watch-local HealthKit during an active `HKWorkoutSession` (live HR/zones — never persisted watch-side). No SQLite on watch in P1–P2.

Page specs (vertical TabView, order fixed):

| Page | Content | Data | Actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| W-1 Readiness | ring + driver word + provisional badge | snapshot.rings.readiness | tap → phone deep link `badan://body/recovery` |
| W-2 Last night | duration, score, stage mini-bar | snapshot.sleepSummary | — |
| W-3 Today strain | strain ring + zone bar | snapshot.rings.strain + zoneSeconds | start workout note |
| W-4 Meds due | due list with per-dose Take/Skip buttons | snapshot.medsDue | `transferUserInfo(AdherenceEventDto)`; optimistic checkmark |
| W-5 Quick log | water / caffeine / mood / symptom-recents grid | recents from snapshot.logRecents | each → `LogEventDto` |

Complications (`BadanWatch/Complications/ComplicationController.swift`, WidgetKit-for-watchOS): `cw_rings` (circular), `cw_readiness_number` (corner), `cw_meds_due` (rectangular count), `cw_water` (gauge). All reload on snapshot receipt. Strength set-logger companion (Phase 2, E-11×E-16): `BadanWatch/Strength/SetLoggerScene.swift` — weight/rep steppers mirroring S-77 template state via live `WCSession` messages, rest timer with `WKHapticType.notification` at T-0. Battery discipline: workout HR display uses platform `HKWorkoutSession` only; no custom sensor polling; snapshot receipt is push-based, no polling loop.

### 24.6 Notification classes — full implementation spec

Common payload rule (all classes, both transports): payload = `{class, template_id, entity_refs[], deeplink, collapse_key, decision_trace_id}` — **never a health value or free-text rendered from health data** when transiting APNs/FCM; server-originated pushes are reference-only triggers and the device renders content locally (mutable-content extension `ios/BadanApp/Platform/NotifRenderExtension/` / `platform/push/PushRenderer.kt`). Locally scheduled notifications may render full text on-device at schedule time but re-verify freshness in the render hook.

| Class id | Class | Trigger source (domain event) | Decision path | Deep-link route | Budget (defaults) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NC-1 | Daily anchors (morning narrative, weekly digest) | `DailyNarrativeReady`, `DigestReady` | full pipeline §24.8; anchor slot logic §24.7 | `badan://today` / `badan://journey/digest/{digest_id}` | ≤1 anchor/day (hard) |
| NC-2 | Care tasks (med reminder, refill nudge) | `MedDoseDue`, `RefillThresholdReached` (from `MedicationRegimen` scheduler in `core-notify/CareTaskScheduler.kt`) | bypasses value-test + global budget (care exemption); quiet-hours *soften* (deliver silently) not suppress; 1 escalation max 30 min later if un-acknowledged | `badan://meds/due` | per-regimen schedule; escalation ≤1/dose |
| NC-3 | State changes (recovery unusually low + why; sensor disconnected; sync broken) | `AnomalyDetected` (composite-severity ≥ threshold, §22.3), `SourceStale`, `SyncConflictDetected`, `PermissionRevoked` | full pipeline; severity gate `severityGate()` before value test | `badan://metric/{metric_id}?focus=deviation` / `badan://settings/sources` | ≤1/day/metric-family; system-health subclass ≤1/day total |
| NC-4 | Encouragement (streaks, goal proximity) | `MilestoneReached` | full pipeline; **opt-in check first** (`settings.notif.encouragement=false` default) | `badan://journey/timeline?highlight={event_id}` | ≤2/week |
| NC-5 | Coach (check-ins, insight follow-ups) | `CheckInDue`, `InsightFollowUpDue` | full pipeline + topic-snooze registry check | `badan://coach/checkin/{id}` / `badan://coach/insight/{insight_id}` | per S-92 cadence config; ≤1/day |
| NC-6 | System (export ready, import finished, permission expiring) | `ExportCompleted`, `ImportBatchCompleted`, `PlatformGrantExpiring` | transactional path: dedup + quiet-hours only (no budget — user-initiated) | `badan://body/exports/{job_id}` / `badan://settings/sources` | n/a (transactional) |

Channel/category registration: Android channels `ch_anchor, ch_care, ch_state, ch_encourage, ch_coach, ch_system, ch_ongoing` (`platform/push/NotificationChannels.kt`); iOS categories with actions (`Take`, `Skip`, `Snooze topic`, `Fewer like this`) in `Platform/NotificationCategories.swift`. Every delivered notification's long-press/action row includes "Fewer like this" → `TopicSnoozeCommand(topic, duration)`.

#### 24.6.1 Deep-link integrity
All routes above must resolve in `AppRouter.swift` / `navigation/BadanNavGraph.kt`; CI test `DeepLinkMatrixTest` (both platforms) walks every `deeplink` value emitted by `NotificationDecisionEngine` fixtures + every widget `widgetURL` and asserts a non-fallback destination (E-10 acceptance).

### 24.7 Smart timing implementation
`core-notify/DeliveryTimePlanner.kt` resolves each candidate's `deliverAt`:
1. Anchors: `wakeDetectedAt + 20min` when a sleep session ended <3 h ago, else the user's configured fallback time; weekly digest: configured day/time.
2. Bedtime-relative: `targetBedtime − offset` from wind-down settings.
3. Workout summaries: `sessionEnd + 5min` (skipped entirely if app was foregrounded on that content since — see rule 5).
4. Care tasks: exact regimen times (Android `AlarmManager.setExactAndAllowWhileIdle` via `platform/push/CareAlarmScheduler.kt`; iOS `UNCalendarNotificationTrigger`).
5. Recency suppression: `suppressIfRecentlyViewed(candidate, window=45min)` consults `core-analytics` local screen-view journal (device-local only) — no notification about content the user just viewed.

### 24.8 The anti-annoyance engine (decision layer)

Engine internals (queue, persistence, replay, test harness) are specified in §59 (core-notify implementation); this section fixes the *behavioral contract*. Pipeline in `core-notify/NotificationDecisionEngine.kt` — stages as named functions, executed in order, each returning `Pass | Drop(reason) | Transform(candidate)`:

```kotlin
fun decide(c: NotificationCandidate): Decision =
  classGate(c)          // class enabled? opt-in classes require explicit grant
  .then(::severityGate) // NC-3 only: composite severity ≥ config threshold
  .then(::valueTest)    // new information? actionable? (template metadata flags)
  .then(::dedupCheck)   // same template+entity delivered within dedup_window?
  .then(::topicSnoozeCheck)
  .then(::classBudget)  // per-class daily caps
  .then(::globalBudget) // global daily cap (default 3; care + system exempt)
  .then(::quietWindows) // quiet hours + user-configurable prayer-time windows → defer or silent-deliver (care)
  .then(::channelRoute) // push | in-app-only | digest-fold (folded items appear in next digest)
  .also { journal(c, it) }  // decision journal row, powers self-audit + §59 replay
```

Budget config shape (server-tunable via `core-flags` remote config, defaults compiled in):

```kotlin
data class NotificationBudgetConfig(
  val globalDailyCap: Int = 3,
  val classCaps: Map<ClassId, Cap>,           // Cap(perDay, perWeek, minGapMinutes)
  val dedupWindowHours: Int = 48,
  val quietWindows: List<LocalTimeRange>,     // user-owned; config supplies defaults only
  val recencySuppressionMin: Int = 45,
  val digestFoldClasses: Set<ClassId>,        // classes that fold rather than drop
)
```

Self-audit surface (S-100 → Notifications → "This week"): data contract `NotificationAuditSummary { weekStart, deliveredCount, byClass: Map<ClassId,Int>, droppedByBudget: Int, foldedToDigest: Int, topTopics: List<TopicCount>, tuneDeeplink }`, computed from the decision journal by `GetNotificationAuditQuery`. Copy pattern: "BADAN sent you 9 notifications this week; tune here." KPI wired to §36 analytics: `notification_disable` events; target notification-driven disable rate < 2 %/month; budget-drop rate is reviewed monthly (a high drop rate means candidate generation is too chatty — fix upstream, not by raising caps).

## 25. Visual design system

### 25.1 Design language: "Warm Instrument"
A precision instrument with human warmth: dark-first but fully dual-theme from day one, generous radii, tactile cards, evocative-but-quiet artwork, data-forward typography. Bevel's observed strengths (dark elegance, pillar accents, scenic heroes, band-charts) are adopted as *principles* and re-expressed originally — no visual cloning. All tokens below are the single source of truth, defined once in `contracts/`-adjacent design token files: `ios/BadanApp/DesignSystem/Tokens/` (generated `Colors.swift`, `Typography.swift`, `Spacing.swift`) and `android/.../designsystem/tokens/` (generated `Color.kt`, `Type.kt`, `Dimens.kt`), both generated from `tooling/design-tokens/tokens.json` by `tooling/scripts/gen_design_tokens.py` (CI check: generated files match source — drift blocks merge).

### 25.5 Chart language (the grammar users learn once)

One component per chart type; iOS `ios/BadanApp/DesignSystem/Charts/`, Android `android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/badan/app/designsystem/charts/`:

| Chart type | Component | Metric families served | iOS file | Android file |

| Ring (scores only, never quantities) | `RingGauge` | sleep/readiness/strain scores | `Charts/RingGauge.swift` | `charts/RingGauge.kt` |
| Vertical range pill | `RangePill` | Health Monitor tiles (today-vs-band) | `Charts/RangePill.swift` | `charts/RangePill.kt` |
| Stacked bars | `StackedBarChart` | sleep stages, cardio focus, macros | `Charts/StackedBarChart.swift` | `charts/StackedBarChart.kt` |
| Ledger area | `LedgerAreaChart` | sleep bank (surplus/deficit shading) | `Charts/LedgerAreaChart.swift` | `charts/LedgerAreaChart.kt` |
| Diverging bar | `DivergingBarChart` | net energy in/out | `Charts/DivergingBarChart.swift` | `charts/DivergingBarChart.kt` |
| Event strip | `EventStripChart` | meds adherence, symptoms, statuses | `Charts/EventStripChart.swift` | `charts/EventStripChart.kt` |
| Point + reference range | `PointRangeChart` | labs/biomarkers | `Charts/PointRangeChart.swift` | `charts/PointRangeChart.kt` |
| Radar (capped at one use) | `MuscleRadarChart` | muscle groups only | `Charts/MuscleRadarChart.swift` | `charts/MuscleRadarChart.kt` |
| Heat calendar | `HeatCalendar` | activity/sleep consistency, year view | `Charts/HeatCalendar.swift` | `charts/HeatCalendar.kt` |
| Day strip | `GlucoseDayStrip` | glucose 24 h + meal markers | `Charts/GlucoseDayStrip.swift` | `charts/GlucoseDayStrip.kt` |

Grammar rules (enforced by component API, not convention): axes always *available* (tap-to-reveal in casual policy); glowing endpoint marks "now"; annotations (statuses/meds/cycle) render only via the shared `AnnotationLayer` (§26.2); every chart exposes `renderShareImage(title, period, units)` so exports/share-cards are share-safe with context baked in; all charts consume `ChartSeries` DTOs from `DerivedValueRepository`/decimation tiers (§30.2) — never raw platform types.

### 25.6 Iconography & shape
Rounded-square metric glyph set, one glyph per registry family + per common metric, named `glyph.<family>.<metric?>` (e.g., `glyph.vitals.hrv`, `glyph.sleep`, `glyph.nutrition.water`). Source SVGs in `tooling/design-tokens/glyphs/`; `gen_design_tokens.py` emits an iOS asset catalog + Android `ImageVector` set; the metric registry (`contracts/metrics/registry/*.yaml`) references glyph ids so registry-driven UI (E-01.3) resolves icons with zero UI code. Settings rows use Bevel-style squircle icon chips (`SettingsGlyphChip` component). Cards: `radius.card` 20 pt; elevation per §25.4.

### 25.7 Motion spec

| Animation | Duration / curve | Trigger | Reduce-Motion behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `motion.ringFill` | 300 ms easeOut, plays once | ring appears | jump to final, 120 ms opacity fade |
| `motion.sheetSpring` | spring(response .45, damping .85) | sheet present | system default (non-spring) |
| `motion.scrubTick` | instant + haptic at band edges | chart scrub | haptic retained, no visual pulse |
| `motion.numberRoll` | 220 ms easeInOut | value change | crossfade |
| `motion.skeletonShimmer` | 1.2 s linear loop, ≤600 ms lifetime rule (§16.9) | loading | static placeholder |
| `motion.landscapeDrift` | ≤0.1 Hz ambient drift | pillar hero idle | fully static frame |
| `motion.milestone` | 600 ms, opt-in celebratory | milestone moments | disabled entirely |

No idle loops outside `landscapeDrift`; no parallax excess; `Reduce Motion`/`animator_duration_scale=0` honored globally via `MotionPolicy` injected next to PresentationPolicy (§26.6).

### 25.8 Inner-landscape art system
BADAN's answer to Bevel's scenic heroes: subtly generative, state-aware, never alarmist.
- **Asset pipeline:** layered vector scenes (sky / horizon / midground / weather particles) authored as SVG layer stacks in `content/art/landscapes/<pillar>/`; `tooling/scripts/landscape_pack.py` compiles them into a platform bundle (iOS asset catalog + Android drawable/vector sets) plus a `scenes.manifest.json` (layer ids, palette slots, particle params). Runtime compositor: `DesignSystem/Landscape/LandscapeRenderer.swift` / `designsystem/landscape/LandscapeRenderer.kt` binds palette slots to tokens and state.
- **State mapping** (input: pillar score band + trend from `GetPillarHeroStateQuery`):

| State input | Scene mapping |
|---|---|
| score in upper band | calm dawn palette, clear sky, high horizon light |
| in-band typical | neutral day palette, drifting soft clouds |
| below band (mild) | soft overcast, muted palette — *never* storm/alarm imagery |
| below band (marked) | gentle rain layer, warm lamp-light accent (comforting, not punitive) |
| provisional/calibrating | misty morning + calibration badge slot |
| no data | still, desaturated scene + empty-state copy slot |

- Reduced-motion: static frame per state. Disable-able: `settings.appearance.pure_data_mode` removes the layer entirely (for both the sterile-averse and the art-averse). Cycle/symptoms pillars use abstract landscapes only (no body imagery). Seasonal app icons ship through the same pipeline (`content/art/icons/`).

### 25.9 RTL mirroring rules (per component class)

| Component class | Rule |
|---|---|
| Navigation, chevrons, back gestures | fully mirrored (system) |
| Cards/lists/chips | mirrored layout; leading glyph flips side |
| Time-axis charts (BandChart, StackedBar, Ledger, EventStrip, HeatCalendar, GlucoseDayStrip) | **plot stays LTR** (time convention); surrounding chrome (title, legend, value readout, period selector) mirrors; scrub tooltip anchors flip |
| RingGauge / RangePill | no mirroring (radial/vertical) ; driver-word text mirrors |
| Steppers (LogStepper) | +/− order mirrors; press-and-hold unchanged |
| SeveritySlider | direction mirrors WITH mirrored labels (low severity starts at reading edge) |
| PeriodSelector | segment order mirrors |
| ShareCard | full mirror; baked-in image respects generating locale |
| Numerals | Eastern/Western digit toggle per locale preference; tabular in both |

String expansion tested (German +30 %); Arabic script metrics verified in every DesignSystem snapshot test (theme × RTL × type-size matrix is the standard grid).

### 25.10 Accessibility requirements (testable checklist)
Each item has an owner-test in `core-testing` or platform UI test suites; the release checklist (E-24) blocks on all:
1. Contrast: all token pairs ≥ WCAG AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 large/graphics) — automated check in `gen_design_tokens.py` on every token change, both themes.
2. Hue-independence: every state indicator has icon/label redundancy — snapshot audit grid rendered in grayscale must remain interpretable (manual gate + CVD-simulated screenshots in CI).
3. Charts expose VoiceOver/TalkBack summary string ("Sleep 7h12m, within your typical range") + per-point navigation; iOS Audio Graphs adopted on BandChart — UI test asserts `accessibilityChartDescriptor` non-nil.
4. Touch targets ≥ 44 pt — lint rule on DesignSystem components (`TouchTargetTest`).
5. Dynamic Type/fontScale to XXL without clipped numerals — reflow snapshots at 200 %.
6. Reduce Motion honored per §25.7 table — `MotionPolicyTest` toggles the flag and asserts variant.
7. All interactive elements labeled + traits correct (buttons vs adjustable) — accessibility snapshot dump diffed in CI.
8. Focus order follows visual order in RTL too — UI test on S-20, S-41, S-56.
9. Haptics never sole feedback channel (paired visual change) — component contract tests (§26).
10. Captions/transcripts required for any future audio content (content pipeline gate, §27).

## 26. Interaction design system

### 26.1 Contract philosophy
Interaction behavior is an API, not a convention: each DesignSystem component publishes responsibilities, typed inputs, emitted events, and legal states. ViewModels bind events to `XxxCommand`/`XxxQuery` use cases; components never touch repositories. Every display component accepts `PresentationPolicy` (depth, labels, density, annotations — the §18.5 mechanism): one component library, two altitudes, zero forks. `PresentationPolicy` lives in `core-model/PresentationPolicy.kt` and is injected at screen scope.

### 26.2 Component behavior contracts (core twelve)

File convention: iOS `ios/BadanApp/DesignSystem/Components/<Name>.swift` (charts under `Charts/`), Android `android/.../designsystem/components/<Name>.kt`. Tests: iOS `BadanAppTests/DesignSystem/<Name>Tests.swift`, Android `designsystem/src/test/.../<Name>Test.kt` (snapshot + behavior).

**C-01 BadanCard** — universal card container.
- Responsibilities: surface + padding + elevation per theme; universal gesture contract (tap = detail, long-press = context menu: pin/hide/explain/export/ask).
- Inputs: `title`, `pillar: Family?` (accent), `policy`, `contextActions: [CardAction]`, `content` slot, `onOpen(route)`.
- Events: `opened`, `contextActionSelected(action)`.
- States: normal · pinned (glyph) · hidden-preview (in layout editor) · provisional (badge slot) · redacted (app-lock).
- Tests: long-press yields exactly the declared actions; tap routes via `onOpen` not internal navigation; provisional badge renders when policy flags calibrating.

**C-02 BandChart** — metric line over personal-normal band + dotted average pill.
- Inputs: `series: ChartSeries`, `band: BaselineBand?`, `period`, `policy` (axes hidden→tap-reveal in casual), `annotations: AnnotationSet?`, `nowMarker: Bool`.
- Events: `scrubbed(point)` (drives tooltip + haptic band-edge ticks), `periodZoomRequested(range)` (pinch, power only), `annotationToggled`.
- States: loaded · loading-skeleton · single-point (dot + band, no fake line) · no-band (calibrating hatch) · empty.
- Tests: casual policy hides axes until tap; band-edge scrub fires haptic event exactly at boundary indices; single-point never renders interpolated line.

**C-03 RingGauge** — scores only, never quantities.
- Inputs: `score: Int?`, `driverWord: String?`, `pillar`, `provisional: Bool`, `size (.hero/.tile/.mini)`.
- Events: `tapped`.
- States: scored · provisional (dashed ring) · empty (hollow + "—") · redacted.
- Tests: fill animation plays once per appearance (`motion.ringFill`); nil score renders hollow not 0; a11y label = "Readiness 82, driver sleep".

**C-04 RangePill** — vertical today-vs-band position (Health Monitor tiles).
- Inputs: `value`, `band`, `unit`, `deviationDirection (.above/.below/.in)`, `policy`.
- Events: `tapped → metric route`.
- States: in-band · out-of-band (amber, arrow+text — never red/green moralizing) · stale (clock glyph) · no-data.
- Tests: out-of-band uses `color.state.outOfBand` + arrow + text (hue-alone lint); stale threshold 36 h renders clock.

**C-05 PeriodSelector** — D/W/M/6M/Y segmented control, one date grammar everywhere (§15.2).
- Inputs: `available: [Period]`, `selected`, `policy` (casual may hide 6M/Y).
- Events: `periodChanged(period)` (ViewModel persists per-surface).
- States: enabled · partially-available (periods without data disabled with tooltip).
- Tests: selection persists per surface via `CustomizationProfile`; disabled period exposes a11y hint "no data for this range"; RTL order mirrors.

**C-06 TrendsTable** — pillar trends list (metric rows: name, sparkline, value, delta).
- Inputs: `rows: [TrendRowModel]`, `density (.compact/.comfortable)` (remembered per surface), `policy`.
- Events: `rowTapped(metricId)`, `densityToggled`, `rowLongPressed(metricId)` (pin/hide).
- States: loaded · partial (some rows no-data with honest "No data") · loading skeleton rows.
- Tests: density persists; no-data rows keep stable ordering (no reflow jumps); sparkline uses decimated series ≤ 30 points.

**C-07 StatusChip** — statuses/contexts (sick, travel, fasting…) in strips and annotations.
- Inputs: `status: StatusInterval`, `interactive: Bool`.
- Events: `tapped → status editor (S-83)`, `removed` (interactive strips only).
- States: active · past (muted) · upcoming (outline).
- Tests: chip color derives from status kind token not free hex; remove emits event without local mutation (optimistic handled by VM).

**C-08 LogStepper** — numeric entry with press-and-hold acceleration (weights, portions, water).
- Inputs: `value`, `step`, `range`, `unit`, `accelerationCurve (after 600 ms ×4, after 1.5 s ×10)`, `hapticsOn`.
- Events: `valueChanged(v)` (debounced commit `valueCommitted(v)`).
- States: enabled · at-bound (end haptic + visual bump) · invalid (unit-guard message slot).
- Tests: hold 2 s from 60 kg with step 2.5 crosses acceleration tiers deterministically (fake clock); range clamp fires `at-bound` once, not repeatedly; RTL flips +/− order.

**C-09 SeveritySlider** — 0–10 severity/RPE with haptic detents.
- Inputs: `value`, `detents: [Int]`, `labels (localized anchor words)`, `policy`.
- Events: `valueChanged`, `committed`.
- States: unset (no default — deliberate; forces intentional entry) · set.
- Tests: unset state submits nil not 0; detent haptic fires at integers only; VoiceOver adjustable trait increments by 1.

**C-10 StatefulContainer** — the §16.9 cross-cutting state wrapper every screen uses.
- Inputs: `state: LoadState<T>` (iOS enum / Android `XxxUiState` sealed interface), slots: `loaded(T)`, `emptyPath`, `deniedFix(PermissionKind)`, `error(AppError)`, `offline`, `provisional-overlay`, `paywalled(context)`.
- Events: `retryTapped`, `fixPermissionTapped`, `upgradeTapped`.
- States: exactly the LoadState variants — components may not invent others.
- Tests: skeleton mirrors loaded layout (snapshot pair diff < threshold); error surfaces support id without stack trace; paywalled never obfuscates numbers (renders explanation variant).

**C-11 AnnotationLayer** — consistent overlay of statuses/meds/cycle events on any time chart.
- Inputs: `annotations: AnnotationSet` (from `GetAnnotationsQuery(metricId, range)`), `visibleKinds: Set<Kind>`, `policy`.
- Events: `annotationTapped(ref)` (opens source event), `visibilityChanged`.
- States: on · off · dense-collapsed (> N marks → clustered pips with count).
- Tests: two-finger tap toggles layer (gesture table); clustering threshold stable across periods; tapped ref resolves to the originating `EventRecord`.

**C-12 ShareCard** — share-safe image composer for charts/digests.
- Inputs: `content (chart snapshot | digest summary)`, `title`, `period`, `units`, `redactions: RedactionPolicy` (sensitive families excluded unless explicitly included per share).
- Events: `shared(channelKind)` (analytics: `share_card_created`, no health values), `cancelled`.
- States: composing · rendering · ready.
- Tests: baked image contains title/period/units (OCR-less: assert draw calls); sensitive-family content requires explicit include flag; RTL render mirrors chrome, plot LTR.

### 26.3 Gesture contract table (global, learn-once)

| Gesture | On | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tap | card/tile/row | open detail | never triggers edit |
| Long-press | card/module | context menu (pin/hide/explain/export/ask) | identical menu order everywhere |
| Long-press | Log tab | recents radial (last 4 log types) | S-01 |
| Scrub (drag) | any time chart | value readout tooltip with date | haptic ticks at band edges |
| Pinch | time charts | period zoom | power policy only |
| Two-finger tap | time charts | annotation layer toggle | C-11 |
| Swipe (leading/trailing) | log rows | edit / delete | manual entries only; delete → undo snackbar |
| Pull-down | lists/Today | refresh = sync with state toast | Bevel parity |
| Pull-down (short) | Today | search | S-20 |
| Drag | Edit-layout mode | reorder modules | drop haptic |

No gesture carries a second meaning anywhere; new gestures require an ADR against this table.

### 26.4 Haptics map

| Event | iOS (`Platform/Haptics.swift`) | Android (`platform/Haptics.kt`) |
|---|---|---|
| Band-edge scrub tick | `.selection` | `CLOCK_TICK` |
| Stepper detent / bound | `.impact(.light)` / `.impact(.rigid)` | `TEXT_HANDLE_MOVE` / `REJECT` |
| Log committed (optimistic) | `.notification(.success)` | `CONFIRM` |
| Undo window expiring (4 s) | none (visual only) | none |
| Destructive confirm shown | `.notification(.warning)` | `LONG_PRESS` |
| Rest timer end (watch) | `WKHapticType.notification` | Wear `CONFIRM` |
| Milestone (opt-in) | `.impact(.soft)` ×2 | `CONFIRM` ×2 |

Haptics are always paired with a visual change (a11y checklist item 9) and respect system haptics-off settings.

### 26.5 Input mechanics, feedback, and error interaction (carried, made concrete)
- **Unit-guarded keypads:** `UnitGuardedKeypad` component validates per metric registry rules (BP systolic>diastolic; glucose sanity range per unit; weight delta > 20 % vs last → confirm sheet). Rules come from registry `validation:` blocks, not hardcoded.
- **Time entry:** default "now" + one-tap backdate chips (−1h / this morning / yesterday) on every log flow; dictation enabled on all text fields.
- **Optimistic UI:** log commands write via `LogXxxCommand` with instant local echo + 5 s undo snackbar; failure → entry marked "not saved" with retry, never silently dropped.
- **Destructive actions:** confirm with consequence statement computed from real counts ("deletes 34 entries; export first?" — count from the actual query) + export-first shortcut.
- **Progressive disclosure:** chips → sheets → pushes in one motion (quick-look sheet expands to full push); "More" rows collapse advanced blocks; first-3-visits helper labels auto-retire (counter in `customization_profiles`).
- **Errors:** field-level inline for recoverable; banner-level for source issues with one-tap fix path; error IDs surfaced for support without stack traces; no blame language ("we couldn't read…" — enforced by the phrasing linter class, §23.9).
- **Sync/processing visibility:** always in the global status sheet (S-02) — never mystery spinners.

## 27. Learning curve and education system

### 27.1 Ramp architecture (carried forward)
Three ramps, all optional, all resumable: **Orientation** (first-run 4-page pillar stories, S-17 — each page teaches *what it is, how to interpret, how it's calculated*); **Deepening** (just-in-time micro-lessons at feature-first-touch, registry §27.4); **Mastery** (library S-93: algorithm pages, data-quality guides, methodology changelog). The "explain this" system stays universal: (i) affordances on every metric/chart, Score Anatomy (S-57) as the deepest layer, and the "explain this to me" AI action rephrasing any screen at chosen depth (§23).

### 27.2 CMS content types and frontmatter schemas
All education content is files-as-content in `content/` (versioned in git, published through the Content CMS service §31.2 with staged rollout — updatable without app release). Four content types, each with a JSON-Schema-validated frontmatter (`contracts/`-adjacent schema: `content/schema/content-frontmatter.schema.json`, CI-validated by `tooling/ci/validate_content.py`):

```yaml
# type: article (long-form education)
id: art.sleep_debt_explained        # stable id, referenced by triggers/links
type: article
title: ""                            # localized per file-tree locale
pillar: sleep                        # family id from registry
reading_level: grade8                # linted by readability check
review:                              # claims-governance gates (§29.6)
  clinical_reviewed_by: ""           # required non-empty to publish
  reviewed_at: 2026-05-01
  claims_lint: pass                  # phrasing linter class run over body
locales: [en, ar]
min_app_version: "1.0"
related_metrics: [sleep.debt, sleep.time_asleep]
telemetry_id: art_sleep_debt         # privacy-safe usefulness counts only
```

```yaml
# type: metric-explainer (bound 1:1 to a registry metric; the (i) target)
id: mx.vitals.hrv_rmssd
type: metric-explainer
metric_id: vitals.hrv_rmssd          # MUST exist in contracts/metrics/registry
sections: [what_it_is, how_measured, device_notes, how_to_read, limits]
device_notes_sources: []             # citations required for accuracy claims
```

```yaml
# type: micro-lesson (≤20 s overlay; just-in-time)
id: ml.first_band_chart
type: micro-lesson
max_display_seconds: 20
dismiss_forever: true                # required true — never blocking
trigger_id: trg.first_band_chart     # must exist in trigger registry
media: band_explainer_overlay        # names an overlay component, not video, in v1
```

```yaml
# type: algorithm-page (per derived metric; the churn-driver antidote)
id: alg.recovery.score.v3
type: algorithm-page
metric_id: recovery.score
algorithm_version: 3                 # binds to AlgorithmVersion entity (§30.1)
tabs: [plain, technical]
sections: [inputs, method_summary, version_history, known_limitations, references]
references: []                       # required non-empty
```

### 27.3 Content folder layout

```
content/
├── schema/content-frontmatter.schema.json
├── en/
│   ├── articles/            # art.*.md
│   ├── metric-explainers/   # mx.<metric_id>.md  (one per registry metric with UI presence)
│   ├── micro-lessons/       # ml.*.md
│   ├── algorithm-pages/     # alg.<metric_id>.v<n>.md
│   └── glossary/            # GENERATED — do not hand-edit (see §27.5)
├── ar/                      # mirrored tree, same ids, translated bodies
├── art/                     # landscapes/, icons/ (§25.8)
└── triggers/registry.yaml   # just-in-time trigger rules (§27.4)
```

The CMS service ingests this tree on merge to `main` (staged: internal → beta → all), serving versioned bundles the app caches offline; content renders even in local-only mode from the last cached bundle plus a shipped baseline bundle in the app binary.

### 27.4 Just-in-time trigger registry
`content/triggers/registry.yaml`, evaluated on-device by `core-insight/EducationTriggerEngine.kt` (subscribes to domain events + first-touch UI signals; per-trigger fired-state in `customization_profiles`):

| Trigger id | Rule (event + condition) | Content | Cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| trg.calibration_status | first `ScoresRecomputed` with provisional flag | ml.why_numbers_wobble | once |
| trg.first_band_chart | first BandChart render per user | ml.first_band_chart | once |
| trg.first_out_of_band | first `AnomalyDetected` surfaced in UI | ml.above_your_normal ("what it means — and what it doesn't") | once |
| trg.first_lab_entry | first `EventRecord(labResult)` logged | ml.reference_range_primer | once |
| trg.first_cycle_band_shift | first phase-conditioned baseline applied in a rendered band | ml.cycle_phase_bands | once |
| trg.first_ai_insight | first `InsightGenerated` viewed | ml.how_insights_are_made | once |
| trg.device_added | `SourceConnectionAdded` with overlapping families | ml.what_your_new_device_adds (templated per source pair) | once/source |
| trg.first_export | first S-61 visit | ml.export_formats_tour | once |

Registry invariants (CI-checked): every trigger's content id exists in both locales; `dismiss_forever` true; ≤20 s; never blocking (overlay, not modal gate); global just-in-time cap 1/day (shares the NC pipeline's `globalBudget` sibling `educationBudget`).

### 27.5 Glossary generation from the metric registry
The glossary is *generated, never hand-written*: `tooling/schema-dictionary-gen/generate_glossary.py` reads `contracts/metrics/registry/*.yaml` (names, localized labels, units, family, definition strings) + merges per-metric `mx.*` explainer summaries, and emits `content/<locale>/glossary/*.md` + a search index consumed by `core-search` (glossary entries reachable from global search, §27.1). CI fails if a registry metric with UI presence lacks a glossary entry or an `mx.*` file — this is the mechanism behind "every ontology term, localized, cross-linked." Casual↔precise label bridging ("Deep sleep — also called slow-wave sleep") comes from the registry's `label_casual`/`label_precise` fields and is shown contextually during the user's first weeks (§17.2).

### 27.6 Algorithm transparency pages
Per derived metric: inputs, method summary (plain + technical tabs), version history with change notes, known limitations, references. Binding is mechanical: publishing a new `AlgorithmVersion` (§30.1) requires a matching `alg.<metric_id>.v<n>.md` before the version can ship (release checklist gate); S-57 Score Anatomy links to the page for the version that produced the displayed value. This industrializes Bevel's Calculations-explainer instinct and is the antidote to the report's #1 churn driver (unexplained score changes).

### 27.7 Localization workflow EN→AR
Roles and gates (applies to all four content types + app strings):
1. **Author (EN)** writes/edits under `content/en/`; PR runs frontmatter schema check, readability lint (grade-8 target for articles/micro-lessons), phrasing/claims linter.
2. **Clinical-claims reviewer** signs any content whose diff touches physiological claims (`review.clinical_reviewed_by` must change with body) — CODEOWNERS enforces on `content/*/articles/`, `metric-explainers/`, `algorithm-pages/`.
3. **Translator (AR)** works from the merged EN version; translation memory tooling optional but ids and frontmatter are copied verbatim (only bodies + `title` translate).
4. **AR medical-language reviewer** (dialect-neutral MSA register, wellness-not-clinical tone) gates `content/ar/` merges — a distinct sign-off from the EN clinical review.
5. **Staleness tracker:** `tooling/scripts/l10n_drift.py` diffs EN/AR content hashes; AR entries > 1 EN version behind are flagged, and the app renders the EN-newer notice ("updated article available in English") rather than silently serving stale guidance.
6. **Telemetry:** per-article usefulness counts (`education_article_rated` — enum rating only) feed a quarterly content review; nothing else is collected (§36).

## 28. Privacy, consent, trust, and responsible UX

### 28.1 Posture
Privacy is a product feature with UI, not a policy PDF: local-first architecture, minimum collection, explicit purpose per data class, no third-party data sale/advertising ever, verifiable user control (export/delete/inspect), and marketing claims that engineering can prove (the thin blind backend §31.1 is the proof).

### 28.2 Data classes at module level

Storage namespaces map to physically separate SQLCipher databases (§32.5): `db_main` and `db_sensitive` (independent keys; `db_sensitive` key derived separately so purge = key destruction + file delete). Consent keys are rows in `consent_records` (§28.3). "AI eligibility" refers to the AI gateway assembly rules (§23.5).

| Class | Examples | Storage namespace | Sync consent key | AI eligibility | Export toggle behavior | Purge semantics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard health | steps, sleep, HR, workouts | `db_main` | `consent.sync.standard` | summarized context allowed (cloud tier) when `consent.ai.cloud` granted; on-device always | included by default in scoped exports | deleted with account/app data; tombstones propagate via sync (§34) |
| Sensitive-plus | cycle, symptoms, meds, conditions, glucose | `db_sensitive` | `consent.sync.sensitive.<family>` (per family, separately consented) | excluded from cloud AI unless explicit `consent.ai.cloud.sensitive.<family>`; on-device allowed | **off by default per export**; explicit per-export include toggle (S-61 scope picker shows a distinct "sensitive data" section) | per-family purge-on-module-disable: user chooses delete vs retain; delete = row purge + key-rotation of family partition + sync tombstones |
| Identity | optional account, email | backend (Identity service) only | n/a (account existence *is* the consent) | never | account data via GDPR export endpoint, not health export | account deletion cascades server-side ≤ 30 days; local mode never creates it |
| Derived | scores, insights, baselines | follows source class (derived-from-sensitive lives in `db_sensitive`) | follows source class | evidence-linked only (references, windows) | follows source class toggles; InputManifest included for provenance | recompute-safe delete: deleting a source class invalidates + purges its derived values (InputManifest makes this mechanical) |
| Telemetry | product analytics | none (event stream, §36.2) | `consent.analytics` (opt-out; opt-in per region where required) | n/a | disclosure page lists full event taxonomy | client-side kill switch; server retention ≤ 15 months |

DI-level enforcement: repositories for sensitive families resolve against `db_sensitive` via the `SensitiveStoreQualifier` in the DI graph; a `core-testing` architecture test asserts no sensitive table is declared in the `db_main` schema files (`core-db/src/.../sensitive/*.sq` vs `main/*.sq`).

### 28.3 Consent model and `consent_records` schema
Layered, granular, revocable: platform permissions (staged bundles §12.6) + BADAN-level purposes (sync, AI processing, analytics — each separate, none bundled with ToS acceptance) + sensitive-class gates (individually consented). Table (in `db_main`, synced as its own change feed so multi-device state converges):

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `consent_id` | ULID pk | |
| `consent_key` | text | namespaced key, e.g. `consent.sync.sensitive.cycle`, `consent.ai.cloud`, `consent.widget.glucose`, `consent.analytics` |
| `purpose_version` | int | version of the purpose text granted against |
| `status` | enum granted / revoked / expired / superseded | append-only: changes append a new row (audit trail), latest row wins |
| `granted_at` / `revoked_at` | timestamp+tz | |
| `granted_via` | enum onboarding / settings / feature_prompt / re_consent | |
| `purpose_text_hash` | text | hash of the exact localized purpose copy shown (provable "what they agreed to") |
| `last_used_at` | timestamp | maintained by the consuming service call sites (sync push, AI request, analytics flush) |
| `prev_consent_id` | ULID? | chain for supersession |

**Consent-versioning flow:** (1) purpose copy lives in `content/` with a `purpose_version`; (2) bumping a version marks all `consent_records` rows with lower `purpose_version` as `superseded` at next app open; (3) the gated feature *pauses* (sync queue holds, AI cloud tier falls back to on-device, analytics stops flushing) until re-consent — never silent expansion; (4) re-consent screen shows a diff-style "what changed"; (5) declining keeps the feature off without nagging (one re-ask max per version). Consent center (S-101) reads this table directly: grant dates, `last_used_at`, one-tap revocation with consequence preview (computed from real dependent-feature list).

### 28.4 Privacy dashboard — counters and their data sources
S-102 shows live "what left this device" counters; every number is computed from a client-side journal, not server logs (the user shouldn't have to trust the server to audit the server):

| Counter | Data source |
|---|---|
| Encrypted sync blobs uploaded (count + last time) | `core-sync` oplog upload journal (`sync_oplog` rows with `pushed_at`) |
| AI cloud requests (count, per-request payload viewer) | AI gateway client journal in `core` — stores the exact assembled payload locally for user inspection (§23.5) |
| Food-database queries (pseudonymized) | food proxy client counter |
| Analytics events sent (count + taxonomy link) | `core-analytics` flush journal |
| Push tokens registered | `PushPort` registration state |
| "Nothing else." row | static — backed by the public analytics disclosure page listing the full event taxonomy (E-08) |

Also on S-102: local-only mode switch (§28.5), per-AI-request payload visibility, security page link (encryption at rest/in transit, E2E sync design summary), deletion entry point. Rule: **no growth hooks inside privacy surfaces** (no referral/invite UI on S-101/S-102/S-104 — ever; enforced by design review checklist).

### 28.5 Local-only mode — implementation notes
First-class configuration, not a degraded state. `LocalOnlyPolicy` is a boolean resolved at DI-graph construction (`ios/BadanApp/App/DI/AppComposition.swift`, `android/.../di/AppModule.kt` — both delegating to shared `core` composition helpers):
- **Never initialized when local-only:** `SyncEngine` (no client object, no key generation, no queue), Identity client (no account endpoints reachable), AI gateway client (cloud tier absent from the capability ladder — `AiTierResolver` returns onDevice|templated only), `PushPort` remote registration (local notification scheduling still works — it's on-device), remote config fetcher in `core-flags` (compiled defaults only), `AnalyticsClient` uploader (journal-only mode or fully off per `consent.analytics`).
- **Unaffected:** full ingestion, scoring, insights (on-device tier), logging, widgets/watch (all snapshot-local), export, education (cached/shipped bundle), search.
- The DI gate is structural: local-only builds of the graph simply have no network-bearing nodes for those services, so "cannot leak" is an architectural property; `core-testing/LocalOnlyGraphTest` asserts the object graph contains zero instances of the excluded types when the flag is set.
- Settings copy states the exact tradeoff (no multi-device sync, no cloud-AI depth, local encrypted backups via user-exported files) — S-16/S-102 both render the same tradeoffs table from one localized source.
- Switching modes later: enabling sync generates keys + uploads from the oplog; disabling sync offers server-side blob deletion with verifiable completion (deletion receipt surfaced in S-104 style).

### 28.6 App lock
Biometric/passcode app lock, local feature: `ios/BadanApp/Platform/AppLock/AppLockService.swift` (LAContext, grace-period option 0/1/5 min) and `android/.../platform/applock/AppLockManager.kt` (BiometricPrompt + Keystore-backed gate). While locked: app switcher snapshot redacted (both platforms), widgets follow `settings.widget_redaction` (§24.2), notifications render class + title but redact narrative preview when lock is on (notification-render hook consults lock state). Lock state never blocks background ingestion (data keeps flowing; only *display* is gated).

### 28.7 Responsible-UX guardrails
Non-diagnostic wording enforcement (§23.9 linter class covers UI copy too); anxiety-aware design (gentle mode, score-hiding toggle, calm anomaly bundling — one composed "here's what changed" instead of N alerts, integrating with NC-3 budgets); no dark patterns (no confirm-shaming, no fake urgency, no obfuscated numbers as paywall bait — C-10's paywalled state renders explanation, never blurred values); age gating (16+ general, 18+ for Bio-Age-class composites, mirroring Bevel's observed gate; no child accounts in scope).

### 28.8 Reproductive-data special handling (rules carried verbatim-in-substance from v1)
Cycle data is sensitive-plus class with these non-negotiable properties, each mapped to its mechanism:
1. **On-device by default** — `db_sensitive` namespace; no `consent.sync.sensitive.cycle` row ⇒ cycle rows never enter the sync oplog (`SyncEngine` change-feed filter is class-aware).
2. **Excluded from cloud AI by default** — AI gateway assembly drops cycle-family context unless `consent.ai.cloud.sensitive.cycle` granted; on-device tier may use it.
3. **Excluded from exports unless explicitly toggled per export** — S-61 scope picker's sensitive section defaults cycle to off *every time* (no sticky include).
4. **Purge-on-module-disable option** — disabling the cycle module presents an explicit delete-vs-retain choice; delete purges `db_sensitive` cycle partition, rotates its key material, invalidates cycle-derived values via InputManifest, and issues sync tombstones if sync was ever on.
5. **Regional threat-model documentation maintained** — jurisdictional data-demand risk assessed and kept current in `docs/compliance/threat-model-reproductive.md` (owned by the §29.6 governance workflow; reviewed with the DPIA §29.4).

## 29. Compliance and regulatory-aware architecture

### 29.1 Regulatory stance
BADAN ships as a **general wellness product**: tracking, logging, interpretation-for-awareness; no diagnosis, treatment, or disease-management claims. A feature review board (product + legal) gates any feature/copy that could cross into medical-device territory (FDA general-wellness guidance logic; EU MDR intended-purpose logic). The architecture is built *audit-ready* so stricter regimes are adoptable later without rewrite (§29.8). Jurisdiction map carried from v1: GDPR (EU/UK — Art. 9 explicit consent, minimization, erasure, portability, DPIA, EU residency option); HIPAA (not applicable by default — no covered-entity flows — but HIPAA-grade controls held anyway); GCC frameworks (Oman PDPL, KSA PDPL, UAE — consent-based processing, residency options, Arabic-language notices); app-store health rules (both stores, §29.7).

### 29.2 GDPR obligations → implementing feature table

| Obligation | Implementing feature / mechanism | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Art. 6/9 — lawful basis, explicit consent for health data | purpose-separated `consent_records` with versioning; nothing bundled into ToS | §28.3; S-101 |
| Art. 13/14 — transparency | layered privacy notice (EN/AR) in-app + privacy dashboard live counters; public analytics-taxonomy disclosure | S-102; `content/legal/` |
| Art. 15 — access | Export Center full-archive template (all classes incl. sensitive with explicit toggle) + account-data export endpoint (Identity service) | S-61; `backend/services/identity` |
| Art. 16 — rectification | all manual entries editable; imported records correctable via source-priority/hide (dedup journal preserves audit) | S-58, S-60 |
| Art. 17 — erasure | S-104 delete flows (scoped: class, module, account) with verifiable completion + server deletion receipts; sync tombstones; backend cascade ≤30 days | §28.2 purge semantics; `backend/services/sync` deletion API |
| Art. 18/21 — restriction/objection | per-purpose consent revocation pauses processing (sync hold, AI fallback, analytics stop) | §28.3 flow step 3 |
| Art. 20 — portability | Export Center **is** the Art. 20 feature: machine-readable CSV/JSON/SQLite with published schema dictionary | §20; `contracts/export/schema/v1/` |
| Art. 25 — data protection by design/default | local-first, E2E sync (server cannot read), sensitive-off-by-default everywhere | §31.1, §28.2 |
| Art. 30 — records of processing | maintained from day one | §29.3 |
| Art. 32 — security of processing | SQLCipher at rest, TLS in transit, E2E envelope, key hierarchy, field-level encryption server-side for the little the server holds | §32.5, §34 |
| Art. 33/34 — breach notification | incident-response runbook with notification timelines (72 h supervisory clock) | `docs/runbooks/incident-response.md` |
| Art. 35 — DPIA | maintained DPIA per §29.4 | `docs/compliance/dpia.md` |
| Chapter V — transfers | region-pinned storage (EU + GCC at launch), vendor DPAs + SCCs in vendor register | `docs/compliance/vendor-register.md`; `backend/infra/environments/` |

### 29.3 Records of processing (RoPA)
Template + living document at `docs/compliance/ropa.md` (one table per processing activity: purpose, data categories, data-class mapping to §28.2, legal basis, recipients/processors, transfers, retention, security measures). Seed activities: account management, encrypted sync blob storage, vendor integration webhook relay, food-database proxying, AI gateway relay, push trigger routing, billing verification, telemetry intake, support correspondence. CI hook: adding a new backend service or vendor to `backend/` or the vendor register without a RoPA row fails the compliance checklist in release CI (`tooling/ci/compliance_check.py` cross-references service list vs RoPA activity ids).

### 29.4 DPIA outline
`docs/compliance/dpia.md`, reviewed at every phase gate and on any new data class/vendor:
1. Processing description (data flows diagram ref: local-first, E2E sync, blind backend §31).
2. Necessity & proportionality (minimization argument per data class; why each backend service exists).
3. Risks to data subjects: re-identification from telemetry (mitigation: no health values in analytics, taxonomy-limited); cloud-AI payload exposure (mitigation: zero-retention vendor terms, payload viewer, sensitive exclusion defaults); reproductive-data jurisdictional demands (mitigation set §28.8 + threat-model doc); sync-server compromise (mitigation: E2E — blobs unreadable); device loss (mitigation: SQLCipher + app lock).
4. Measures per risk with owner + implementation reference (each row cites a §28/§32/§34 mechanism — no unimplemented mitigations allowed to stand).
5. Residual risk sign-off (DPO-designate + product lead), review log.

### 29.5 Backend audit-log event list
All cloud-side data access is audit-logged (admin access near-nil by design — E2E means the server usually *can't* read). Append-only log in the telemetry service's isolated audit store (`backend/services/telemetry/audit/`), events (machine-readable, no health payloads by construction):

| Event | Emitted by |
|---|---|
| `auth.login_succeeded` / `auth.login_failed` / `auth.token_refreshed` | identity |
| `account.created` / `account.deleted` / `account.export_requested` | identity |
| `sync.blob_written` / `sync.blob_read` / `sync.blob_deleted` / `sync.deletion_receipt_issued` | sync |
| `sync.feed_reset` (device re-pair) | sync |
| `integration.webhook_received` / `integration.payload_delivered_and_purged` / `integration.token_refreshed` / `integration.killswitch_toggled` | integrations |
| `ai.request_relayed` (vendor, token counts only) / `ai.vendor_retention_verified` | ai-gateway |
| `push.trigger_sent` (class + collapse key only) | push |
| `billing.entitlement_changed` | billing |
| `admin.access_attempted` (any human/staff read path — expected ≈ zero; alerts on occurrence) | all services |
| `config.remote_flag_changed` | contentcms/flags |
| `deletion.cascade_started` / `deletion.cascade_completed` | identity+sync |

Retention: audit log 24 months, immutable storage class; monthly review runbook `docs/runbooks/audit-review.md`.

### 29.6 Claims & copy governance workflow
Marketing/store/app-UI copy passes the same wording-linter class as AI output (no cure/treat/diagnose verbs — `contracts/phrasing/guardrails.yaml`); science pages cite sources and state consumer-device accuracy limits; "not a medical device" placements standardized (onboarding, reports, CGM surfaces) as specific contextual disclaimers, not wallpaper. Sign-off matrix:

| Artifact class | Author | Mandatory reviewer(s) | Sign-off | Gate mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| App UI strings touching health interpretation | feature dev | phrasing linter (automated) + content lead | content lead | CI linter on string catalogs |
| Education content (articles, mx, alg pages) | content author | clinical-claims reviewer (+ AR reviewer for ar/) | clinical reviewer | frontmatter `review.*` fields + CODEOWNERS (§27.7) |
| Insight/narrative templates | template author | phrasing linter + clinical reviewer | clinical reviewer | template registry publish step |
| Marketing site / store listings | marketing | legal + phrasing linter run on copy deck | legal | pre-publish checklist `docs/compliance/claims-checklist.md` |
| New feature crossing wellness boundary (any scoring of disease-adjacent signals, any "risk" language) | product | feature review board (product+legal) | board minute recorded in `docs/adr/` | ADR required before build |
| Privacy/consent copy | product | legal + DPO-designate | legal | consent purpose_version bump process (§28.3) |

### 29.7 App-store health-data declaration checklists

**Apple App Store (App Review + Privacy):**
1. App Privacy "nutrition label": Health & Fitness data → declared, "Data Not Linked to You" for local-only paths; linked only where account sync applies; no tracking, no data used for advertising.
2. HealthKit entitlement usage strings (`NSHealthShareUsageDescription`, `NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription`) — plain-language, per staged bundle value copy (§12.6).
3. Guideline 2.5.1: HealthKit data used only for health/fitness purposes; never stored in iCloud (we don't — E2E blobs are our own store); no ads from health data.
4. Guideline 5.1.3: no health data to third parties for marketing/analytics — analytics taxonomy contains no health values (link disclosure page in review notes).
5. Reproductive-health scrutiny: cycle features documented for review (on-device default, §28.8) in review notes.
6. Account deletion in-app (S-104) — required since account creation exists.
7. Wellness disclaimers present on Bio-Age and CGM surfaces (screenshot evidence pack in `docs/compliance/store-review-pack/ios/`).
8. Sign in with Apple offered if any third-party login is offered.

**Google Play (Health apps policy + Data safety):**
1. Health Connect access declaration form: each requested data type mapped to a visible user feature (matrix maintained at `docs/compliance/store-review-pack/android/hc-datatype-feature-matrix.md`) — HC types are "restricted"; approval required before release.
2. Data safety form: health data collected/shared answers consistent with the privacy notice; encryption-in-transit yes; user-initiated deletion yes (S-104 link).
3. Health apps declaration (wellness category), including the required privacy-policy URL and no-ads-from-health-data attestation.
4. `ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION`, `BODY_SENSORS`, exact-alarm (care reminders) permissions each justified in the declaration.
5. Foreground-service type declarations (`dataSync` for long imports, §32.2).
6. Account deletion web path (Play requirement) + in-app path both live.
7. Wear OS + widget screenshots consistent with health-data redaction claims.

Both checklists live as tracked files under `docs/compliance/store-review-pack/` and are release-checklist items (E-24); any HC/HK data-type addition re-triggers items I-1/A-1.

### 29.8 Future-stricter readiness
If/when clinical features arrive (§45): FHIR module isolated behind its own consent + storage domain; BAA-capable infrastructure list pre-identified (AWS/GCP/Azure health options per report); QMS-lite habits started now — design history + risk logs on scoring algorithms (the `AlgorithmVersion` + algorithm-page + golden-fixture apparatus of §27.6/§30.1 *is* the design-history file seed) so a future regulated module inherits provenance, not chaos.
