## 50. Android implementation architecture

Mirror of §49 with Android idioms; parity is contractual (v1 Law 7, §33.4: divergence forbidden on metric math/phrasing/export/dedup).

### 50.1 Module list

| Gradle module | Contents |
|---|---|
| `:android:app` | single-activity Compose app; `features/`, `designsystem/`, `platform/`, `navigation/` |
| `:android:widgets` | Glance widgets + receivers |
| `:android:wear` | Wear OS app: tiles, complications, quick-log |
| `:android:baselineprofile` | Macrobenchmark + baseline profile generation (cold-start budget CI) |

### 50.2 Single-activity Compose architecture

`MainActivity` hosts `BadanNavHost` (Navigation-Compose, type-safe routes mirroring iOS route structs: `MetricDetailRoute(metricId, period)`); per-feature packages `net.badan.app.features.<feature>` each contain `XxxScreen.kt`, `XxxViewModel.kt`, `XxxUiState.kt` (sealed interface: `Loading/Loaded/Empty/Denied/Error` — conventions §3). Process-death restoration via `SavedStateHandle` on every ViewModel (route args re-hydrate; parity with 49.5 path persistence).

### 50.3 DI decision: **Hilt** (not manual)

Chosen over the iOS-style manual container because Android's DI seams are framework-owned: `@HiltViewModel` + `SavedStateHandle` injection, `@HiltWorker` for the WorkManager jobs in 50.4, broadcast receivers for Glance, and service injection for the import foreground service all get compile-time-validated wiring for free; a manual container would re-implement `ViewModelProvider.Factory`, `WorkerFactory`, and scoping by hand across 4 modules. KMP core stays framework-free: one `CoreModule.kt` (`@Provides @Singleton fun coreRuntime(...): CoreRuntime`) exposes the same facade split as iOS (`TodayFacade`, `MetricsFacade`, …), so feature code injects facades, never engines. Instrumented tests use `@TestInstallIn` fixture facades.

### 50.4 Health Connect adapter (`adapters/port-health-android` + `platform/health/`)

- **Availability states** (`HcAvailability.kt`): `Available`, `UpdateRequired` (`SDK_UNAVAILABLE_PROVIDER_UPDATE_REQUIRED` → Play deep-link flow), `NotInstalled` (pre-14 devices → guided install, v1 §37.3 case 15), `Unsupported` (manual-mode product, v1 §37.1 case 1). The capability descriptor (§51.2) encodes the state so core logic degrades without platform checks.
- **Permission flow:** `PermissionController.createRequestPermissionResultContract()` launched per staged bundle (Core at onboarding; Nutrition/Glucose/Cycle on module activation, v1 §12.6); background-read permission requested separately with its own explainer; denial → `foreground-refresh mode` banner state, never silent.
- **Changes API polling:** `HcChangesPoller.kt` stores per-type changes tokens in `sync.sq/read_anchors (store='hc')`; token-expired responses trigger windowed re-read + dedup (idempotent by design, v1 §34.3).
- **WorkManager job names** (unique-work, all `@HiltWorker`s in `platform/health/work/`):
  - `net.badan.work.hc_changes_poll` — PeriodicWork 15 min, network-not-required
  - `net.badan.work.hc_backfill` — OneTime expedited, chunked 30-day windows
  - `net.badan.work.nightly_recompute` — Periodic 24 h, charging+idle constraints
  - `net.badan.work.sync_push` — OneTime on oplog threshold + Periodic 6 h
  - `net.badan.work.export_scheduled` — Periodic per schedule (Pro)
  - `net.badan.work.vendor_pull` — Periodic 1 h when vendor connections exist (§51.3 fallback polling)

### 50.5 Foreground-service import flow

`ImportForegroundService` (`foregroundServiceType="dataSync"`, `platform/importer/`): used **only** for explicit long user-initiated imports (archive ZIP, multi-year backfill). Notification shows batch progress + cancel; work is checkpointed per `import_batches` row so process death resumes; falls back to `hc_backfill` WorkManager chunks if the user dismisses. Everything else stays in WorkManager (OEM-survivability, v1 §32.2).

### 50.6 Glance widgets (`:android:widgets`)

`TodayRingsWidget`, `SentenceWidget`, `HealthMonitorGridWidget`, `MedsDueWidget` (action: take), `WaterQuickLogWidget` (action: +glass), `SleepLastNightWidget`, `GlucoseStripWidget` (opt-in). Same `WidgetSnapshot.json` contract as iOS (written to app files dir by workers); `GlanceStateDefinition` reads snapshot only — no engine boot in the widget process. Update triggers: `updateAll()` from `nightly_recompute` / `hc_changes_poll` completions.

### 50.7 Wear OS (`:android:wear`)

Tiles: `ReadinessTileService`, `LastNightTileService`, `MedsDueTileService`; complications: readiness number, rings, water. Quick-log Wear activity mirrors watchOS set (water/caffeine/mood/symptom/med). Data path: Wear Data Layer (`WearDataRelay.kt`) with the same queued-replay semantics as 49.9; workout capture uses Health Services on Wear, landing in HC → normal adapter path.

### 50.8 OEM battery-optimization onboarding component

`features/onboarding/BatteryCoachScreen.kt` + `platform/oem/OemPlaybook.kt`: detects manufacturer (`Build.MANUFACTURER` × known ROM quirks), loads per-OEM steps from `content/oem-playbook/*.yaml` (CMS-updatable without release — the v1 §37.6 playbook), requests `ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` where policy-appropriate, and verifies afterwards via a sync-latency self-check (`hc_changes_poll` gap monitor) that surfaces the "opens refresh your data" degraded mode honestly (v1 §37.3 case 14).

### 50.9 ProGuard/R8 rules for KMP

`android/app/proguard-badan.pro`: keep `kotlinx.serialization` serializers for `net.badan.**` (`-keepclassmembers @kotlinx.serialization.Serializable class net.badan.** { *; }` + generated companions); keep SQLDelight driver classes and SQLCipher JNI (`net.sqlcipher.**`); keep Wire-generated proto adapters; strip `kotlinx.coroutines.debug`; no reflection elsewhere by policy (arch lint forbids `Class.forName` in core). R8 full mode on; `:android:baselineprofile` regenerates profiles per release train.

### 50.10 Build variants

`debug` (dev backend, flag panel, StrictMode), `beta` (staging, Play internal track, sampled analytics), `release`. One flavor dimension reserved (`store`) for future alternative-store builds; not used at launch.

### 50.11 Android test harnesses

1. **JVM/Robolectric:** ViewModels + UiState reducers with fixture facades (fast lane; no emulator).
2. **Compose UI tests:** screen-level semantics tests + screenshot tests (Roborazzi) themes × RTL × font scales — same matrix as iOS snapshots.
3. **Instrumented (managed devices):** HC adapter against the real Health Connect provider seeded by `tooling/fixture-gen` APK; permission-denial matrix automation; conformance kit (§51.9).
4. **Macrobenchmark:** cold start <400 ms cached (baseline profile enforced), 1-year chart frame timing.
5. **Device zoo (beta ring):** Samsung/Pixel/Xiaomi background-sync reality checks (v1 §33.5) reported via opt-in diagnostics.

## 51. Ingestion adapter framework

The buildable spec for v1 §11 (ingestion) and §30.6 (dedup). Everything here lives in `adapters/port-health` (interfaces) and `core-ingest` (pipeline); platform actuals in §49.7/§50.4.

### 51.1 `HealthStorePort` — full interface

`adapters/port-health/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/adapters/health/HealthStorePort.kt`:

```kotlin
interface HealthStorePort {
    suspend fun availability(): StoreAvailability   // store health: Available | UpdateRequired | NotInstalled | Unsupported
    suspend fun capabilities(): CapabilityDescriptor // static + probed; drives §12 fallbacks programmatically
    /** Per-type permission state incl. background-read where the platform splits it. */
    suspend fun permissionState(types: Set<MetricTypeId>): Map<MetricTypeId, PermissionState>
    /** Launch platform permission UX for a staged bundle; returns per-type outcome. */
    suspend fun requestPermissions(bundle: PermissionBundle): PermissionRequestResult
    /** Anchored delta read; page-sized; anchor==null → windowed initial read. */
    suspend fun readSamples(type: MetricTypeId, range: InstantRange, anchor: ReadAnchor?): SamplePage
    /** Sessions (sleep/workout) with sub-structures (stages, laps, HR series refs). */
    suspend fun readSessions(kind: SessionKind, range: InstantRange, anchor: ReadAnchor?): SessionPage
    fun observe(types: Set<MetricTypeId>): Flow<StoreChangeEvent>  // change events: types + reason (delivery|permission|reset)
    suspend fun enableBackgroundDelivery(types: Set<MetricTypeId>): BackgroundDeliveryResult  // reports granted cadence
    /** Write-back (v1 §11.5); records carry BADAN sync-identifier for self-source filtering. */
    suspend fun writeRecords(records: List<WriteRecord>): WriteResult
    suspend fun deleteOwnRecords(ids: List<ExternalRecordId>): DeleteResult  // own-written records only (platform rule)
    suspend fun sourcesFor(type: MetricTypeId): List<StoreSource>  // Data Sources UI (v1 §6.2)
    /** Deepest readable history for a type (HK: full; HC: 30d default) → backfill plan + archive-import prompt. */
    suspend fun historicalWindow(type: MetricTypeId): InstantRange?
}
```

All returns are wrapped in a `PortResult<T>` (sealed: `Ok`, `Denied(kind)`, `StoreUnavailable(state)`, `TransientFailure(retryAfter)`, `PermanentFailure(code)`) so the pipeline's error policy (51.5) is type-driven, not exception-driven.

### 51.2 Capability descriptor model

```kotlin
data class CapabilityDescriptor(
    val store: StoreKind,                       // HK | HC | VENDOR(vendorId) | IMPORT(format)
    val storeVersion: String?,                  // HC provider version / iOS version
    val types: Map<MetricTypeId, TypeCapability>,
    val background: BackgroundCapability,       // Immediate | Hourly | PollOnly | None
    val historicalDepth: HistoricalDepth,       // Full | Days(n) | Unknown
)
data class TypeCapability(
    val read: Support, val write: Support,      // Support = Full | Partial(note) | None
    val series: Boolean,                        // beat-to-beat / intraday series available
    val sinceVersion: String?,                  // e.g., HC alcohol type gated by version (v1 §12.4)
)
```

Registry entries (§48.6) reference required capabilities; `core-registry` × `CapabilityDescriptor` join computes each module's denied/degraded state matrix — the programmatic form of v1 §12's ✅/🔶/🔌/✍️ legend.

### 51.3 `VendorApiAdapter` + webhook delivery DTOs

```kotlin
interface VendorApiAdapter {                    // Garmin, Dexcom, Oura, broker (v1 §13)
    val vendorId: VendorId
    suspend fun beginAuth(): AuthRedirect                        // OAuth URL, PKCE
    suspend fun completeAuth(callback: AuthCallback): VendorConnection
    suspend fun refreshAuthHealth(conn: VendorConnection): AuthHealth   // feeds S-60 status
    suspend fun pull(conn: VendorConnection, cursor: VendorCursor?): VendorBatch   // polling fallback
    fun capabilities(): CapabilityDescriptor
}
```

Webhook path (backend integration hub, v1 §31.2) delivers to the device queue as DTOs defined in `contracts/api/backend-openapi.yaml`:

```yaml
VendorDeliveryDto: { delivery_id: ulid, vendor: enum, user_ref: opaque, idempotency_key: string,
                     payload_kind: enum[activity, sleep, glucose_series, body, workout_file],
                     transport_schema_version: semver, encrypted_payload: base64, expires_at: date-time }
```

Device acks by `delivery_id`; unacked deliveries replay for 7 days (v1 §31.4); decrypted payloads enter the same `NormalizationPipeline` with `path=vendor_api`.

### 51.4 `ArchiveImporter` + streaming parse contract

```kotlin
interface ArchiveImporter {
    val format: ArchiveFormat                    // AppleHealthZip | GarminTakeout | OuraTakeout | FitbitTakeout | GenericCsv
    suspend fun probe(file: FileHandle): ImportPlan          // detected types, est. rows, date span, unit warnings
    fun parse(file: FileHandle, plan: ImportPlan): Flow<RawRecordChunk>   // streaming: ≤5k records/chunk, constant memory
    suspend fun resume(batchId: UlidBatchId): Flow<RawRecordChunk>        // from persisted chunk cursor
}
```

Contract: parsers never materialize the archive (XML/CSV pull-parsed); each chunk is transactionally committed with `batch_id` + chunk index so cancel/undo/resume operate on `import_batches` rows (§52.2); `GenericCsv` runs the unit-guard mapping UI (E-15) before parse.

### 51.5 Pipeline stage classes

Order fixed per v1 §11.3; each stage stamps `stage_version` into the batch record.

| Stage class (core-ingest/stages/) | Input → Output | Error policy | Fixture set (core-testing/fixtures/ingest/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SourceTagger` | `RawRecordChunk` → `TaggedRecord[]` (Provenance attached) | missing source metadata → tag `unknown_source` flag, continue | `tagger/hk_watch.json`, `tagger/hc_samsung.json`, `tagger/import_no_device.json` |
| `UnitNormalizer` | `TaggedRecord` → `NormalizedRecord` (SI-canonical + original kept) | unknown unit → quarantine record + `UnitQuarantined` journal row; batch continues | `units/mgdl_mmol.json`, `units/lb_kg.json`, `units/unknown_unit.json` |
| `TimezoneResolver` | `NormalizedRecord` → +`tzId`, UTC canonical ts | absent tz → device-tz-at-ingest + `tz_assumed` quality flag | `tz/dst_spring.json`, `tz/travel_shift.json`, `tz/future_clock_skew.json` (quarantines future samples, v1 §37.4) |
| `TypeMapper` | platform type → `MetricTypeId` via `HkTypeMap`/`HcTypeMap` | unmapped type → retained in raw log, counted, not an error | `typemap/hk_full_sweep.json`, `typemap/hc_versioned_types.json` |
| `QualityFlagger` | record → +`QualityFlags` (bounds, artifacts) | never drops; flags only (visible-but-marked, v1 §37.5) | `quality/hr_spike.json`, `quality/cgm_compression_low.json`, `quality/spo2_altitude.json` |
| `DedupEngine` | records × existing window → keep/suppress decisions | rule conflict → prefer conservative (keep both, suppress none) + journal `conflict` row | conformance suite 51.9 (≥40 cases, CI-blocking per E-03.2) |
| `SessionAssembler` | samples/sessions → stitched `Session`s | unresolvable overlap → keep both sessions + `needs_user_choice` flag (S-xx reconciliation UI) | `assembler/*` (51.7) |
| `AggregateComputer` | canonical records → daily/hourly aggregate upserts (§52.6 tiers) | arithmetic overflow/NaN → skip cell + integrity log | `aggregate/day_rollover_tz.json`, `aggregate/partial_day.json` |
| `RecomputeNotifier` | batch summary → `IngestBatchCompleted` event (§48.7) | bus failure → event persisted to `jobs.sq/pending_events`, redelivered | `events/batch_completed_replay.json` |

### 51.6 DedupEngine rule inventory + decision journal

Rules evaluated in priority order (first-match wins per record pair); all thresholds live in remote config (fixable without release, v1 §30.6):

| # | Rule class (core-ingest/dedup/rules/) | Targets | Logic sketch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ExactHashRule` | imports vs anything | content hash (type, ts, value, source uuid) equal → suppress newcomer |
| 2 | `PlatformIdentityRule` | re-syncs | deterministic id (source UUID + type, v1 §30.5) equal → upsert, never duplicate |
| 3 | `SelfSourceRule` | own write-backs | BADAN sync-identifier prefix → drop at door (never re-ingest, v1 §11.5) |
| 4 | `ManualAuthorityRule` | weight/BP/labs | manual entry wins vs device same-window; both retained, device suppressed (v1 §11.4) |
| 5 | `SessionSimilarityRule` | sleep/workouts | boundary overlap ≥70% + same kind → merge candidates → SessionAssembler |
| 6 | `OverlapAggregateRule` | steps/energy/distance | interval overlap + magnitude similarity → primary-source election by user priority ranking |
| 7 | `AdherenceWindowRule` | med logs | same regimen ≤5 min apart → collapse w/ undo (v1 §37.2 case 11) |
| 8 | `ImportOverLiveRule` | archive batches | window pre-scan → per-record fallthrough to rules 1/5/6; produces import report counts |

Decision journal — table `dedup_decisions` (in `jobs.sq`, §52.1):

```sql
CREATE TABLE dedup_decisions (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,  batch_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  rule TEXT NOT NULL,  rule_version TEXT NOT NULL,          -- rule class name + version
  kept_record_id TEXT,                                      -- winner (nullable for collapse cases)
  suppressed_record_id TEXT,                                -- loser; mirrors samples.suppressed_by
  score REAL,                                               -- similarity score where applicable
  reversible INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,  decided_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  detail TEXT                                               -- JSON: thresholds, overlap %, sources
);
```

Reversal = clear `suppressed_by` + journal a compensating row; lineage sheets (v1 §20.4) render straight from this table.

### 51.7 SessionAssembler algorithms

**Sleep stitching (`assembler/SleepStitcher.kt`):**
1. Collect candidate segments per local-night window (18:00 → 14:00 next day, tz-resolved).
2. Merge same-source segments separated by <30 min gaps (awake-in-bed bridging); gaps become `awake` stage spans.
3. Cross-source: if boundary overlap ≥70% → elect primary by source ranking (user-overridable, remembered); non-primary retained with `suppressed_by`, surfaced as "2 sources, view both" (v1 §37.2 case 7).
4. Classify primary vs nap: duration ≥3 h AND midpoint inside user's typical sleep window → primary; else nap; user reclassification stored as source-pattern hint (v1 §37.5 case 25).
5. Join overnight covariate samples (HR/RR/SpO₂/wrist temp) into session aggregates via session-window join (v1 §12.2).
Fixtures: `assembler/ring_vs_watch_night.json`, `assembler/split_night_wakeup.json`, `assembler/nap_afternoon.json`, `assembler/shift_worker_day_sleep.json`, `assembler/dst_night.json`.

**Workout merge (`assembler/WorkoutMerger.kt`):**
1. Signature = (type taxonomy id, start ±3 min, duration ±10%) → merge candidates (v1 §37.2 case 8).
2. Winner = richer source (has HR series > has laps > summary-only); loser suppressed; winner's session absorbs any fields it lacks from loser (`merged_from` array in session detail JSON).
3. Manual quick-add overlapping an imported workout → prompt-once, remembered preference.
Fixtures: `assembler/garmin_plus_hk_dupe.json`, `assembler/strength_manual_vs_watch.json`, `assembler/back_to_back_intervals.json`.

### 51.8 Backpressure and batching model

- Ingest is single-writer: `IngestScheduler` owns a serialized queue (Kotlin `Channel(UNLIMITED)` of `IngestJob`, one consumer coroutine) — SQLite write-lock contention eliminated by design.
- Debounce: store change events coalesce per 90 s window per store; backfill/import jobs run at `low` priority and yield every chunk (thermal/battery-aware, v1 §32.3).
- Chunk sizes: platform delta reads 2k records/page; archive chunks ≤5k; pipeline transactions per chunk (crash = at-most-one-chunk replay, idempotent by rules 1–2).
- Live-import UX: progress events per chunk (`ImportProgress(batchId, done, total)`) feed the foreground-service notification (50.5) and iOS progress Live Activity (v1 §24.3).

### 51.9 Adapter conformance test kit

`core-testing/adapter-kit/HealthStorePortConformanceKit.kt` — abstract suite every adapter (HK, HC, vendor, importer-backed fake store) must extend and pass:

1. **Idempotent re-read:** same range twice → zero new canonical records.
2. **Anchor continuity:** write-after-anchor is returned exactly once; anchor survives process restart.
3. **Deletion propagation:** store-side delete → tombstone suppression within one poll cycle.
4. **Permission downgrade:** revoked type → `Denied` result, no exception, no partial rows.
5. **Capability honesty:** every type claimed `Full` read must return fixture data; `None` must return `Unsupported`.
6. **Self-source filtering:** adapter's own `writeRecords` output never re-ingested.
7. **Unit fidelity:** fixture values survive normalize→export round-trip within precision (registry-driven).
8. **Timezone battery:** DST spring/fall + travel fixtures produce correct local-night attribution.
9. **Throughput floor:** 100k-sample backfill completes under memory ceiling (streamed), measured.
10. **Dedup handshake:** overlapping fixture from a second fake source yields journal rows, not duplicates.

New adapter = new `XxxStoreConformanceTest : HealthStorePortConformanceKit()` + recorded fixture pack; CI-blocking, same suite both platforms (byte-identical expectations, v1 §33.4).

## 52. Persistence schema plan

Implements v1 §30 (entities, timeseries strategy, governance) and §32.5 (crypto). One SQLCipher database per user profile; a second DB namespace for sensitive-plus classes (purge-on-disable, v1 §28.7).

### 52.1 SQLDelight file inventory

`core-db/src/commonMain/sqldelight/net/badan/db/` — one `.sq` per aggregate; queries live beside their tables:

| File | Tables (primary) | Named queries (examples) |
|---|---|---|
| `samples.sq` | `samples`, `interval_records` | `samplesForMetricRange`, `latestSample`, `suppressedForLineage` |
| `sessions.sq` | `sessions`, `session_stages`, `session_metrics` | `sessionsForNight`, `workoutsInRange`, `sessionWithStages` |
| `event_records.sq` | `event_records`, `status_intervals` | `timelineWindow`, `eventsOfTypeRange`, `activeStatusAt` |
| `derived_values.sq` | `derived_values`, `input_manifests` | `latestScore`, `scoreHistory`, `manifestForValue` |
| `baselines.sq` | `baselines` | `baselineFor(metric, context)`, `provisionalBaselines` |
| `insights.sq` | `insights`, `insight_feedback`, `insight_cooldowns` | `undeliveredCandidates`, `feedbackForTemplate` |
| `sources.sq` | `source_connections`, `source_devices`, `source_priorities` | `connectionsWithHealth`, `priorityRanking(metric)` |
| `meds.sq` | `medication_regimens`, `adherence_events`, `conditions`, `condition_links` | `dueDoses(day)`, `adherenceRateRange`, `regimenChangeMarkers` |
| `customization.sq` | `customization_profiles`, `consent_records`, `flag_overrides` | `activeLayout(surface)`, `consentState(class)` |
| `sync.sq` | `sync_oplog`, `sync_state`, `read_anchors`, `tombstones` | `pendingOps`, `anchorFor(store, type)` |
| `search.sq` | `search_fts` (FTS5), `search_synonyms` | `searchAll(query)` — grammar + usage owned by §58 |
| `jobs.sq` | `import_batches`, `export_jobs`, `ingest_log`, `dedup_decisions`, `pending_events`, `job_checkpoints` | `resumableBatches`, `exportHistory` |
| `aggregates.sq` | `agg_hourly`, `agg_daily`, `agg_weekly` | `dailySeries(metric, range)` — chart fast-path |

### 52.2 DDL sketches — the 12 most important tables

Types: `TEXT` ULIDs (v1 §30.5), `INTEGER` epoch-millis UTC, `TEXT` JSON for closed payloads. Provenance is denormalized columns (struct-on-every-record, v1 §30.1), not a join.

```sql
-- samples.sq ------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE samples (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                       -- ulid
  metric_id TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- registry id: vitals.hrv_rmssd
  value REAL NOT NULL,                       -- SI-canonical
  original_value REAL, original_unit TEXT,   -- as-received (v1 §11.3)
  measured_at INTEGER NOT NULL, recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  tz_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_connection_id TEXT NOT NULL,        -- FK sources.source_connections
  source_device_id TEXT,                     -- FK sources.source_devices
  ingestion_path TEXT NOT NULL,              -- platform|vendor|broker|manual|import
  batch_id TEXT,                             -- FK jobs.import_batches / ingest batch
  external_id TEXT,                          -- platform UUID (deterministic identity)
  quality_flags INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- bitmask (gap_filled, artifact, tz_assumed…)
  suppressed_by TEXT                         -- dedup pointer; NULL = live (Law 5: never deleted)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_samples_identity ON samples(metric_id, external_id, source_connection_id)
  WHERE external_id IS NOT NULL;             -- idempotent re-sync
CREATE INDEX idx_samples_metric_time ON samples(metric_id, measured_at);   -- the workhorse
CREATE INDEX idx_samples_batch ON samples(batch_id);                        -- batch undo

CREATE TABLE interval_records (              -- aggregates with duration (steps buckets…)
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, metric_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  start_at INTEGER NOT NULL, end_at INTEGER NOT NULL, tz_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  value REAL NOT NULL, original_value REAL, original_unit TEXT,
  source_connection_id TEXT NOT NULL, source_device_id TEXT, ingestion_path TEXT NOT NULL,
  batch_id TEXT, external_id TEXT, quality_flags INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, suppressed_by TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX idx_intervals_metric_start ON interval_records(metric_id, start_at, end_at);

-- sessions.sq -----------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE sessions (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL,                        -- sleep_primary|sleep_nap|workout
  subtype TEXT,                              -- workout taxonomy id
  start_at INTEGER NOT NULL, end_at INTEGER NOT NULL, tz_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  local_night TEXT,                          -- 'YYYY-MM-DD' attribution for sleep (v1 §37.4)
  source_connection_id TEXT NOT NULL, source_device_id TEXT, ingestion_path TEXT NOT NULL,
  batch_id TEXT, external_id TEXT,
  detail TEXT,                               -- JSON: laps, merged_from[], strength sets ref
  quality_flags INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, suppressed_by TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_kind_start ON sessions(kind, start_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_local_night ON sessions(local_night) WHERE kind LIKE 'sleep%';

CREATE TABLE session_stages (                -- sleep stages / workout segments
  session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id), seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
  stage TEXT NOT NULL, start_at INTEGER NOT NULL, end_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (session_id, seq));

-- event_records.sq --------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE event_records (                 -- closed union (v1 §30.1)
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  event_type TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- meal|symptom|med_adherence|note|status|lab_result|cycle_event|measurement
  payload_schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
  payload TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- typed JSON per event_type (contract-validated)
  occurred_at INTEGER NOT NULL, recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL, tz_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_connection_id TEXT, ingestion_path TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual',
  batch_id TEXT, quality_flags INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, suppressed_by TEXT,
  edited_at INTEGER, edit_audit TEXT         -- JSON audit trail (v1 §21.1)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_events_type_time ON event_records(event_type, occurred_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_events_time ON event_records(occurred_at);        -- unified Timeline

-- derived_values.sq -------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE derived_values (                -- append-only (v1 §30.1: never overwrite)
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, metric_id TEXT NOT NULL,   -- scores are registry metrics (v1 §10.17)
  period_key TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- 'day:2026-07-10' | 'session:<ulid>' | 'week:2026-W28'
  value REAL NOT NULL, confidence REAL, provisional INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  algorithm_id TEXT NOT NULL, algorithm_version TEXT NOT NULL,
  computed_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  input_manifest_id TEXT REFERENCES input_manifests(id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_derived_lookup ON derived_values(metric_id, period_key, computed_at DESC);
-- UI reads: latest row per (metric_id, period_key); history remains for audit.

CREATE TABLE input_manifests (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  inputs TEXT NOT NULL);                     -- JSON: [{record_id, metric_id, weight, window}] → Score Anatomy

-- baselines.sq --------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE baselines (                     -- materialized (v1 §30.1)
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  metric_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  covariate_context TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default',   -- 'phase:luteal' | 'status:travel' | composite key
  window_days INTEGER NOT NULL,
  center REAL NOT NULL, spread REAL NOT NULL,          -- median + MAD
  band_low REAL NOT NULL, band_high REAL NOT NULL,
  n_points INTEGER NOT NULL, provisional INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  algorithm_version TEXT NOT NULL, valid_from INTEGER NOT NULL, computed_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_baseline_key ON baselines(metric_id, covariate_context, window_days, valid_from);

-- insights.sq ---------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE insights (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, template_id TEXT NOT NULL, template_version TEXT NOT NULL,
  generated_at INTEGER NOT NULL, period_key TEXT NOT NULL,
  depth_variant TEXT NOT NULL,               -- casual|power
  rendered_text TEXT NOT NULL, locale TEXT NOT NULL,
  evidence_refs TEXT NOT NULL,               -- JSON: derived_value ids + record ids ("why am I seeing this")
  delivered_via TEXT,                        -- feed|push|digest|none
  state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'    -- candidate|shown|dismissed|snoozed
);
CREATE INDEX idx_insights_template_time ON insights(template_id, generated_at);

-- sources.sq ---------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE source_connections (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT NOT NULL,   -- kind: platform_store|vendor|broker|manual|import
  vendor_id TEXT, display_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  auth_state TEXT,                           -- ok|expiring|expired|revoked (S-60)
  connected_at INTEGER NOT NULL, last_delivery_at INTEGER,
  hidden INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0          -- hide-source (Bevel parity)
);
CREATE TABLE source_priorities (             -- per-metric ranking overrides (v1 §11.4)
  metric_id TEXT NOT NULL, source_connection_id TEXT NOT NULL, rank INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (metric_id, source_connection_id));

-- meds.sq --------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE medication_regimens (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, medication_name TEXT NOT NULL, ingredient TEXT, strength TEXT, form TEXT, route TEXT,
  schedule TEXT NOT NULL,                    -- JSON: pattern (times/PRN/cycling/taper)
  start_at INTEGER NOT NULL, end_at INTEGER,
  change_note TEXT                           -- feeds regimen-change chart markers (v1 §21.5)
);
CREATE TABLE adherence_events (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, regimen_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES medication_regimens(id),
  due_at INTEGER, acted_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  action TEXT NOT NULL,                      -- taken|late|skipped
  skip_reason TEXT, tz_id TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE INDEX idx_adherence_regimen_time ON adherence_events(regimen_id, acted_at);

-- sync.sq ---------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE sync_oplog (
  seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  entity TEXT NOT NULL, entity_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  op TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- upsert|tombstone
  device_id TEXT NOT NULL, lamport INTEGER NOT NULL,     -- logical clock (v1 §34.2)
  payload_cipher BLOB,                       -- E2E envelope; server-opaque
  sensitivity_class TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'standard',    -- selective sync gate (v1 §34.2)
  pushed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);
CREATE INDEX idx_oplog_pending ON sync_oplog(pushed, seq);
CREATE TABLE read_anchors (                  -- HK anchors + HC changes tokens (§49.7/§50.4)
  store TEXT NOT NULL, type_id TEXT NOT NULL, anchor BLOB NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (store, type_id));

-- jobs.sq -----------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE import_batches (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, source_kind TEXT NOT NULL, file_name TEXT, started_at INTEGER NOT NULL, finished_at INTEGER,
  state TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- probing|running|paused|done|undone
  chunk_cursor INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- resume point (§51.4)
  counts TEXT                                -- JSON: {added, updated, suppressed} → import report
);
-- + dedup_decisions (DDL in §51.6), ingest_log (raw payload retention refs),
--   pending_events, export_jobs, job_checkpoints

-- aggregates.sq --------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE agg_daily (
  metric_id TEXT NOT NULL, day TEXT NOT NULL,            -- 'YYYY-MM-DD' local
  min REAL, max REAL, avg REAL, sum REAL, n INTEGER NOT NULL,
  coverage REAL,                             -- fraction of expected samples present
  computed_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (metric_id, day)
);
-- agg_hourly / agg_weekly identical shape with hour/week keys
```

### 52.3 Index inventory with query justifications

| Index | Serves |
|---|---|
| `idx_samples_metric_time` | metric detail charts, baseline windows, export range scans — the single hottest path |
| `idx_samples_identity` (partial unique) | idempotent platform re-sync; makes `PlatformIdentityRule` an upsert |
| `idx_samples_batch` / `idx_intervals_*` batch | one-tap import undo (v1 §37.2 case 9) |
| `idx_sessions_local_night` (partial) | "last night" queries, Sleep Bank ledger, night attribution across DST/travel |
| `idx_events_time` + `idx_events_type_time` | unified Timeline interleave; symptom/med filtered lists |
| `idx_derived_lookup` (DESC) | latest-score reads on Today (<400 ms cold-start budget: single index hit per ring) |
| `idx_baseline_key` (unique) | band rendering is a lookup, never a model run (v1 §30.1) |
| `idx_oplog_pending` | sync push batching without full scans |
| `idx_adherence_regimen_time` | adherence-rate rollups + physician report ranges |
| `agg_daily` PK | multi-year chart render <100 ms via tier selection (52.6), no raw scans |

Rule: any new query added to a `.sq` file must cite its index in the PR description; `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` snapshot tests in `core-db` fail on full-table scans over `samples`, `event_records`, `sync_oplog`.

### 52.4 Encryption setup (SQLCipher key flow)

1. First launch: `DbKeyProvider` generates 256-bit `dbKey` via `port-crypto` CSPRNG.
2. `dbKey` wrapped by platform keystore: iOS Keychain (`kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` — background ingest must run pre-unlock-session) / Android Keystore AES-GCM. Raw key never touches disk.
3. `DatabaseFactory` opens SQLCipher with `PRAGMA key`; `PRAGMA cipher_memory_security = ON`; verify with `PRAGMA cipher_integrity_check` on open (v1 §37.6 case 30 → snapshot restore path).
4. Sensitive-plus namespace (cycle etc.) = second DB file `badan_sensitive.db`, own wrapped key → disable-module purge is file deletion + key destruction (v1 §28.7).
5. Key hierarchy up-chain (device key → sync key → export passphrase) is `core-sync/crypto/KeyHierarchy.kt` per v1 §32.5; DB key never leaves device, never syncs.
6. App-group access (iOS widgets) uses the same Keychain access group; widgets get read-only pre-rendered snapshots anyway (49.8) so extension DB opens are rare.

### 52.5 Migration framework rules

- **Forward-only** `.sqm` migrations (`migrations/1.sqm…N.sqm`); no down-migrations ever ship (restore = resync/reimport story, v1 §37.6).
- Every released schema version gets a frozen fixture DB `core-testing/fixtures/db/vN.db` (seeded, encrypted with test key); migration test matrix runs vK→vN for **all** K<N on every PR touching `.sq`/`.sqm` (v1 §30.4).
- Migrations must be resumable-safe: each wrapped in a transaction; long data migrations (recompute-style) are *not* done in `.sqm` — they enqueue a `job_checkpoints` backfill job post-migration (UI shows "upgrading your data" state).
- Destructive changes (column drop) require: two-release deprecation (write-both), ADR, and export-schema impact note (§48.4) — internal refactors never break the published dictionary (decoupled mapping layer, v1 §30.4).
- Soak test: E-24 schema-migration soak runs the full K→N matrix against a 5-year synthetic heavy-user DB (52.7) nightly.

### 52.6 Retention and decimation tiers

Raw is sacred for manual/lab/session data (never decimated). High-frequency device series decimate by tier (v1 §30.2):

| Tier | Table | Resolution | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| T0 raw | `samples` | as-received | 24 months for continuous HR-class series; forever for everything else |
| T1 | `agg_hourly` | hourly stats | forever |
| T2 | `agg_daily` | daily stats + coverage | forever |
| T3 | `agg_weekly` | weekly stats | forever |

Decimation job runs inside `nightly-recompute`; T0 rows past retention are exported to the local archive spool first if the user enabled "keep raw forever" (Files/Drive), then removed — with the policy stated in Settings and the export manifest (ownership honesty). Chart renderer picks tier by zoom (raw <7d, hourly <90d, daily <2y, weekly beyond).

### 52.7 Size-budget model

Heavy-user synthetic profile (continuous HR, nightly sleep, 2 workouts/day, CGM, full logging): T0 HR ≈ 1 sample/5 s ≈ 17k rows/day ≈ 95 B/row ≈ 1.6 MB/day → 24-month cap ≈ 1.2 GB *uncapped*; with 5-second→minute pre-aggregation at ingest for continuous series (registry-flagged `preaggregate: minute`) → ~80 MB/24mo. All other families ≈ 15–30 MB/multi-year. Target envelope: **50–150 MB multi-year** (v1 §32.6) enforced by a `DbSizeBudgetTest` running the 5-year synthetic generator (`tooling/fixture-gen/heavy-user`) and asserting post-decimation size; storage meter surfaced in Settings (v1 §37.7 case 35).

### 52.8 FTS5 virtual tables

`search.sq`: `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE search_fts USING fts5(entity_type, entity_id UNINDEXED, title, body, locale, tokenize='unicode61 remove_diacritics 2');` — populated by `core-search/SearchIndexer` from registry names/synonyms (EN+AR), notes, symptoms/meds/conditions, insights, education slugs. `search_synonyms` maps cross-script aliases ("hrv" ↔ Arabic label). Query grammar, ranking, and the search experience are owned by §58; this section owns only the storage: triggers keep FTS in sync on `event_records`/`insights` writes, and FTS tables are excluded from sync (rebuildable) and from exports.

## 53. Sync engine implementation plan

Implements v1 §34 (offline/sync/conflict doctrine: local-first, E2E-encrypted, convergence-not-gating) and v1 §31.2 (blind Sync service). The device DB is the source of truth; the server is an opaque replication target that stores encrypted blobs and change-feed metadata only. This section specifies the client engine in `core/core-sync/`, the wire contract in `contracts/sync/`, and the two-device test harness in `core/core-testing/`.

### 53.1 Architecture

```
Repositories (core-db) ──write interceptor──▶ OplogWriter ──▶ sync_oplog (SQLDelight)
                                                                │
SyncEngine (core-sync) ◀── SyncScheduler (triggers: app-fg, push-poke, periodic, oplog-threshold)
   │  SessionRunner (state machine §53.6)
   ├─▶ EnvelopeCodec (E2E encrypt/decrypt, CryptoPort)          │
   ├─▶ TransportClient (HTTP/2 to backend/services/sync per contracts/api/backend-openapi.yaml + contracts/sync/sync.proto)
   ├─▶ ConflictPipeline (detect → classify per v1 §34.3 → resolve → emit SyncConflictDetected)
   └─▶ ApplyWriter (inbound ops → repositories, marked origin=sync to suppress re-capture)
```

Key invariants (enforced by tests in §53.13): (1) derived values never enter the oplog — they are recomputed locally from synced inputs (v1 §34.3); (2) the server never receives a plaintext byte of any entity payload; (3) applying the same op twice is a no-op (idempotent apply keyed by `op_id`); (4) a device can always operate with sync disabled — `core-sync` is an optional dependency wired only when the sync consent purpose (v1 §28.3) is granted.

### 53.2 Components and file paths

| Component | Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `SyncEngine` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/SyncEngine.kt` | Facade: start/stop, status flow, force-sync |
| `OplogWriter` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/oplog/OplogWriter.kt` | Serializes entity mutations into `sync_oplog` rows inside the same DB transaction as the write |
| `OplogCompactor` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/oplog/OplogCompactor.kt` | Coalesces superseded ops pre-upload; prunes acked ops |
| `EnvelopeCodec` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/crypto/EnvelopeCodec.kt` | Encrypt/decrypt `SyncEnvelopeDto` via `CryptoPort` |
| `KeyRing` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/crypto/KeyRing.kt` | Key hierarchy per v1 §32.5: device key → sync master key (recovery-phrase derivable) → per-class content keys |
| `SessionRunner` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/session/SessionRunner.kt` | Drives the §53.6 state machine |
| `TransportClient` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/transport/TransportClient.kt` | Ktor client for the blind-store API (§53.8) |
| `ConflictPipeline` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/conflict/ConflictPipeline.kt` | §53.7 |
| `ApplyWriter` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/apply/ApplyWriter.kt` | Transactional inbound apply + tombstone handling |
| `HydrationRunner` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/hydration/HydrationRunner.kt` | New-device full-history restore (§53.10) |
| `SyncScheduler` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/SyncScheduler.kt` | Trigger debounce, backoff (§53.11), circuit breaker |
| `SelectiveSyncPolicy` | `core/core-sync/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/sync/policy/SelectiveSyncPolicy.kt` | Consent-gated class filter (§53.9) |
| Wire schemas | `contracts/sync/sync.proto`, `contracts/sync/protocol.md` | Frozen envelope + session messages |
| Server | `backend/services/sync/` | Blob store, change feeds, device registry (no decryption capability) |

### 53.3 Oplog design

Table `sync_oplog` in `core/core-db/src/commonMain/sqldelight/net/badan/db/sync_oplog.sq`:

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `op_id` | TEXT PK | ULID (offline-generatable, sortable — v1 §30.5) |
| `device_id` | TEXT | stable per-install id |
| `lamport` | INTEGER | per-device monotonic counter (logical clock per v1 §34.2) |
| `entity_kind` | TEXT | enum: `event_record`, `session`, `sample_manual`, `medication_regimen`, `adherence_event`, `customization_profile`, `consent_record`, `insight_feedback`, `ai_memory`, `saved_view`, `import_batch_meta` |
| `entity_id` | TEXT | target ULID |
| `op_kind` | TEXT | `UPSERT`, `PATCH` (field-level LWW map), `DELETE` (tombstone), `IMPORT_BATCH_MARK`, `UNDO_BATCH` |
| `data_class` | TEXT | `standard` \| `sensitive_plus` \| `derived_meta` (drives §53.9 gating; classes per v1 §28.2) |
| `payload` | BLOB | canonical protobuf of the entity delta (plaintext at rest locally — DB is SQLCipher-encrypted) |
| `schema_version` | INTEGER | payload schema semver-major |
| `created_at` / `hlc_ts` | INTEGER | wall + hybrid logical clock timestamp |
| `upload_state` | TEXT | `pending` → `inflight` → `acked` (acked rows pruned by compactor after 7d) |

Op kinds deliberately exclude platform-imported samples: those are re-derived on every device from its own store or from vendor delivery queues (deterministic ids make re-sync idempotent — v1 §34.3 row 1). Only *user-authored* and *device-unique* data syncs; this keeps oplog volume small (target: <500 ops/day heavy logger).

**Change capture.** Every repository write method in `core-db` repositories (`EventRecordRepository`, `SessionRepository`, `CustomizationRepository`…) accepts a `WriteOrigin` (`USER`, `INGEST`, `SYNC`, `MIGRATION`). A SQLDelight-transaction-scoped interceptor (`OplogWriteInterceptor` installed by `core-sync` DI) appends an oplog row for `USER` writes to syncable `entity_kind`s in the same transaction — capture can never be lost to a crash between write and log. `SYNC`-origin writes bypass capture (loop prevention layer 1).

### 53.4 E2E envelope format

Defined in `contracts/sync/sync.proto` as `SyncEnvelopeDto`; layering:

```
layer 0 (server-visible): envelope_id, user_id, device_id, seq (server-assigned feed cursor),
                          data_class_bucket ("std"|"sp"), size, created_at   ← routing metadata only
layer 1 (encrypted, AES-256-GCM, content key K_class[key_id]):
        op batch: repeated { op_id, lamport, hlc_ts, entity_kind, entity_id, op_kind,
                             schema_version, payload_bytes }
layer 2 (per-attachment): content-addressed blob ids (BLAKE3 hash), each blob separately
        encrypted with a derived blob key; envelope carries only ids + keys-wrapped-by-K_class
```

Key ids: every envelope's layer-1 header names `key_id` (e.g., `sync-std-k3`). `KeyRing` supports rotation: new envelopes use the newest key; old keys retained for decrypt; rotation event itself syncs as an `UPSERT` on a `keyring_state` entity encrypted under the master key. Sensitive-plus envelopes use a distinct content key (`sync-sp-k*`) so revoking sensitive-class sync consent can be enforced by destroying that key client-side and issuing server-side bucket deletion (§53.9).

### 53.5 Session protocol state machine

`SessionRunner` states (protocol messages in `contracts/sync/protocol.md`):

```
IDLE → HANDSHAKE:   POST /v1/sync/session {device_id, protocol_version, cursor_map}
                    → server returns {session_token, server_cursor_map, throttle_hints}
HANDSHAKE → PULL:   GET /v1/sync/changes?since=<cursor> (paged, 256 envelopes/page)
                    each page: decrypt → ConflictPipeline → ApplyWriter → advance local cursor
PULL → PUSH:        compact pending oplog → batch into ≤1 MiB envelopes → PUT /v1/sync/changes
PUSH → ACK:         server responds per-envelope {envelope_id, seq}; mark ops acked
ACK → COMPACT:      OplogCompactor prunes acked ops; if new pending ops appeared → PUSH
COMPACT → DONE:     emit SyncCycleCompleted domain event (contracts/events/domain-events.yaml);
                    update SyncStatus flow (drives v1 §34.4 status surface S-02)
any state → FAILED(reason) → SyncScheduler backoff (§53.11)
```

Pull-before-push is mandatory: it guarantees the conflict pipeline sees remote state before local ops upload, so field-level LWW merges are computed once, on the pushing device, and re-verified deterministically on receivers (same HLC comparison → same result).

### 53.6 Conflict pipeline

`ConflictPipeline.process(inbound: Op, local: EntityState?): Resolution` — stages:

1. **Detect** — conflict iff inbound targets an `entity_id` with local unacked ops or a newer local `hlc_ts`.
2. **Classify** — per the v1 §34.3 matrix, keyed by `entity_kind`: platform samples (unreachable — not synced); manual logs → `FIELD_LWW_WITH_AUDIT`; customization → `KEY_LWW`; deletions → `TOMBSTONE_WINS_WITH_GRACE` (7-day grace: an edit after a tombstone within grace resurrects with notice); import-batch undo → `BATCH_SCOPED`.
3. **Resolve** — `FIELD_LWW_WITH_AUDIT`: merge field maps by max HLC per field; if any *materially different* field lost (value fields, not timestamps), write a conflict copy to `event_records` audit payload (`conflict_of` pointer) — v1 §34.3 "conflict copy retained".
4. **Record** — emit `SyncConflictDetected { entityKind, entityId, policy, materiallyLossy }`; only `materiallyLossy=true` surfaces UX ("kept both versions of your note from Tuesday" — v1 §34.4); the rest go to diagnostic logs (§57.B).

### 53.7 Server blind-store API (contracts/sync)

| Endpoint | Method | Server behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/sync/session` | POST | authenticate device key, mint short-lived session token, return cursors |
| `/v1/sync/changes` | GET | stream envelopes `seq > cursor` per bucket; server never inspects layer 1 |
| `/v1/sync/changes` | PUT | append-only store; assign `seq`; enforce per-user quota + size caps |
| `/v1/sync/blobs/{hash}` | PUT/GET | content-addressed encrypted attachments; dedup by hash |
| `/v1/sync/devices` | GET/DELETE | device registry; revoke device (stops its token; user-visible in settings) |
| `/v1/sync/buckets/sp` | DELETE | destroy sensitive-plus bucket on consent revocation (§53.9) |

Server-side compaction: after all registered devices' cursors pass `seq` N and age > 30d, superseded envelopes for the same `entity_id` may be dropped (server sees `entity_id` only as an opaque per-envelope *count*, so compaction uses a client-uploaded, encrypted-manifest-driven "safe-to-drop set" — the client computes it during COMPACT and posts envelope-id lists).

### 53.8 Selective-sync consent gates

`SelectiveSyncPolicy.allowed(dataClass): Boolean` reads `ConsentRecord`s (v1 §28.2/§28.3): standard-class sync requires the `sync` purpose; sensitive-plus requires the additional per-class consent. Denied classes: `OplogWriter` still captures ops (so a later grant syncs history) but `SessionRunner` filters them at PUSH; envelopes are bucketed so a `sp` grant never leaks into `std`. Consent revocation → destroy `sync-sp-k*` keys locally, call `DELETE /v1/sync/buckets/sp`, mark sp ops `local_only`. Cycle data additionally follows v1 §28.7 (excluded unless its own toggle set).

### 53.9 Hydration algorithm (new device / restore)

`HydrationRunner` (v1 §34.4 "recent data first"):

1. HANDSHAKE with empty cursors → server returns feed extents per bucket.
2. Fetch **newest-first** in reverse-seq pages; apply with `origin=SYNC`; after each page covering a full day-boundary, trigger `RecomputeCoordinator` (§54.4) for that day range — Today screen is usable after page 1.
3. Parallel lane: platform-store backfill (v1 §11.7) runs independently; dedup handles overlap.
4. Progress: `HydrationProgress(daysRestored, totalDays, phase)` flow → restore UI; resumable via persisted page cursor; interrupted hydration resumes, never restarts.
5. Completion → full forward PULL from cursor 0 gap-fill check (detects pages missed during reverse walk), then normal cycle.

### 53.10 Backoff, retry, loop detection

| Failure | Policy |
|---|---|
| Network unreachable | retry on connectivity-regained signal; no timer spin |
| 5xx / timeout | exponential backoff 30 s → 1 m → 5 m → 30 m → 6 h, ±20% jitter |
| 401 (token) | one silent re-handshake; second failure → surface auth-repair state on S-02 |
| 409 (cursor divergence) | full cursor renegotiation; if 3× in 24 h → circuit breaker |
| Quota exceeded | pause PUSH, keep PULL; surface storage notice |
| Decrypt failure (bad key_id) | quarantine envelope (`sync_quarantine` table), continue; never block feed on one poison envelope |

**Loop-detection circuit breaker:** `SyncScheduler` tracks a rolling 1 h window of cycle-triggering causes; if >12 cycles/h with ≥1 op re-uploaded for the same `entity_id` set (signature: hash of entity ids), the breaker opens for 6 h, emits `SyncLoopSuspected` diagnostic event, and flags telemetry (v1 §36.4 sync-health dashboard). Layer-2 loop prevention: `ApplyWriter` drops inbound ops whose `op_id` exists locally (self-echo) — combined with `origin=SYNC` capture suppression this makes echo loops structurally impossible; the breaker is defense-in-depth for logic bugs.

### 53.11 Failure handling summary

Crash-safety: capture is transactional (§53.3); apply is transactional per page with cursor advanced in the same transaction. Partial upload: server append is idempotent on `envelope_id`. Clock skew: HLC bounds wall-clock drift; a device with >24 h skew gets `hlc_ts` clamped and a diagnostic warning. Storage pressure: oplog capped at 50 MB; beyond cap, oldest `pending` standard-class ops trigger a "sync overdue" notice rather than data loss.

### 53.12 Test plan

Harness: `core/core-testing/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/testing/sync/TwoDeviceSimulator.kt` — two in-memory DB + `SyncEngine` instances against `FakeSyncServer` (in-process implementation of §53.7 with fault injection: drop, delay, reorder, 5xx, duplicate-delivery).

| Fixture | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `sync/fixture_two_device_meal_edit.json` | same `MealEntry` edited on A and B offline → field-LWW result identical on both; conflict copy present; `SyncConflictDetected` emitted once |
| `sync/fixture_tombstone_grace.json` | delete on A, edit on B within grace → resurrect + notice |
| `sync/fixture_import_batch_undo.json` | `UNDO_BATCH` on A removes batch on B |
| `sync/fixture_hydration_30d.json` | fresh device restores newest-first; Today renders after page 1; final state byte-equal to source device export |
| `sync/fixture_selective_sp_gate.json` | symptom ops never appear in `std` bucket; sp consent revoke destroys bucket |
| `sync/fixture_poison_envelope.json` | quarantine, feed continues |
| `sync/fixture_loop_breaker.json` | injected echo bug trips breaker ≤ 12 cycles |
| `sync/fixture_derived_never_synced.json` | oplog contains zero `derived_values` rows after full recompute |

Property test: random interleavings of 200 ops across 3 simulated devices converge to identical DB digests (convergence property, 1,000 seeds in CI nightly).

### 53.13 Phased delivery

P0: oplog + capture interceptor + envelope codec + fixtures (no server). P1: session protocol vs staging `backend/services/sync`, standard-class sync, S-02 status, hydration. P2: sensitive-plus buckets + consent gates, attachments, compaction, circuit breaker, device registry UI. P3: key rotation, quota UX, multi-region residency routing (v1 §31.3).

## 54. Derived-metrics engine implementation plan

Implements v1 §22.1–22.5 (intelligence stack, baseline engine, explainable scores) and v1 §32.3 (compute scheduling) as concrete modules in `core/core-scoring/` and `core/core-baseline/`. Rationale and score semantics live in v1 §10/§22; this section owns the runtime.

### 54.1 Architecture: the computation DAG

Every derived metric is a node in a dependency DAG derived at startup from the metric registry (`core-registry` loading `contracts/metrics/registry/*.yaml`, each derived entry declaring `inputs: [metric ids]` and `calculator: <id>`). Edges are input dependencies; the DAG is validated acyclic at registry-load time (cycle → hard startup failure in debug, registry-entry quarantine in release).

```
samples/sessions/event_records (canonical, post-dedup)
      └─▶ L1 aggregates (daily rollups: sleep.time_asleep, activity.steps_daily…)
            └─▶ L2 baselines (Baseline entities per metric × window × covariate context — core-baseline)
                  └─▶ L3 scores (sleep.score, recovery.score, strain.score…)
                        └─▶ L4 composites (biology.bio_age, energy bank ledgers)
```

Recompute of a node dirties its transitive dependents only for the affected day-range — no whole-DB recompute on a single late sample.

### 54.2 Components and file paths

| Component | Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `MetricDag` | `core/core-scoring/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/scoring/dag/MetricDag.kt` | Build/validate DAG from `MetricRegistry`; topological dirty-set expansion |
| `RecomputeCoordinator` | `core/core-scoring/**/RecomputeCoordinator.kt` | Trigger intake, debounce, chunking, scheduling via platform job APIs (v1 §32.2) |
| `MetricCalculator` (API) | `core/core-scoring/**/calc/MetricCalculator.kt` | Plugin interface (§54.4) |
| `CalculatorRegistry` | `core/core-scoring/**/calc/CalculatorRegistry.kt` | id→calculator binding; version handshake vs registry `algorithm_version` |
| `InputManifestRecorder` | `core/core-scoring/**/InputManifestRecorder.kt` | Snapshot refs for Score Anatomy (v1 §22.5, §30.1) |
| `BaselineEngine` | `core/core-baseline/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/baseline/BaselineEngine.kt` | Robust stats (median/MAD), covariate contexts (v1 §22.2) |
| `DerivedValueRepository` | `core/core-db/**/DerivedValueRepository.kt` | Append-only versioned writes (v1 §30.1: recompute appends, never overwrites) |
| `BackfillRecomputeJob` | `core/core-scoring/**/BackfillRecomputeJob.kt` | Chunked historical recompute on algorithm update |

### 54.3 RecomputeCoordinator triggers

| Trigger | Source event | Debounce / policy |
|---|---|---|
| New data | `IngestBatchCompleted { dayRange, metricFamilies }` | 90 s debounce, coalescing day-ranges; immediate if user is on a screen bound to a dirty metric |
| Day rollover | `DayRolledOver` (tz-aware, from `ClockPort` alarm) | run at rollover + when device wakes past it |
| Settings change | `CalculationSettingsChanged { keys }` (HRV method, zones, units — v1 §6.1 Calculations parity) | immediate, affected subgraph only, UI shows "recomputing…" (v1 §32.3) |
| Algorithm update | `AlgorithmVersionActivated { calculatorId, version }` (registry update via CMS) | staged backfill (§54.6), never blocks foreground |
| Status/covariate edit | `ActivityStatusChanged` (retroactive apply — v1 §6.2 item 5) | recompute affected day-range incl. baseline re-conditioning |
| Sync apply | `SyncCycleCompleted { dirtyDays }` | same as new-data path |

Execution: coordinator resolves dirty nodes via `MetricDag.dependentsOf(dirtySet)`, orders topologically, executes per-day-per-node with results committed per node (crash resumes from last committed node). Heavy runs ride BGProcessingTask / WorkManager per v1 §32.2; thermal/battery yielding per v1 §32.3.

### 54.4 Calculator plugin API

```kotlin
// core/core-scoring/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/scoring/calc/MetricCalculator.kt
interface MetricCalculator {
    val id: String                      // matches registry `calculator:` field, e.g. "sleep_score"
    val version: Int                    // bumped with any math change; stamps DerivedValue.algorithmVersion
    val outputMetric: String            // e.g. "sleep.score"
    val inputSpec: InputSpec            // required/optional metric ids + window lengths
    fun compute(window: DayWindow, inputs: CalcInputs): CalcResult
}

data class CalcInputs(
    val series: Map<String, List<DerivedValue>>,   // resolved upstream nodes
    val raw: RawSlice,                             // scoped repository reads (read-only)
    val baselines: Map<String, Baseline>,          // covariate-matched (cycle phase, status)
    val context: CovariateContext,                 // status intervals, cycle phase, travel/tz
    val settings: CalcSettings                     // user calculation prefs (HRV method…)
)

data class CalcResult(
    val value: DerivedValue?,                      // null = insufficient data (recorded as gap, not zero)
    val confidence: Confidence,                    // provisional/low/normal (v1 §22.2 provisional flag)
    val contributions: List<InputContribution>,    // Score Anatomy feed (v1 §22.5)
    val manifest: InputManifest                    // exact input refs + versions
)
```

Calculators are pure: no repository writes, no wall-clock, no platform APIs. All time comes from `window` and injected `ClockPort` (which they receive only as frozen `now` for "as-of" semantics); all randomness banned (lint rule `NoRandomInCalculators` in `tooling/ci/`). Determinism contract: same fixture DB + same settings + same version ⇒ byte-identical `DerivedValue` set on iOS and Android (v1 §33.4 "divergence forbidden: metric math").

### 54.6 InputManifest, backfill, determinism

**InputManifest** (v1 §30.1): `InputManifestRecorder` persists, per `DerivedValue`, the exact input refs: upstream `derived_value` ids, raw record id-ranges + count + digest, baseline ids, settings hash, calculator id+version. Anatomy sheet (S-level UI) and exports (§56.5) read it verbatim — no recomputation needed to explain a historical score.

**Backfill-recompute chunking:** `BackfillRecomputeJob` walks backward in 30-day chunks (recent-first — user-visible surfaces heal first), each chunk a resumable unit with progress persisted to `recompute_jobs` table; UI shows "re-deriving history: 14 of 36 months" (v1 §32.3). Old `DerivedValue` versions retained (append-only) → "your scores were re-derived" notice with algorithm changelog link (v1 §30.1, §18/§27 algorithm-docs surface).

**Determinism rules:** no wall-clock (`ClockPort` injected, frozen per run); no platform locale in math (formatting is UI-side); floating-point pinned to Double with defined summation order (inputs sorted by ULID before folds); all thresholds from registry YAML, not code constants (server-tunable per v1 §30.6 pattern requires re-versioning: threshold changes bump `version`).

### 54.7 Failure handling

Missing inputs → `value=null` gap + `Confidence.INSUFFICIENT` (never fabricated zeros); calculator exception → node quarantined for that day, `CalculatorFailed` diagnostic event, other nodes proceed (DAG isolation); repeated failure (>3 days same node) → flag to `core-flags` kill-switch check (a remotely disabled calculator renders its surfaces in "temporarily unavailable" state, raw inputs still visible per Law 1); registry/calculator version mismatch → refuse to run, surface in debug diagnostics.

## 55. Insight generation engine implementation plan

Implements v1 §23.7 (insight quality system: template registry, dedup memory, feedback, kill-switch), §23.3 (grounding + verifier pass), and §23.9 (wording guardrails) as runtime in `core/core-insight/` with templates authored in `content/insight-templates/`. The AI/LLM smoothing layer (v1 §23.2 tiers) is downstream and owned by the §55-adjacent phrasing/AI sections; this section owns deterministic candidate generation, verification, and lifecycle.

### 55.1 Architecture

```
domain events (ScoresRecomputed, IngestBatchCompleted, MealLogged, SymptomLogged, DayRolledOver)
   └─▶ TriggerEvaluator (per-template trigger DSL against DerivedValueRepository + baselines)
         └─▶ EvidenceAssembler (resolves evidence requirements → EvidenceRefs)
               └─▶ PhrasingEngine.render (core-phrasing: variant selection, tone, locale)
                     └─▶ InsightVerifier (claim extraction + tolerance check vs engine values)
                           └─▶ DedupMemory (cooldowns, novelty) ─▶ persistence (insights table)
                                 └─▶ SurfacingRouter (Today feed / detail screens / digest fold /
                                      NotificationDecisionEngine candidate — §59)
```

Everything left of `PhrasingEngine` is numeric/deterministic; everything the user reads is verified before persistence — an unverifiable sentence is dropped, never softened (v1 §23.3).

### 55.2 Components and file paths

| Component | Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `InsightEngine` | `core/core-insight/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/insight/InsightEngine.kt` | Event subscription, orchestration |
| `TemplateRegistry` | `core/core-insight/**/registry/TemplateRegistry.kt` | Load/validate `content/insight-templates/*.yaml`; hot-reload via CMS bundle updates (v1 §31.2 Content CMS) |
| `TriggerEvaluator` | `core/core-insight/**/trigger/TriggerEvaluator.kt` | Evaluate trigger DSL (§55.3) |
| `EvidenceAssembler` | `core/core-insight/**/evidence/EvidenceAssembler.kt` | Materialize `EvidenceRef`s; abort candidate if any requirement unmet |
| `InsightVerifier` | `core/core-insight/**/verify/InsightVerifier.kt` | §55.5 |
| `DedupMemory` | `core/core-insight/**/dedup/DedupMemory.kt` | cooldown ledger (`insight_dedup_ledger` table) |
| `FeedbackStore` | `core/core-insight/**/feedback/FeedbackStore.kt` | 👍/👎 + per-user template weights (v1 §23.7) |
| `SurfacingRouter` | `core/core-insight/**/SurfacingRouter.kt` | placement decision; notification candidates handed to §59 pipeline |
| Template schema | `contracts/phrasing/guardrails.yaml` (linter input) + `content/insight-templates/schema.json` | authoring contract |
| Eval harness | `core/core-testing/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/testing/insight/InsightEvalHarness.kt` | §55.9 |

### 55.3 Template format spec

One YAML file per template family in `content/insight-templates/` (e.g., `sleep_debt_rising.yaml`); validated against `schema.json` in CI and at CMS-publish time:

```yaml
id: sleep_debt_rising            # stable, referenced by dedup ledger + kill-switch flag
version: 3
family: sleep
depth_variants: [casual, balanced, power]   # v1 Law 4: same truth, two altitudes
trigger:                          # boolean DSL over metric refs; evaluated by TriggerEvaluator
  all:
    - metric: sleep.bank
      window: latest
      op: lt
      value: { hours: -3 }
    - metric: sleep.bank.delta_7d
      op: lt
      value: { hours: -1 }        # worsening, not just bad
    - not: { status_active: [sick, injured] }   # Karim safeguard (v1 §23.9)
evidence:                         # required refs; candidate dies if any is unresolvable
  - ref: sleep_bank_series_14d    # bound into phrasing + "why am I seeing this"
  - ref: avg_bedtime_7d
cooldown: { days: 5, scope: template }         # scope: template | family | metric
max_per_digest: 1
phrasing:
  en:
    casual:
      - "You're about {debt_hours} short on sleep this week. Tonight's a good night to go early."
    power:
      - "Sleep Bank at {debt_hours} ({delta_7d} vs last week). Average bedtime {avg_bedtime}; a {suggest_shift} earlier start would clear the deficit in ~{recovery_nights} nights."
  ar: { ... }                     # authored, not machine-translated (v1 §23.8)
numeric_slots:                    # every slot maps to an engine value; verifier checks each
  debt_hours: { source: sleep.bank, format: duration_h_m }
  delta_7d: { source: sleep.bank.delta_7d, format: signed_duration }
actions: [view_sleep_bank, adjust_bedtime_target, snooze_topic]
guardrail_class: standard         # standard | reviewed (symptoms/meds/glucose/cycle need human review, v1 §23.9)
kill_switch_flag: ff_insight_sleep_debt_rising
```

Trigger DSL grammar (`trigger/TriggerDsl.kt`): combinators `all/any/not`; leaf predicates `metric` (op ∈ lt/gt/between/crossed_below/crossed_above/streak_ge), `status_active`, `cycle_phase` (sensitive-plus templates only, on-device eval only per v1 §28.7), `data_present`, `days_since_event`. No arbitrary expressions — the DSL is intentionally closed so triggers are statically analyzable (cost bounding + linting).

### 55.4 Candidate generation flow

1. `InsightEngine` subscribes to the domain-event bus; each event maps to the template subset whose triggers reference the touched metrics (index built at registry load — no full scan per event).
2. `TriggerEvaluator` evaluates against `DerivedValueRepository` + `Baseline` lookups; provisional-confidence inputs (v1 §22.2) fail triggers unless template sets `allow_provisional: true` (calibration-honesty templates only).
3. `EvidenceAssembler` resolves each evidence ref into an `EvidenceRef(entityKind, ids, window)` — persisted with the insight so "why am I seeing this" (v1 §23.10) replays exact data.
4. `PhrasingEngine` (core-phrasing) selects variant by user depth setting + tone matrix + locale, fills numeric slots, runs the phrasing linter (banned frames from `contracts/phrasing/guardrails.yaml`).
5. `InsightVerifier` (§55.5) → `DedupMemory` check → persist to `insights` table with `templateId`, `version`, `evidenceRefs[]`, `renderedVariants` (all depths rendered at generation so depth toggles don't re-run the pipeline) → emit `InsightGenerated`.
6. `SurfacingRouter` decides placement: Today feed always; notification only if template declares `notify_eligible: true` AND §59 pipeline admits it; digest fold otherwise.

#### 55.4.1 Insight lifecycle state machine

Persisted `insights.state` column; transitions owned by `InsightEngine` (generation side) and `SurfacingRouter`/UI (consumption side):

```
CANDIDATE ──verifier pass──▶ VERIFIED ──dedup pass──▶ ACTIVE ──surfaced──▶ SEEN
    │ verifier fail                │ cooldown hit          │ user 👍/👎 ──▶ RATED
    ▼                              ▼                        │ evidence window aged out (template ttl_days)
 DROPPED(reason)              SUPPRESSED                    ▼
                                                         EXPIRED (kept for history/eval; excluded from feeds)
ACTIVE ──kill_switch_flag off──▶ WITHHELD (reversible: flag back on → ACTIVE if not expired)
```

`DROPPED`/`SUPPRESSED` candidates persist 30 days in a diagnostics-only table (`insight_rejections`) feeding the §55.9 eval harness and the verifier-rejection dashboard (v1 §36.4) — rejection analysis without user-visible noise.

### 55.5 Verifier implementation

`InsightVerifier` (v1 §23.3 verifier pass, deterministic even in Tier-1 LLM-smoothed mode):

- **Claim extraction:** every `{slot}` occurrence in rendered text is a claim; additionally a regex pass over the rendered string finds bare numerals/durations/percentages NOT originating from a declared slot → automatic rejection (an LLM-smoothed sentence may not introduce numbers).
- **Tolerance rules:** slot value must equal engine value after declared formatting; rounded display values tolerate only the declared rounding (e.g., `duration_h_m` truncates seconds; `percent_0dp` rounds half-up). Comparative words ("above/below/near") map to checkable predicates: "near" requires |z| < 0.5 vs the cited baseline.
- **Guardrail re-check:** linter regexes run on final rendered output (defense-in-depth beyond template-time linting; catches slot-value concatenation accidents).
- Failure → candidate dropped + `InsightVerificationFailed { templateId, reason }` diagnostic event; >N failures/week per template auto-opens an ops alert (v1 §36.4 verifier-rejection dashboard).

### 55.6 Dedup memory and cooldowns

`insight_dedup_ledger` table: `(template_id, scope_key, last_fired_at, fire_count)`. Scope keys per template `cooldown.scope`: template-global, family, or metric-instance. Novelty rule: a candidate whose numeric slots are within tolerance of the previous firing's slots extends cooldown ×2 (no "still short on sleep" drumbeat — v1 §23.7 no-repeats). Ledger syncs (entity kind `insight_feedback` bucket) so two devices don't double-fire.

### 55.7 Feedback loop and kill-switch

- `FeedbackStore`: 👍/👎 per insight → `insight_feedback` rows; per-user template weight = Beta-smoothed helpfulness ratio; weight < 0.25 after ≥4 votes auto-suppresses the template for that user (surfaced in settings as "muted insights", un-mutable). Topic-snooze from notifications (v1 §23.6) writes the same store.
- Kill-switch: each template names a `kill_switch_flag` (`ff_insight_<id>`); `TemplateRegistry` consults `core-flags/FeatureFlagService` at evaluation time — ops can retire a misfiring template in minutes without a release (v1 §23.7). Killing a template also hides its *already-persisted* unread instances (rendering checks the flag).

### 55.8 Failure handling

Registry bundle fails schema validation → previous bundle retained, `ContentBundleRejected` diagnostic (staged rollout per v1 §31.2). Template referencing an unknown metric id → that template quarantined, rest load. Evidence unresolvable → candidate silently dropped (never a half-evidenced insight). Event-bus burst (large import) → `InsightEngine` coalesces to one evaluation pass per template per day-range. Locale variant missing → fall back to EN only if user opted into mixed-language; otherwise template skipped and flagged (no half-localized insight — v1 §3.20 danger).

### 55.9 Test plan and eval harness

| Fixture | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `insight/fixture_sleep_debt_trigger.db` + `expected_candidates.json` | trigger fires exactly on threshold day; cooldown suppresses day+2 |
| `insight/fixture_verifier_reject_cases.yaml` | 20 adversarial rendered strings (hallucinated number, wrong rounding, banned frame) all rejected with reasons |
| `insight/fixture_status_suppression.db` | Sick/Injured suppress performance-critique templates (Karim case) |
| `insight/fixture_provisional_gate.db` | provisional baselines block non-calibration templates |
| `insight/fixture_feedback_suppression.db` | 4×👎 mutes template for user; ledger syncs across TwoDeviceSimulator |
| `insight/fixture_killswitch.db` | flag off → no eval, no render of persisted unread |

**Insight quality regression suite** (`InsightEvalHarness`): a corpus of ~50 scenario DBs × all templates → snapshot of (fired templates, rendered EN/AR casual+power text). Any diff in a PR requires content-owner review (like golden files). Quality metrics tracked per run: firing rate per template, verifier rejection rate, banned-frame hit rate (must be 0), AR/EN slot-format parity.

### 55.10 Phased delivery

P0: registry loader + DSL + verifier + 5 seed templates + harness. P1 (E-07): ~40 launch templates (sleep/recovery/strain/vitals + calibration honesty), feedback store, dedup, kill-switches, AR parity. P2: nutrition/glucose/cycle reviewed-class templates, LLM smoothing integration point (verifier unchanged), proactive check-in templates (v1 §23.6). P3: template weights informing digest ranking; cohort-context templates (v1 §22.6).
