## 56. Export subsystem implementation plan

Implements v1 §20 (formats, scoping, provenance, PDF reports, scheduled exports, deletion interplay) as `core/core-export/` plus `tooling/schema-dictionary-gen/`. Exports always generate locally (v1 §34.5 — cloud never required); the engine therefore must be memory-disciplined on-device.

### 56.1 Pipeline architecture

```
ExportRequest (format × scope, v1 §20.3)
  └─▶ ScopeResolver (metrics/date/source/raw-vs-derived/units/language → concrete query plan)
        └─▶ QueryPlanner (per-table cursors, decimation tier choice, row-count preflight)
              └─▶ StreamingWriter (per-format; §56.3) ─ rows streamed, never materialized
                    └─▶ ManifestBuilder (schema version, row counts, checksums, provenance notes — v1 §20.5)
                          └─▶ Packager (ZIP assembly, optional passphrase encryption via port-crypto)
                                └─▶ Delivery (port-files: share sheet / Files / SAF; scheduled targets §56.6)
```

### 56.2 Components and file paths

| Component | Path |
|---|---|
| `ExportEngine` (facade + job runner) | `core/core-export/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/export/ExportEngine.kt` |
| `ScopeResolver` / `QueryPlanner` | `core/core-export/**/plan/ScopeResolver.kt`, `**/plan/QueryPlanner.kt` |
| `CsvWriter` | `core/core-export/**/writers/CsvWriter.kt` — tidy long format per v1 §20.2 (one file per metric; columns exactly: `timestamp_start, timestamp_end, metric_id, value, unit, source_app, source_device, quality_flags, algorithm_version, suppressed_by`) |
| `JsonBundleWriter` | `core/core-export/**/writers/JsonBundleWriter.kt` — schema-versioned, nested by domain + dictionaries slice |
| `SqliteBundleWriter` | `core/core-export/**/writers/SqliteBundleWriter.kt` — builds a fresh SQLite file with app-mirroring views per `contracts/export/schema/v1/sqlite-views.schema.json` |
| `PdfReportComposer` (data side) | `core/core-export/**/writers/PdfReportComposer.kt` — assembles `ReportModel` (sections, charts-as-data, narrative slots); native renderers in `ios/BadanApp/Platform/` and `android/app/**/platform/` turn it into PDF (print-safe rules v1 §20.6) |
| `ParquetWriter` (P3) | `core/core-export/**/writers/ParquetWriter.kt` |
| `ExportMappingLayer` | `core/core-export/**/mapping/ExportMappingLayer.kt` (§56.4) |
| `ManifestBuilder` / `Packager` | `core/core-export/**/manifest/`, `**/package/` |
| `ExportScheduler` | `core/core-export/**/ExportScheduler.kt` (§56.6) |
| Dictionary generator | `tooling/schema-dictionary-gen/` (§56.7) |
| Job persistence | `export_jobs` table (v1 §30.1 entity) — status, scope hash, artifact path, checksum |

### 56.3 Interfaces

```kotlin
// core/core-export/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/export/writers/StreamingWriter.kt
interface StreamingWriter {
    val format: ExportFormat
    suspend fun open(target: FileHandle, plan: QueryPlan, mapping: ExportMapping)
    suspend fun writeChunk(rows: List<ExportRow>)        // ≤2,000 rows per chunk
    suspend fun finish(): WriterResult                   // per-file row counts + sha256
}

data class ExportRequest(
    val format: ExportFormat,                            // CSV, JSON_BUNDLE, SQLITE, PDF_REPORT, ARCHIVE_ZIP
    val scope: ExportScope,                              // metricSelector, dateRange, sources,
                                                         // includeSuppressed, rawDerivedMode, unitProfile, language
    val sensitiveInclusion: SensitiveInclusion,          // per-class explicit toggles (v1 §20.9, §28.7)
    val encryptPassphrase: CharArray?
)
```

#### 56.3.1 Export job state machine

`export_jobs.status` transitions (driven by `ExportEngine`; every transition timestamped for the export-history UI):

```
QUEUED ─▶ PLANNING (scope resolution + preflight estimate)
       ─▶ WRITING (per-file progress: files_done/files_total, resumable checkpoint per file)
       ─▶ PACKAGING (manifest + checksums + ZIP + optional encryption)
       ─▶ READY (artifact in export-tmp, awaiting delivery)
       ─▶ DELIVERED (share-sheet completion / scheduled target confirm) ─▶ PURGED (artifact deleted, +24 h)
any ─▶ FAILED(reason: DISK_SPACE | QUERY_ERROR | CANCELLED | DELIVERY_REJECTED) — FAILED jobs keep
      their scope hash so "retry" re-enqueues identically; CANCELLED purges temp files atomically (§56.7)
```

### 56.4 Schema-versioned mapping layer

`ExportMappingLayer` is the decoupling required by v1 §30.4: internal tables never serialize directly. `contracts/export/schema/v1/` holds JSON Schemas (`csv-manifest`, `json-bundle`, `sqlite-views`); `ExportMapping` tables (code-generated from those schemas by `tooling/schema-dictionary-gen`) map internal column → export column + unit conversion + enum rendering. Internal refactors change only the mapping; published majors stay readable (semver + changelog per v1 §20.5). A CI snapshot test (`export/schema_snapshot_test`) fails any PR that alters export output bytes for the frozen fixture without a schema-version bump.

### 56.5 Manifest, checksums, provenance

`manifest.json` in every archive: app version, export schema version, generation timestamp + tz notes, scope echo, dedup-policy description string, per-file row counts + sha256, algorithm registry slice (id, version, methodology URL) for every derived metric present, and per-metric source chains (v1 §20.5 — truncation detectable, derived vs raw separated). `DataDictionary.md` (generated, §56.7) ships inside every archive.

### 56.6 Scheduled and automated exports (Pro, v1 §20.7)

`ExportScheduler` persists recurrence rules (`weekly`/`monthly` × format × scope) in `export_jobs`; execution rides the same background lanes as recompute (BGProcessingTask / WorkManager). Delivery targets via `port-files`: local Files/Drive/iCloud document providers; webhook target P3 (personal API adjacency, v1 §20.8). Shortcuts/App Actions ("export last month as CSV") call `ExportEngine.enqueue()` with a preset scope. Flag: `ff_export_scheduled`.

### 56.7 Large-export memory strategy

Rules (v1 §32.6 memory ceilings): all reads are keyset-paginated cursors (`(metric_id, start_ts, id)`), never `SELECT *` materialization; writers stream to temp files in the app cache dir (`export-tmp/<job_id>/`), fsynced per chunk; ZIP assembled by streaming-append (no in-memory archive); `SqliteBundleWriter` writes via a second SQLDelight connection with `PRAGMA journal_mode=OFF` on the artifact; peak RSS budget for a 5-year heavy-user full export: <120 MB, CI-measured on the perf fixture. Jobs are resumable per completed file; cancellation deletes `export-tmp/<job_id>/` atomically.

### 56.8 Deletion-flow integration

Account/data deletion (v1 §20.9, §28.4) calls `ExportEngine` first: the deletion wizard's "take your data" step enqueues a full ARCHIVE_ZIP with `sensitiveInclusion=ALL_PROMPTED`; deletion proceeds only after artifact delivery confirmation or explicit skip. BADAN retains no copy post-delivery (generation artifacts purged on job completion + 24 h). Sensitive-class inclusion requires the extra per-export toggle even in the deletion flow.

### 56.9 Dictionary generator tool

`tooling/schema-dictionary-gen/` (Kotlin CLI, run in CI): inputs `contracts/export/schema/v1/*.schema.json` + `contracts/metrics/registry/*.yaml` → outputs (1) `docs/data-dictionary/` (published site source), (2) `DataDictionary.md` archive template, (3) generated `ExportMapping` Kotlin tables. Guarantees the published dictionary can never drift from what the writers emit — same source of truth (v1 §20.5, Priya archetype requirement).

### 56.10 Failure handling

Disk full → preflight estimate from `QueryPlanner` row counts; job refuses to start under 2× estimated headroom. Crash mid-job → resume from last completed file. Share-sheet cancel → artifact retained 24 h in export history for retry. Unit-profile mismatch (mmol/L vs mg/dL) is impossible-by-construction: conversion lives in `ExportMapping`, tested per locale fixture (v1 §3.16 danger). Scheduled-export failures notify via the System notification class (v1 §24.6) once, then fold to in-app status.

## 57. Logging subsystem implementation plan

"Logging" means two unrelated systems; this section implements both and keeps them strictly apart: **(A) the user-logging flows engine** — the command layer behind v1 §21 (food, exercise, symptoms, meds, journal); **(B) diagnostic logging** — structured app logs for debugging and support, governed by the never-log-health-values policy (v1 §36.2 spirit applied to logs).

### 57.A User-logging flows engine (command layer)

#### 57.A.1 Architecture

All log mutations flow through `XxxCommand` use cases (naming per conventions §3) in `core/core-model`-adjacent use-case packages, backed by repositories in `core-db`. Commands are the single write path for user-authored data — UI never touches repositories directly (v1 §26.6 policy layering). Each command implements one contract:

```kotlin
// core/core-ingest/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/logging/LogCommand.kt
interface LogCommand<I : LogInput, R : LogReceipt> {
    fun validate(input: I): ValidationResult            // pure; drives inline field errors
    suspend fun execute(input: I): R                    // transactional write + fan-out
    suspend fun undo(receipt: R)                        // time-boxed undo (default 30 s snackbar; edits forever via audit)
}
```

`execute` performs, in one DB transaction: entity write (with `Provenance(path=MANUAL, recordedAt, measuredAt, tz)`), audit-trail entry (v1 §21.1 every log editable/deletable with audit), oplog capture (`WriteOrigin.USER` → §53.3). Post-commit fan-out (outbox pattern, `pending_fanout` table so a crash never loses a side effect): domain event emit → write-back queue → recompute trigger → search-index update (§58.3).

#### 57.A.2 Command inventory

| Command | Path (`core/core-ingest/**/logging/commands/`) | Validation rules | Write path | Fan-out | Undo model |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LogMealCommand` | `LogMealCommand.kt` | ≥1 item; portion > 0; time not >7d future; kcal sanity bound (0–8,000/entry, soft-warn) | `MealEntry` + items → `event_records` | `MealLogged` → nutrition recompute → HK/HC write-back (macros/micros/water/caffeine/alcohol toggles, v1 §11.5) → alias learning (§57.A.4) | delete entry + reverse write-back |
| `LogSymptomCommand` | `LogSymptomCommand.kt` | canonical-or-custom symptom id; severity in scale (3-level casual / 0–10 power); duration ≥0 | `SymptomEvent` → `event_records` (sensitive-plus store) | `SymptomLogged` → recurrence engine → correlation candidates | delete event |
| `LogAdherenceCommand` | `LogAdherenceCommand.kt` | regimen exists + active at time; state ∈ taken/late/skipped(+reason) | `AdherenceEvent` (sensitive-plus) | `AdherenceLogged` → adherence recompute → reminder-cancellation | flip/delete event |
| `LogWorkoutCommand` | `LogWorkoutCommand.kt` | type known/custom; duration 1 min–24 h; RPE 1–10 | `WorkoutSession` → `sessions` | `WorkoutLogged` → strain/load recompute → HC/HK write-back → dedup guard vs auto-import (v1 §21.3) | delete session + reverse write-back |
| `LogStrengthSetCommand` | `LogStrengthSetCommand.kt` | weight ≥0, reps 1–100; ≤3 taps repeat path (v1 §3.7) | set row within active session runner | live session totals; on session end → `WorkoutLogged` | remove set |
| `LogMeasurementCommand` | `LogMeasurementCommand.kt` | metric-specific physiologic bounds from registry (`validation:` block); unit-guarded input (v1 §11.2 manual risks) | `Sample(manual)` | `MeasurementLogged` → manual-wins dedup rule (v1 §11.4) → recompute | delete sample |
| `LogMoodCommand` / `LogWaterCommand` / `LogCaffeineCommand` / `LogAlcoholCommand` | one file each | slider/preset ranges | `event_records` / `samples` | subjective series wiring (v1 §21.8); water/caffeine write-back | delete |
| `LogLabResultCommand` | `LogLabResultCommand.kt` | biomarker id from registry; unit ∈ allowed set; ref-range optional | `LabResult` → `event_records` | `LabResultLogged` → biology recompute → BioAge input refresh | delete |
| `LogCycleEventCommand` | `LogCycleEventCommand.kt` | sensitive-plus consent surface; phase-model inputs | `event_records` (sensitive store) | `CycleEventLogged` → phase recompute (on-device only) | delete |
| `LogNoteCommand` | `LogNoteCommand.kt` | length ≤ 10k; attachments via content-addressed blobs | `event_records` | search-index only | delete |

All commands: retro-logging first-class (backdate picker feeds `measuredAt`; `recordedAt` always now — v1 §21.1); fully offline (writes are local; write-back and sync queue). **Offline queue:** write-back fan-out entries persist in `pending_fanout` with per-target retry (same backoff table as §53.10); platform-store write failures never fail the command — the local entity is truth (Law 1 ordering).

#### 57.A.3 Recents, favorites, and speed providers

- `RecentsProvider` (`core/core-ingest/**/logging/recents/RecentsProvider.kt`): per-command MRU with frequency-decay score (`score = Σ 0.9^days_since_use`), backing the 2-tap re-log requirement (v1 §21.1 ≤3 interactions; J8).
- `FavoritesStore`: explicit pins (foods, meals, workouts, symptom sets) — `customization_profiles` payload, synced.
- `MealTemplateProvider`: "my usual breakfast" one-tap (v1 §21.2 favorites/recents/meals).

#### 57.A.4 Personal-alias store

`AliasStore` (`core/core-ingest/**/logging/alias/AliasStore.kt`): every accepted AI-parse correction persists `(userPhrase, resolvedItems[], locale)` (v1 §21.2 corrections loop — "my 'toast' = 2 slices whole wheat + butter"). Lookup runs *before* remote parse: exact + fuzzy (trigram) match on-device; hits short-circuit the cloud call (cost + privacy win). Symptom synonyms (v1 §21.4 "did you mean 'light-headed' (used 4×)?") share the same store with `kind=symptom`. Sensitive-plus storage class; syncs under sp bucket.

### 57.B Diagnostic logging

#### 57.B.1 Structured logger

`DiagLog` (`core/core-model/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/diag/DiagLog.kt`): `DiagLog.event(category, level, message, fields: Map<String, DiagValue>)`. Categories (closed enum): `INGEST`, `DEDUP`, `SCORING`, `SYNC`, `EXPORT`, `INSIGHT`, `NOTIFY`, `SEARCH`, `UI_NAV`, `PERMISSION`, `BILLING`. Levels: `DEBUG` (dev builds only), `INFO`, `WARN`, `ERROR`. Sink: in-memory ring buffer → encrypted rolling files (`diag/`, 5 × 2 MB, FIFO), local only; crash reporter (Sentry-class, v1 §36.4) receives only `WARN+` breadcrumbs post-scrub.

#### 57.B.2 What is NEVER logged (policy + lint)

Policy (extends v1 §36.1 "no health values in analytics" to diagnostics): no metric values, no food/symptom/med names, no note text, no lab values, no coordinates, no user identifiers beyond install pseudo-id. Allowed: metric *ids/families*, counts, durations of operations, error codes, record *counts* per batch, entity kinds. Enforcement is typed, not disciplinary: `DiagValue` admits only `CountV`, `DurationV`, `EnumV(registryEnum)`, `ErrorCodeV`, `MetricIdV` — there is no string-payload constructor. Lint `NoRawStringInDiagFields` (in `tooling/ci/lints/`) blocks any interpolated string reaching `fields`; `message` must be a compile-time constant (lint-checked). PII-scrubbing second line: the bundle exporter (§57.B.3) runs regex scrub (emails, numbers-with-units patterns) and refuses to package on hits, failing loudly in CI's scrub-test.

#### 57.B.3 Diagnostic bundle export

User-triggered from Settings → Help ("share diagnostics with support"): `DiagBundleBuilder` packages ring buffer + device/app metadata + feature-flag state + last 50 `SyncConflictDetected`/`CalculatorFailed`-class events (ids only) into an encrypted ZIP the *user* attaches to a support email — BADAN never auto-uploads logs (v1 §28 posture). Preview screen shows the exact contents before share (payload-visibility pattern, v1 §23.5).

### 57.4 Failure handling

Command transaction failure → typed `AppError` → UI error state, input preserved (never lose a typed meal); fan-out failures retry from `pending_fanout` independently; alias-store corruption → rebuild from audit trail; ring-buffer write failure → silent drop (diagnostics must never crash the app).

## 58. Search and filtering implementation plan

Implements v1 §35 (global search, structured filtering grammar, NL bridge, performance targets) as `core/core-search/`. The NL query path (v1 §35.3) belongs to the AI sections; §58 owns the index, the grammar, and the `FilterSpec` handoff target that NL queries compile into.

### 58.1 Architecture and FTS5 index tables

SQLite FTS5 virtual tables in `core/core-db/src/commonMain/sqldelight/net/badan/db/search.sq`, contentless-delete mode (`content=''`) with explicit docid management so index rows never duplicate source-of-truth data:

| Index table | Sources | Indexed columns |
|---|---|---|
| `fts_metrics` | registry (names, synonyms, casual+precise labels, EN+AR localized — v1 §35.1) | `label, synonyms, family, metric_id(unindexed)` |
| `fts_entries` | `event_records` (notes, meal item names, symptom labels incl. customs, med names, condition labels) | `text, kind(unindexed), entity_id(unindexed), day(unindexed)` |
| `fts_foods_personal` | favorites, recipes, aliases | `name, brand` |
| `fts_content` | education articles, glossary, settings screens (static, shipped pre-built in the content bundle) | `title, body, route(unindexed)` |
| `fts_insights` | insight history rendered text | `text, template_id(unindexed)` |

Tokenizer: `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2` everywhere, plus a custom normalization pass **before** insertion and before query (`ArabicNormalizer` in `core/core-search/**/normalize/ArabicNormalizer.kt`): alef variants (أ إ آ ا → ا), teh marbuta → heh, alef maqsura → yeh, tatweel stripped, Arabic-Indic digits → ASCII. FTS5's unicode61 handles case/diacritics for Latin; the normalizer makes Arabic matching behave equivalently. Prefix indexes `prefix='2 3'` for search-as-you-type.

### 58.2 Components

| Component | Path |
|---|---|
| `SearchIndexer` | `core/core-search/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/search/SearchIndexer.kt` |
| `QueryParser` | `core/core-search/**/query/QueryParser.kt` |
| `FilterSpec` + compiler | `core/core-search/**/filter/FilterSpec.kt`, `FilterCompiler.kt` (→ SQL) |
| `Ranker` | `core/core-search/**/rank/Ranker.kt` |
| `FoodSearchMerger` | `core/core-search/**/food/FoodSearchMerger.kt` |
| `SavedViewStore` | `core/core-search/**/views/SavedViewStore.kt` |

### 58.3 Incremental indexing flow

Event-driven, no periodic rebuild: `SearchIndexer` subscribes to domain events (`MealLogged`, `SymptomLogged`, `InsightGenerated`, `NoteLogged`, `EntryEdited`, `EntryDeleted`, registry/content bundle updates) and applies per-row upsert/delete to the FTS tables inside a low-priority queue (batched, 250 ms debounce). Sync-applied inbound ops (§53) route through the same events, so a hydrated device indexes as it restores. Full rebuild exists only as a recovery action (`SearchIndexer.rebuild()`, chunked, resumable) triggered by index-corruption detection (FTS integrity check on schema migration).

Query data flow: keystroke → `ArabicNormalizer` → `QueryParser` (operator extraction) → `FilterCompiler` SQL against FTS tables (local, synchronous budget 50 ms) → `Ranker` → grouped `SearchResults` flow to UI; food surfaces additionally fan out to `FoodSearchMerger` (§58.7). Interfaces:

```kotlin
// core/core-search/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/search/SearchApi.kt
interface SearchIndexer {
    suspend fun apply(change: IndexChange)              // event-driven upsert/delete (§58.3)
    suspend fun rebuild(progress: FlowCollector<RebuildProgress>)
    suspend fun integrityCheck(): IndexHealth
}
interface Ranker { fun rank(hits: List<FtsHit>, query: ParsedQuery, usage: UsageSignals): List<RankedResult> }
```

### 58.4 Query grammar and FilterSpec

```kotlin
// core/core-search/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/search/filter/FilterSpec.kt
data class FilterSpec(
    val text: String?,                       // FTS clause (normalized)
    val dateRange: DateRangeSel?,            // preset (TODAY, D7, D30, M3, Y1) or custom
    val pillars: Set<Pillar> = emptySet(),   // sleep, fitness, nutrition, vitals, biology, cycle, meds, symptoms
    val kinds: Set<EntryKind> = emptySet(),  // meal, workout, symptom, adherence, note, lab, insight
    val sources: SourceSel? = null,          // include/exclude source_connection ids
    val tags: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    val statusOverlap: Set<ActivityStatus> = emptySet(),   // days overlapping Sick/Travel… (v1 §35.2)
    val hasData: Boolean? = null,            // registry browser: only metrics with data
    val outOfBand: Boolean? = null,          // registry browser: outside personal band
    val severity: IntRange? = null,          // symptoms
    val mealType: Set<MealType> = emptySet(),
    val sort: SortSpec = SortSpec.RELEVANCE_THEN_RECENCY,
    val limit: Int = 50
)
```

`QueryParser` accepts free text plus inline operators (power affordance, casual users never need them): `tag:late-meal`, `source:garmin`, `severity:>5`, `during:sick`, `before:2026-03`, quoted phrases. Output is always a `FilterSpec` — the same DTO the filter-chip UI builds, saved views persist, NL queries compile into ("open as filter" handoff, v1 §35.3), and export scopes accept (one grammar, three payoffs — v1 §35.2). `FilterCompiler` renders it to indexed SQL (FTS join + covering-index predicates), never string-concatenated user input.

### 58.5 Ranking rules

Score = FTS5 `bm25()` weighted per column (label 4×, synonyms 2×, body 1×) + type prior (metrics > personal foods > entries > content > insights for short queries; recency-boosted entries for date-shaped queries) + personal-usage boost (`RecentsProvider` frequency-decay score, §57.A.3) + exact-prefix bonus. Grouped presentation by type with per-group caps (v1 §35.1); typo tolerance via FTS prefix + trigram fallback table for zero-hit queries (edit-distance ≤1 suggestions: "did you mean").

### 58.6 Cross-script matching

Requirement (v1 §35.1): "searching 'hrv' in Arabic UI still hits." Implementation: `fts_metrics` indexes EN and AR labels + a curated translit-synonym column from the registry (each metric entry carries `search_synonyms: {en: [...], ar: [...]}` including Latin abbreviations in the AR list — HRV, VO2, BMI are used verbatim by Arabic speakers). Query pass runs the input against the index twice when the input script differs from UI locale (raw + normalized-translit); union of hits, dedup by metric_id. No runtime transliteration engine — curation in the registry is cheaper and testable (`search/fixture_cross_script.yaml`: 40 query→expected-hit pairs EN↔AR).

### 58.7 Remote food-search merge

`FoodSearchMerger` (local-first display, v1 §35.4): personal items (`fts_foods_personal` + aliases) render instantly (<50 ms); remote query to `backend/services/fooddata` proxy fires debounced 300 ms; remote results stream in *below* the pinned local section, deduped against local by provider-id; verified-first ranking within the remote section (v1 §21.2). Offline: local section only + quiet "search more foods when online" row. Remote calls pseudonymized per v1 §31.2.

### 58.8 Saved views

`SavedViewStore` persists named `FilterSpec`s (`saved_view` payload in `customization_profiles`, synced — usable in Timeline, registry browser, and export scopes per v1 §35.2). Views carry `pinned` flag (appear as chips on their host surfaces). Deleting a referenced source degrades the view gracefully (dangling source id ignored + badge).

### 58.9 Performance targets and test plan

Targets (v1 §35.4 + §32.6): search-as-you-type p95 < 50 ms on-device against a 5-year fixture (250k entries); index write amplification < 5 ms per logged entry; index size < 8% of DB size; rebuild of 5-year fixture < 60 s background.

| Fixture | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `search/fixture_5yr_index.db` | latency + size targets (CI perf lane, device-class matrix) |
| `search/fixture_arabic_normalization.yaml` | alef/teh-marbuta/diacritic/digit variants all match |
| `search/fixture_cross_script.yaml` | 40 EN↔AR pairs hit |
| `search/fixture_incremental_consistency.db` | 1k random log/edit/delete ops → index equals from-scratch rebuild |
| `search/fixture_filterspec_compile.yaml` | 25 FilterSpecs → SQL uses indexes (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN assertions, no table scans) |
| `search/fixture_food_merge.json` | local pinned first; remote dedup; offline degradation |
| `search/fixture_operator_grammar.txt` | parser round-trips operators; malformed input degrades to plain text, never errors |

### 58.10 Phased delivery

P1 (within E-05 shell scope): metrics + entries + content indexes, QueryParser, FilterSpec + chips, ranking v1, Arabic normalizer. P2: personal-food merge (with E-12), insights index, saved views, typo suggestions. P3: NL "open as filter" handoff (E-17/E-19 adjacency), export-scope reuse.

## 59. Notifications and digest engine implementation plan

Implements v1 §24.6–24.8 (taxonomy, smart timing, anti-annoyance decision engine) and v1 §22.9 (digest cadence) as `core/core-notify/` with platform schedulers in `adapters/` and `ios|android/Platform`. Push payloads are references, never health values (v1 §31.2 Push service).

### 59.1 Architecture

```
Candidate producers: SurfacingRouter (§55), med reminder scheduler, anchor scheduler,
                     system events (export ready, sync broken, permission expiring)
   └─▶ NotificationDecisionEngine.decide(candidate): Decision
         pipeline (ordered stage functions):
         valueTest → dedup → budgetCheck → quietHours → channelRoute
   └─▶ Decision ∈ { Deliver(channel, time), Digest(fold), InAppOnly, Drop(reason) }
         └─▶ LocalNotificationPort (platform scheduling) / in-app inbox / digest queue
               └─▶ NotificationAuditStore (every decision recorded — self-audit + telemetry)
```

All decisions run on-device (anchors fire offline — v1 §34.5). Remote pushes (vendor webhook data arrived, content updates) carry only a `ref` payload; the device fetches/decrypts, renders locally, and the rendered candidate *still passes the decision pipeline* — a push is a hint, never a bypass.

### 59.2 Components

| Component | Path |
|---|---|
| `NotificationDecisionEngine` | `core/core-notify/src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/notify/NotificationDecisionEngine.kt` |
| Stage functions | `core/core-notify/**/stages/ValueTest.kt`, `Dedup.kt`, `BudgetCheck.kt`, `QuietHours.kt`, `ChannelRoute.kt` |
| `NotificationConfig` | `core/core-notify/**/config/NotificationConfig.kt` (schema §59.3; defaults shipped in `content/`, user overrides in `customization_profiles`) |
| `AnchorScheduler` | `core/core-notify/**/AnchorScheduler.kt` (wake-relative computation §59.5) |
| `DigestComposer` | `core/core-notify/**/digest/DigestComposer.kt` |
| `NotificationAuditStore` | `core/core-notify/**/audit/NotificationAuditStore.kt` (`notification_audit` table) |
| `LocalNotificationPort` | `adapters/port-push/**/LocalNotificationPort.kt`; actuals: UNUserNotificationCenter (iOS), AlarmManager+NotificationManager channels (Android) |
| Renderers | `ios/BadanApp/Platform/NotificationRenderer.swift` (Notification Service Extension), `android/app/**/platform/NotificationRenderer.kt` |

### 59.3 Decision pipeline and config schema

```kotlin
fun interface NotifyStage { fun apply(c: Candidate, ctx: DecisionContext): StageResult }
// StageResult = Continue(c') | Reroute(channel) | Drop(reason)  — stages are pure; ctx carries
// clock (ClockPort), audit history, budgets state, user config; order fixed:
val pipeline = listOf(valueTest, dedup, budgetCheck, quietHours, channelRoute)
```

- **valueTest** — candidate must carry `noveltyToken` (new information) + `actionRef` (deep link) or it drops (v1 §24.8 "new information? actionable?"); suppress if user viewed the same surface within `recentlySeenWindow` (default 45 min — v1 §24.7 last rule).
- **dedup** — same `topicKey` delivered within topic cooldown → Drop; insight candidates already carry §55.6 dedup, this catches cross-producer repeats (insight + digest tease).
- **budgetCheck** — per-class daily budgets + global cap (§59.4); over-budget candidates re-route to digest-fold rather than drop (information preserved, interruption avoided).
- **quietHours** — user windows incl. prayer-time-configurable presets (v1 §2.1 Law 7, §24.8); care-task escalations may deliver at window edge, never inside; digest folds ignore quiet hours (they're pull surfaces).
- **channelRoute** — maps class → push / in-app inbox / digest per config + entitlement + platform channel (Android channels registered per class so OS-level per-class opt-out mirrors in-app config).

Config schema (`NotificationConfig`, JSON in customization profile): per-class `{enabled, budgetPerDay, channel, escalation}`, global `{dailyCap, quietWindows[], recentlySeenWindowMin, digestDay, digestHour}`.

### 59.4 Per-class budget defaults

| Class (v1 §24.6) | Default state | Budget/day | Over-budget behavior | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Daily anchors | ON | 1 | never exceeds (hard) | morning narrative; weekly digest counts as anchor on its day |
| Care tasks (meds, refill) | ON when meds exist | per-regimen, escalate once max | deliver (care exempt from global cap) | quiet-hours aware edge delivery |
| State changes | selective ON | 1 | digest-fold | composite-severity gated upstream (v1 §22.3) |
| Encouragement | OFF | 1 | drop | opt-in only (v1 §24.6) |
| Coach / check-ins | configured cadence | 1 | digest-fold | topic-snooze honored forever (v1 §23.6) |
| System (export ready, sync broken, permission expiring) | ON | 2 | in-app only | transactional |
| **Global cap** | — | 3 (default) | digest-fold | user-tunable 1–6 |

### 59.5 Scheduling and wake-relative anchors

Platform scheduling via `LocalNotificationPort`: iOS `UNCalendarNotificationTrigger`/`UNTimeIntervalNotificationTrigger` (64-pending-limit managed by a rolling 7-day scheduling horizon); Android exact alarms only for care tasks (`SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` rationale UX), inexact windows otherwise + WorkManager fallback for OEM-throttled devices (v1 §37.6 playbook).

**Wake-relative anchor computation** (v1 §24.7 "post-wake narrative beats fixed 7:00"): `AnchorScheduler` schedules a provisional anchor at `personalWakeP80 + 20 min` (80th percentile wake time from the last 14 `SleepSession` ends, tz-aware). When the sleep-session-end event actually arrives (`SessionAssembled{kind=sleep}`), the provisional is cancelled and the anchor fires at `wake + 20 min` if the narrative is ready (recompute completed), else as soon as `ScoresRecomputed` lands, capped at provisional time + 2 h. No sleep data → fixed-time fallback (user-set, default 07:30 local). Bedtime nudges compute relative to target bedtime; workout summaries fire on `WorkoutLogged` within minutes (v1 §24.7).

### 59.6 Digest generation jobs

`DigestComposer` runs as a background job (weekly: user-set day/hour, default Sun 18:00; monthly: 1st): assembles content from insight history (`insights` where `surfaced=digest_fold` + top-weighted per §55.7 feedback), trend queries (`TrendDeltaCalculator` outputs, "what changed" per v1 §22.9), adherence recap, experiment results (P3), and the notification self-audit line (§59.7). Output = a `DigestDocument` persisted locally (readable offline, listed in a digests archive), plus one anchor-class notification referencing it. Rendering depth follows user altitude (casual: one focus theme; power: full change table) — same Law-4 dual rendering.

### 59.7 On-device content rendering and self-audit

**Payload = reference:** every delivered notification carries `{candidateId, deepLink, class}`; visible title/body are rendered on-device at display time — iOS via Notification Service Extension pulling from the shared app-group store, Android at post time (app process). Lock-screen privacy: sensitive-plus-related notifications use redacted public versions ("You have a reminder") per platform visibility settings.

**Self-audit surface** (v1 §24.8): `NotificationAuditStore` records every candidate with its decision + stage that decided it. Settings → Notifications shows "BADAN sent you N this week" + per-class counts + top drop reasons + one-tap tuning; every delivered notification supports long-press → "fewer like this" → topic-snooze write (same store §55.7 reads).

### 59.8 Deep-link integrity and telemetry

- **Deep-link integrity test plan:** every template/producer declares its `actionRef` route; CI test enumerates all producible refs and asserts each resolves in both apps' route tables (`AppRouter.swift`, `navigation/` graph) — no dead notification taps (E-10 acceptance, v1 §42). Fixture `notify/fixture_deeplink_matrix.yaml` lists ref → expected screen id; UI smoke test taps 10 sampled refs per release.
- **Disable-rate telemetry hooks:** analytics events (values-free per conventions §3): `notification_delivered {class}`, `notification_opened {class}`, `notification_disabled {class, scope}` (scope: topic/class/os-level detected via permission recheck), `digest_opened {period}`. KPI wiring: notification-driven disable rate < 2%/month (v1 §24.8) monitored on the §36.1 notification-health funnel; a class breaching 2× baseline auto-opens review and can be remotely budget-tightened via `core-flags` config (`ff_notify_budget_override`).

### 59.9 Failure handling

Permission denied → all candidates route in-app inbox; status shown in self-audit surface. OS purge of pending schedules (iOS 64-limit, OEM kill) → reconciliation on every app foreground (compare intended vs pending, reschedule diff). Recompute not ready at anchor time → §59.5 grace logic, never a stale narrative (candidate carries `dataAsOf`; delivery re-validates freshness). Clock/tz change → `AnchorScheduler` full reschedule on `TimeZoneChanged`. Digest job miss (device off) → next foreground catch-up, badge instead of late-night push.

### 59.11 Phased delivery

P1 (E-10): pipeline + budgets + anchors (fixed-time) + care tasks + audit store + deep-link CI. P2: wake-relative anchors, digest composer (E-18 adjacency), self-audit surface, Android channel mirroring, quiet-hours presets. P3: check-in cadence integration (E-17), digest ranking by feedback weights, remote budget override flag.

## 60. Feature flag and remote config architecture

Rationale lives in v1 §36.3 (experimentation limits) and §9.8 (flag/kill-switch as hidden enabling feature). This section implements the system: module `core/core-flags/`, service `FeatureFlagService`, remote delivery via the Content CMS service (`backend/services/contentcms/`).

### 60.1 `core-flags` design

```
core/core-flags/
├── flags.yaml                          # single source of truth: every flag, typed, with defaults per build channel
├── src/commonMain/kotlin/net/badan/flags/
│   ├── FlagRegistry.kt                 # GENERATED from flags.yaml at build time (tooling/scripts/flaggen)
│   ├── FeatureFlagService.kt           # evaluation API (below)
│   ├── FlagOverrideStore.kt            # persisted remote overrides (customization_profiles-adjacent table flag_overrides)
│   ├── RemoteConfigClient.kt           # pulls signed flag-config document from contentcms; ETag-cached
│   ├── ExperimentAssigner.kt           # deterministic bucketing (pseudonymous id hash % 1000)
│   └── KillSwitchGuard.kt              # hard-off wrapper for integration/insight-template classes
└── src/commonTest/kotlin/…             # FlagEvaluationTest, SkewFallbackTest, BucketingStabilityTest
```

Evaluation API (frozen before Wave 1 fan-out — see §66.2):

```kotlin
interface FeatureFlagService {
    fun isEnabled(flag: Flag.Bool): Boolean                    // Flag.* constants generated into FlagRegistry
    fun <T : Enum<T>> variant(flag: Flag.Variant<T>): T        // experiment arms
    fun killSwitchActive(scope: KillScope): Boolean            // KillScope.Integration(vendor) | KillScope.InsightTemplate(family)
    val changes: Flow<FlagChange>                              // UI reacts without restart only for flags marked hot=true
}
```

Evaluation order: **kill-switch → remote override (if fresh + signature valid) → experiment assignment → compiled local default.** Every flag in `flags.yaml` declares: `key`, `type` (bool|variant), `default` per channel (debug/beta/prod), `hot` (evaluable mid-session vs next-launch), `owner` (track id), `state` (lifecycle), `delete_by` (date), `analytics_exposure` (whether an exposure event fires — see §61 event `flag_exposed`).

### 60.2 Flag lifecycle and deletion-deadline policy

| State | Meaning | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `draft` | In development; default OFF in prod, ON in debug | May not gate release-blocking tests |
| `rollout` | Staged % rollout via remote config | Must have guardrail metrics named in flags.yaml (`guardrails: [crash_free, notif_disable_rate]`) |
| `ga` | 100% on; remote override retained as kill capability only | `delete_by` set to ≤ 2 release trains out |
| `cleanup` | Code paths being removed | CI check `flaggen --report-overdue` fails the PR pipeline (§63.1) if `delete_by` passed |
| `permanent` | Explicitly exempt (kill-switches, entitlement gates, local-only exclusions) | Requires `owner` + ADR reference |

Deletion deadline policy: a flag reaching `ga` gets a `delete_by` date stamped at promotion; `tooling/scripts/flaggen/` emits a weekly overdue report and the PR pipeline fails when any non-`permanent` flag is >1 train past `delete_by`. Dead flags are a merge-conflict and test-matrix tax; the deadline is CI-enforced, not aspirational.

### 60.4 Kill-switch class

Kill-switches are `permanent` flags with reserved namespace `ff_kill_*`, evaluated by `KillSwitchGuard` **before** any other logic and honored even when stale (last-known-good persists):

- `ff_kill_integration_<vendor>` — one per vendor (`garmin`, `dexcom`, `broker_terra`…): stops webhook-derived ingestion and hides connect CTAs; mirrors backend integration-hub kill-switches (v1 §31.4) so client and server disable together.
- `ff_kill_insight_template_<family>` — disables a misbehaving insight-template family (e.g., a phrasing regression found post-release) without an app release; `InsightEngine` checks the guard before emitting candidates.
- `ff_kill_ai_cloud` — severs cloud AI routing globally (gateway incident); clients fall back to templates with the "plainer prose, same truth" rule (v1 §32.4).
- `ff_kill_notifications_class_<class>` — per §24.6 class emergency mute.

### 60.5 Experiment assignment integration

`ExperimentAssigner` buckets on the rotated pseudonymous analytics id (§61.4); assignment is deterministic and logged via `flag_exposed` only on first evaluation per session. Hard rules restated from v1 §36.3 as code-level constraints: experiments may target only flags whose `flags.yaml` entry carries `experimentable: true`, and the schema validator rejects `experimentable: true` on any flag whose owner module is `core-scoring`, `core-phrasing`, or `core-insight` truth paths. Local-only users (v1 §28.5): `ExperimentAssigner` returns the safe default arm and emits nothing.

### 60.6 Offline and local-only behavior; config-skew handling

- **Offline:** compiled defaults + last persisted override document; no evaluation ever blocks on network. `RemoteConfigClient` refresh is a low-priority WorkManager/BGAppRefresh task.
- **Local-only mode:** no remote fetch at all — compiled defaults only, kill-switch documents excepted **only** if the user enabled the "safety config" toggle in S-102 (default off, disclosed in the privacy dashboard traffic list).
- **Skew failure handling:** the remote document carries `min_client_flag_schema`; if the client's generated `FlagRegistry` version is older, unknown flags are ignored and known flags applied (forward-compatible). Signature-invalid or unparsable documents are discarded with a `flag_config_rejected` client metric (§65.1); the app never crashes on config — worst case is compiled defaults, which by policy must always be a shippable configuration (checked by `FlagEvaluationTest.defaults_are_release_safe`).

### 60.7 Debug and QA tooling

Debug builds ship a hidden Flags screen (shake gesture → diagnostics menu): every registered flag with source annotation (default/remote/experiment/killed), local override toggles (debug channel only, persisted per install), and a "copy flag state" action that produces the JSON attached to bug reports. Beta builds expose read-only flag state in the same menu (support triage: "which arm was this user in?"). Prod builds compile the screen out. CI uses `flaggen --matrix` to run the core unit suites twice — all-flags-default and all-`rollout`-flags-on — so a flagged path cannot rot untested (the two-configuration rule; full combinatorial testing is explicitly not attempted).

## 61. Analytics event taxonomy

Governance rationale in v1 §36.1–36.2. This section is the taxonomy itself. Source of truth: `contracts/events/analytics-events.yaml`; `core-analytics` codegen (`tooling/scripts/analyticsgen/`) emits typed Kotlin event constructors — an event or property not in the contract **cannot be compiled**, and free-string properties do not exist in the API.

### 61.1 Schema governance

- Every event entry in `analytics-events.yaml`: `name` (snake_case, verb-last), `trigger` (one sentence), `properties` (each: name, type ∈ {enum, int_bucket, bool, string_id_from_registry}, allowed values), `phase`, `owner_track`, `funnels` (memberships), `pii_review: done_by/date`.
- CI validation (`analyticsgen --validate`, PR pipeline stage §63.1): names match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`; every enum closed; every `int` is a declared bucket set (e.g., `duration_bucket: [<10s,10-30s,30-120s,>120s]`); no property of raw type `string` except registry-controlled ids (`metric_family`, `module_id`, `article_id`, `template_family` — each validated against its registry file).
- **Privacy rules as validation constraints (allowlist approach):** health *values* are unrepresentable — there is no numeric property type except declared buckets of durations/counts of *app activity*; banned property names (`value`, `score`, `hr`, `weight`, `glucose`, `kcal`, plus a regex list in the contract header) fail validation; `metric_family` (e.g., `vitals`) is allowed, `metric_id` (e.g., `vitals.hrv_rmssd`) is allowed only on navigation events, and no property may combine `metric_id` with any bucket that could reconstruct a reading. The public analytics disclosure page (v1 §36.2) is generated from this same YAML by `tooling/schema-dictionary-gen/`.

### 61.3 Funnel definitions (ordered event lists + conversion targets)

| Funnel | Ordered events | Targets |
|---|---|---|
| F1 Activation | `onboarding_started` → `health_permission_result(granted>0)` → `backfill_completed` → `first_insight_shown` → `today_viewed` (D1) | ≥80% reach `first_insight_shown` in session 1 (v1 Phase-1 exit); D1 `today_viewed` ≥45% |
| F2 Logging adoption | `log_hub_opened` → first of (`meal_logged`,`symptom_logged`,`med_action_logged`,`mood_checkin_completed`) → second log within 7d | ≥50% hub→first-log; ≥60% first→second within 7d |
| F3 Export/ownership | `export_started` → `export_completed` → repeat `export_started` within 90d | Completion ≥97%; ≥10% of MAU export in first 90d (tests the §5.5 export-wedge bet) |
| F4 Paywall | `paywall_viewed` → `trial_started` → `purchase_completed` → still entitled at +90d | View→trial ≥8%; trial→pay ≥40%; 90d retention ≥85% |
| F5 Notification health | `notification_sent` → `notification_opened` → `today_viewed` within 5m; guardrail: `notification_snoozed` + OS-disable | Open rate ≥35% anchors; disable rate <2%/month (§24.8 KPI) |

Sampling and retention rules (declared per event in the YAML, enforced by the telemetry service): high-volume navigation events (`today_viewed`, `metric_detail_viewed`, `pillar_viewed`) sampled at 20% beyond the first occurrence per user-day; funnel-member events never sampled; raw events retained 13 months, aggregates indefinitely; `local_only_toggled(enabled=true)` is the final event from a device and triggers server-side purge of its queued raw events after aggregation.

### 61.4 Transport, identity, dashboards

Client batches through `core-analytics` → `backend/services/telemetry/`; pseudonymous id rotated every 90 days (funnel windows ≤90d by design); opt-out drops the queue on device. Dashboard inventory (built in the telemetry warehouse, one owner each): **Activation** (F1, per-platform/locale splits) · **Engagement** (DAU/WAU, `today_viewed` depth, module adoption from `today_edited`/`module_visibility_changed`) · **Logging** (F2, method mix, `log_abandoned` steps) · **Export & ownership** (F3, format mix) · **AI quality/cost** (joined with §65.2 gateway metrics; `ask_answered.verifier_result`) · **Notification health** (F5 per class) · **Paywall/revenue** (F4, plan mix) · **Sync & data quality** (`sync_failed`, `source_auth_expired`, `import_completed` dup ratios) · **Stability** (`error_shown` by class × screen, joined to crash rates).

### 62.3 The four flagship suites

**62.3.1 Dedup conformance suite** (`core/core-testing/fixtures/dedup/`, ≥40 cases per E-03.2, CI-blocking). Fixture catalog structure:

```
fixtures/dedup/
├── catalog.yaml                  # index: case id, family, description, origin (real-world source), added-in version
├── steps-phone-watch-01/
│   ├── input.jsonl               # canonical records from ≥2 sources, provenance included
│   ├── expected.jsonl            # survivors + suppressed records with suppressed_by pointers + rule id fired
│   └── meta.yaml                 # tolerances (e.g., minute-bucket step counts), notes
├── sleep-ring-vs-watch-01/ … workout-garmin-hk-dupe-02/ … import-over-live-03/ …
```

Runner (`DedupConformanceSuite` in core-testing) executes `DedupEngine` per case and diffs serialized output; failure prints the decision journal. Coverage floor mirrors v1 §37.2 cases 6–11 (each is ≥3 fixtures). Adding a threshold tune (server config, §30.6) requires a fixture demonstrating the case it fixes.

**62.3.2 Cross-platform parity suite** (release-blocking, nightly). Mechanics: one seeded SQLDelight fixture DB (`fixtures/parity/parity-seed-v<N>.db`, ~90 days of multi-source data incl. cycle + statuses) → shipped into an iOS XCTest host running the KMP framework and an Android instrumentation test → both run the full derivation pipeline (ingest→dedup→baselines→scores→insight candidates→export) → serialize `derived_values`, `baselines`, insight candidate set, and CSV/JSON export bytes with fixed-precision number formatting → artifacts uploaded → `tooling/scripts/parity-diff/` byte-compares. Any diff fails with a per-record report. This enforces v1 §33.4's "divergence forbidden" list mechanically.

**62.3.3 Phrasing guardrail red-team suite.** Corpus: `contracts/phrasing/guardrails.yaml` rules compiled into positive/negative cases plus a maintained adversarial set (`fixtures/phrasing/redteam/*.yaml`): diagnosis-flavored claims, alarm words, "Detraining" under Injured status (the Karim case, v1 §3.13), luteal-phase false-alarm phrasings, calibration overconfidence, banned certainty adverbs. Assertions: `PhrasingLinter` blocks every banned case; every LLM-path output (recorded eval set of ≥500 generations per release from the AI gateway staging) passes the same linter with ≥99% precision on the numeric-claim verifier (E-17 target); AR and EN rule parity (every rule has cases in both languages). Monthly wording audit (v1 §40.4) adds cases; the suite only grows.

**62.3.4 Migration soak suite.** `fixtures/db-versions/` keeps one seeded DB per released schema version (generated at each release by `tooling/fixture-gen/`, realistic volume: 200k samples, 800 sessions, 2k events, all sensitive classes). Suite: open each vN.db → run all forward migrations → assert (a) row-count invariants, (b) spot-check queries per table, (c) full re-derivation completes and matches vN-fixture golden scores within algorithm-version rules, (d) migration duration budget (<10s for the 200k-sample DB on CI hardware; user-facing budget in §64.1). Runs nightly and on any PR touching `core/core-db/`.

### 62.6 Beta rings and release QA checklist

Rings: **R0** team dogfood (daily debug builds, all flags debug-on) → **R1** internal ~50 (weekly, TestFlight internal / Play internal) → **R2** closed beta 500–1,000 (per release train, both stores; device-zoo gaps recruited deliberately: Samsung/Xiaomi heavy) → **R3** open beta (RC builds) → production staged rollout 1%→10%→50%→100% with §65 alert gates between steps.

Release QA checklist (every train, owned by TRACK-QA-RELEASE; blocking):
1. PR/nightly suites green incl. parity, dedup conformance, migration soak, red-team phrasing.
2. §32.6 perf budgets measured on SE 3 + Pixel 6a (cold start, chart render, battery attribution).
3. Snapshot diff review: both themes × RTL × 3 type sizes — zero unexplained diffs.
4. Device-zoo 48h background-sync pass on S24/Xiaomi/OnePlus.
5. Manual pass of the §16.9 state matrix on 5 rotating screens (denied/empty/offline/provisional/paywalled).
6. Onboarding fresh-install on min-OS devices, EN and AR.
7. Export round-trip: full CSV/JSON archive re-imported into a fresh install via CSV mapper; record counts match.
8. Delete-account drill on staging: verifiable package produced, backend blobs gone.
9. Widget/complication render check after 24h idle.
10. Store metadata/screenshots regenerated if UI changed; privacy nutrition labels / Data safety form diffed.
11. Algorithm-version diff report reviewed (no unintended re-derivations, §64.5).
12. Crash-free ≥99.7% in R2 for ≥4 days before R3.
13. Flag states audited (`flaggen --report`): no `draft` flag defaulted on in prod config.
14. Runbook links in new alerts resolve (§65.3).

## 63. CI/CD and environment strategy

### 63.1 Pipeline inventory

**PR pipeline** (target: ≤20 min wall clock, stages parallel where independent; config `tooling/ci/pr-pipeline.yml`):

| Stage | Contents | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Static | format, lint (ktlint/SwiftLint/detekt/ruff), license headers | 2 min |
| 2. Contracts | JSON-Schema/OpenAPI/proto validation; analyticsgen + flaggen validators; registry schema check | 1 min |
| 3. Affected detection | module graph diff (§63.2) decides stages 4–8 scope | 30 s |
| 4. Core | affected KMP module unit+golden tests (JVM target) | 6 min |
| 5. Adapters | contract tests vs fakes + recorded fixtures | 4 min |
| 6. iOS | XcodeGen → build affected targets + unit tests (no UI flows) | 10 min |
| 7. Android | assemble + unit tests + Paparazzi snapshots (affected) | 8 min |
| 8. Backend | affected service pytest + schemathesis contract stage | 5 min |
| 9. Gates | flag-overdue check, migration-numbering check (§66.5), danger rules (PR checklist §66.7) | 1 min |

**Nightly pipeline:** full (non-affected-scoped) matrix + parity suite (§62.3.2) + dedup conformance full + migration soak + perf micro-bench trend + iOS/Android UI-flow suites on device farm + screenshot matrix (themes×RTL×type sizes) + dependency/vulnerability audit + backend load smoke. Failures page the owning track's channel, not individuals.

**Release pipeline (per platform):** tag `ios/vX.Y.0` or `android/vX.Y.0` on the release branch → full nightly suite must be green on that SHA → version/build-number stamp → signed archive (fastlane `gym` / Gradle `bundleRelease`) → symbol upload (dSYM/mapping to crash backend, §65.1) → upload to TestFlight internal / Play internal → ring promotions are manual pipeline approvals with checklist links (§62.6) → staged production rollout with automated halt on §65.3 alert breach.

**Backend deploy pipeline:** PR merge → build containers per affected service → contract tests vs `contracts/api/backend-openapi.yaml` → auto-deploy **dev** → auto-deploy **staging** + smoke suite (sync round trip with test device keys, webhook replay fixture, AI-gateway canary prompt) → **prod** by manual approval, canary 5% for 30 min with RED-metric gate (§65.2) → full. Infra changes via `backend/infra/terraform/` plan-review-apply, never console edits.

### 63.2 Monorepo-aware selective builds

`tooling/scripts/affected/` computes the changed-file → module map from the Gradle project graph + declared cross-links (`ios/` depends on `core/*` published framework; `android/app` on `core/*`; backend services on `contracts/api`; everything on `contracts/`). Rules: changes under `contracts/` build **everything** (that is the point of freezing them early, §66.1); changes under `ios/BadanApp/Features/Today/` build iOS only; `core/core-scoring/` builds core + both apps + parity marker (nightly parity forced next run). CI caching: Gradle remote build cache + Xcode derived-data cache keyed on `project.yml` + package checksums.

### 63.3 Environments

| Surface | Environments | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | `local` (docker-compose in `backend/`), `dev` (auto-deploy, synthetic data only), `staging` (release-candidate, sandbox vendor creds, store sandbox billing), `prod` (EU + GCC regions per v1 §31.3) | No real health payloads outside prod (E2E blobs are opaque everywhere anyway); staging retention 14 days |
| iOS app | `Debug` (local backend or dev, debug flag channel), `TestFlight` (staging, beta flag channel), `Prod` (prod, prod flag channel) | Bundle-id suffixes `.debug`/`.beta`; HealthKit entitlements identical across configs |
| Android | `debug`, `beta` (Play tracks internal/closed/open), `release` | applicationIdSuffix mirrors iOS |
| Content/flags | contentcms `draft` → `staged` (beta channel) → `published` (prod) | Insight templates and flag docs promoted like code |

### 63.4 Secrets management

No secrets in the repo, ever (CI secret-scan in stage 1). Backend: cloud secret manager, CI access via OIDC federation (no long-lived tokens); vendor API creds per environment, sandbox vs prod separated at the account level. Mobile signing: iOS via fastlane `match` (encrypted certs repo, CI-read-only); Android via Play App Signing + upload key in CI keystore secret. Client apps ship zero embedded secrets — vendor OAuth uses backend-brokered flows (integration hub, v1 §31.2); the AI gateway key never exists client-side.

### 63.5 Store submission automation and release trains

Fastlane lanes in `tooling/ci/fastlane/`: `ios_beta`, `ios_release` (gym→pilot→deliver with metadata from `content/store/ios/<locale>/`), screenshot generation from UI-test harness for EN+AR; Android via Gradle Play Publisher (`publishBundle`, track promotion, staged rollout fractions, metadata from `content/store/android/`). Release trains: **2-week cadence**; branch cut Monday week 1 (`release/x.y`), R1 same day, R2 Wednesday, R3/RC Monday week 2, store submission Wednesday, staged rollout through week 2. Hotfix path: branch from the release tag, cherry-pick fix, expedited pipeline (full suite minus device-zoo manual), both stores' expedited review; hotfix increments patch version and merges back to main same day. Feature-incomplete work rides trains behind `draft` flags — trains never wait for features.

Train calendar (repeats every 2 weeks; owner: TRACK-QA-RELEASE release captain, rotating):

| Day | Action | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| Mon W1 | Cut `release/x.y`; R1 build to internal rings | Nightly green on cut SHA |
| Wed W1 | R2 promotion (closed beta both stores) | PR + nightly suites, flag audit |
| Fri W1 | R2 health review; hotfix-only merges to release branch begin | Crash-free trend, §65.3 alerts quiet |
| Mon W2 | R3/RC promotion (open beta) | §62.6 items 1–5 |
| Wed W2 | Store submission (App Review + Play review) | §62.6 all items |
| Fri W2–ongoing | Staged rollout 1%→10%→50%→100% | §65 gates between steps; halt = automatic |

### 63.6 Artifact retention

PR artifacts (test reports, snapshots, parity diffs) 14 days; nightly artifacts 30 days; release artifacts (signed binaries, symbol files, SBOM, fixture DBs for that schema version, export-schema snapshot) retained indefinitely; fixture DBs and golden files versioned in Git LFS. Crash symbol files retained for every released build forever (long-tail OS-upgrade crashes are real).

## 64. Migration and versioning strategy

Rationale: v1 §30.4 (schema governance), §34.2 (sync), §20 (export stability), §22.5/§37.8 (algorithm change trust). Five versioned surfaces, each with rules, process, and tests. Governing principle: **every surface versions independently; the contracts repo records all of them; nothing breaks a reader older than N-2.**

### 64.1 Surface 1 — Local DB schema (SQLDelight)

- **Rules:** forward-only migrations, one `.sqm` file per version in `core/core-db/src/commonMain/sqldelight/migrations/`; no destructive column drops within a phase (rename-and-deprecate, drop after 2 trains); additive columns nullable or defaulted; migration files immutable once released.
- **Numbering:** migration numbers are reserved via `core/core-db/MIGRATIONS.lock` (single-line-per-version file; TRACK-QA merges reservation PRs) to prevent two parallel agents claiming version 12 (§66.5 heat map).
- **Process:** write `.sqm` → bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` → regenerate DAOs → add/refresh soak fixture (§62.3.4) → user-facing budget: migrations on a heavy multi-year DB complete <3 s on an SE 3-class device or must run chunked-with-progress under a "updating your library" screen (only permitted at app-update launch, never mid-session).

### 64.2 Surface 2 — Sync protocol

- **Rules:** every envelope carries `protocol_version` + `payload_schema_version` per entity type (`contracts/sync/sync.proto`); servers are version-agnostic (blobs are opaque) so negotiation is client↔client via the sync metadata document; compatibility window **N-2**: a device two protocol versions behind must still push/pull; unknown payload fields are preserved, not stripped (round-trip safety for older writers).
- **Process:** protocol change → ADR → proto bump → `EnvelopeVersionNegotiationTest` matrix (vN writer × vN-2 reader and inverse) → beta ring devices intentionally version-skewed for one train before GA. When N-3 devices connect, they receive a sync-paused state with an "update required" card (S-02) — never silent divergence.

### 64.3 Surface 3 — Export schema

- **Rules:** semver on `contracts/export/schema/v1/*.schema.json`; **additive = minor** (new columns appended at end of CSVs, new optional JSON fields), **breaking = major** with the old major still generatable for ≥12 months (Priya's Jupyter notebooks are a contract, v1 §3.18); every export embeds `schema_version`, `algorithm_versions` map, and dedup-policy id in `manifest.json`.
- **Process:** change → dictionary changelog entry (generated into `docs/data-dictionary/CHANGELOG.md` by `tooling/schema-dictionary-gen/`) → `SchemaSnapshotTest` update in the same PR (snapshot diff is the review artifact) → published dictionary page regenerated. Reader guarantees stated in the dictionary: column order stable within a major; encodings fixed (UTF-8, RFC 4180, ISO-8601 with offset); units column always present.

### 64.4 Surface 4 — Contracts & codegen

- **Rules:** `contracts/` is frozen per §66.1; any change re-runs all codegen (registry, analytics, flags, API models) and rebuilds everything (§63.2). Breaking changes (removing an event property, renaming a metric id, changing a domain-event payload) require an **ADR** in `docs/adr/` naming: motivation, blast radius (which tracks/modules), migration steps per consumer, and version bumps on affected surfaces. Metric ids are immortal — a wrong id is deprecated (`deprecated: true, superseded_by:`) never deleted, because exports and baselines reference it.
- **Process:** contracts PRs require sign-off from TRACK-CONTRACTS plus every consuming track named in the ADR (enforced by CODEOWNERS on `contracts/`).

### 64.5 Surface 5 — Algorithm versions

- **Rules:** every `DerivedValue` carries `algorithm_version` (v1 §30.1); recomputation appends, never overwrites. Version bump classes: **patch** (bugfix, silent re-derivation allowed for affected window), **minor** (behavior tweak; re-derivation + changelog entry in S-57's linked page), **major** (model change; requires the §37.8 flow).
- **Re-derivation runbook** (`docs/runbooks/algo-rederivation.md`): (1) ship new calculator behind `draft` flag; (2) staged backfill recompute as chunked background job with progress (v1 §32.3), old versions retained; (3) score-distribution drift monitor (§65.1) compared pre/post on beta rings — drift beyond envelope halts rollout; (4) in-app change note ("Recovery model v3: what changed and why") delivered with the recompute, plus optional 2-week side-by-side old/new for power users; (5) export dictionary notes the new algorithm id; (6) flag → ga → cleanup per §60.2.

### 64.6 The five surfaces at a glance

| Surface | Version carrier | Compatibility rule | Blocking test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local DB | `SCHEMA_VERSION` + `.sqm` files | Forward-only; immutable once released | Migration soak (§62.3.4) |
| Sync protocol | `protocol_version` + per-entity `payload_schema_version` | N-2 window; unknown fields preserved | `EnvelopeVersionNegotiationTest` matrix |
| Export schema | semver in `manifest.json` | Additive=minor, breaking=major kept ≥12 mo | `SchemaSnapshotTest` |
| Contracts/codegen | file-level versions + ADR log | Consumers sign ADR; ids immortal | Stage-2 validators + full rebuild |
| Algorithms | `algorithm_version` on every `DerivedValue` | Append-only re-derivation; change notes for minor+ | Golden suites + drift monitor (§65.1) |

### 64.7 Worked example — add a column to `event_records`

Goal: add `body_position` (enum: sitting/standing/lying) to measurement-type `EventRecord` payloads for BP context. Every artifact touched, in order:

1. `docs/adr/ADR-0042-bp-body-position.md` — motivation, blast radius (core-model, core-db, sync payload v2, export minor, both log screens); TRACK-CONTRACTS + CORE-DATA + both feature tracks sign.
2. `contracts/events/domain-events.yaml` — `MeasurementLogged` payload schema v2 adds optional `body_position`.
3. `contracts/metrics/registry/vitals.yaml` — BP entry gains display rule for the context chip (registry-driven UI binding, E-01.3).
4. `core/core-db/MIGRATIONS.lock` — reserve migration 13.
5. `core/core-db/src/commonMain/sqldelight/migrations/13.sqm` — `ALTER TABLE event_records ADD COLUMN body_position TEXT DEFAULT NULL;` + `SCHEMA_VERSION = 13`.
6. `core/core-model/…/EventRecord.kt` — `MeasurementPayload` gains `bodyPosition: BodyPosition?` (payload schema v2; v1 payloads decode with null).
7. `core/core-testing/fixtures/db-versions/` — regenerate v12 fixture golden expectations; soak suite must pass v12→13.
8. `core/core-sync/` — `payload_schema_version` bump for `event_records` entity; `EnvelopeVersionNegotiationTest` case: v1-payload reader ignores field, preserves on round-trip (N-2 window intact — no protocol bump needed, payload-only).
9. `contracts/export/schema/v1/csv-manifest.schema.json` — minor bump v1.4.0: `body_position` column appended to `event_records.csv`; `SchemaSnapshotTest` snapshot updated; dictionary changelog entry generated.
10. iOS `ios/BadanApp/Features/Log/` S-81 measurement sheet — position segmented control (optional, default none); Android `android/app/…/features/log/` mirrors.
11. Analytics: none — `measurement_logged` already carries `measurement_family`; positions are health context, not loggable telemetry (§61.1 allowlist).
12. Parity seed DB regenerated (`fixtures/parity/parity-seed-v+1.db`) including positioned BP rows; parity suite green.
13. Release notes + regenerated data dictionary ship in the next train. Total: 1 ADR, 2 contract files, 1 lock line, 1 migration, 1 model change, 2 fixture regens, 1 export snapshot, 2 feature screens.

## 65. Observability and error reporting structure

Extends v1 §36.4. Split: client-side (privacy-constrained, §65.4), backend-side (service health), alerting (owned, runbooked), incidents.

### 65.1 Client-side

- **Crash/ANR:** Sentry-class SDK on both apps (self-hosted or EU-resident vendor); dSYM/mapping upload in release pipeline (§63.1); release-health gate: crash-free sessions ≥99.7% (v1 Phase-1 exit) enforced between rollout stages. Breadcrumbs are screen/route ids and event names only — never log payloads (§65.4).
- **Perf beacons vs §32.6 budgets:** sampled (5%) timing beacons: `cold_start_ms` (to Today interactive, cached vs first-ever), `chart_render_ms` (1-year decimated series), `db_open_ms`, `migration_ms`, `import_throughput_rows_s`, `background_battery_attribution` (platform APIs, daily). Each beacon carries device-class bucket, not model string. Dashboards trend p50/p95 per release; regression >15% p95 on two consecutive nightlies files a release blocker.
- **Sync-health client metrics:** `sync_cycle_result` (ok/fail+stage), `ingest_latency_bucket` (platform-store event → row committed; the §62.5 OEM reality metric), `dedup_suppression_ratio` drift, `flag_config_rejected`, `oplog_backlog_bucket`. Aggregated on-device daily, sent as counters (no timestamps of health events).
- **Score-distribution drift monitor:** weekly on-device histogram of score buckets (0–100 in 10s) per score kind, submitted as counts; backend compares population shape across app versions — the §64.5 gate.
- **Error taxonomy:** one sealed hierarchy in `core-model`, mapped to user messages in `core-phrasing` (message keys, localized) and to metrics automatically:

```kotlin
sealed interface AppError {
    data class PermissionDenied(val kind: PermissionKind) : AppError            // → S-16.9 denied state, fix-path CTA
    data class SourceUnavailable(val source: SourceRef, val cause: SourceCause) : AppError // cause: AuthExpired|VendorOutage|PlatformMissing
    data class SyncFailure(val stage: SyncStage, val retryable: Boolean) : AppError
    data class StorageFailure(val kind: StorageKind) : AppError                 // Corruption|Full|CryptoUnavailable
    data class IngestRejected(val reason: IngestReason) : AppError              // FutureTimestamp|BoundsViolation|SchemaUnknown
    data class AiUnavailable(val tier: AiTier, val fallback: Fallback) : AppError // fallback: Template|Queue|None
    data class ExportFailed(val format: ExportFormat, val stage: ExportStage) : AppError
    data class EntitlementRequired(val feature: FeatureKey) : AppError          // renders paywalled state, never obfuscation
    data class Unexpected(val code: SupportCode) : AppError                     // user sees "support id: BD-xxxx"
}
```

Mapping rules: every `AppError` renders through the §16.9 state system (no raw toasts); every surface of one emits `error_shown {error_class, screen}` (§61.2); `Unexpected` support codes are grep-able in crash breadcrumbs for support triage.

### 65.2 Backend-side

- **Per-service RED metrics** (rate/errors/duration, per endpoint) for all nine services (v1 §31.2), exported to the metrics stack defined in `backend/infra/`; SLOs: sync p95 <400 ms per envelope batch, identity p95 <200 ms, availability 99.9% monthly for sync/identity/push.
- **Integration-hub vendor dashboards:** per vendor (Garmin, Dexcom, broker…): webhook receipt rate vs expected, delivery-queue depth, replay-buffer utilization, token-refresh failure rate, vendor-API error mix, per-vendor kill-switch state (§60.4). Contract-test canaries against vendor sandboxes run every 6h (v1 §31.4).
- **AI-gateway metrics:** cost per request/day per model route, token counts, p50/p95 latency, verifier-rejection rate (target <1% reaching users — rejects fall back to templates), zero-retention header verification canary, per-tier traffic split (cloud vs on-device is a client metric joined here), guardrail-lint failures by rule id (feeding the §62.3.3 corpus).
- **Telemetry service self-metrics:** event-schema validation rejects (should be ~0 — client codegen prevents), queue lag.

### 65.3 Alerting table (alert → threshold → owning track → runbook)

| Alert | Threshold | Owning track | Runbook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crash-free below gate | <99.7% on rollout stage | TRACK-QA-RELEASE | `docs/runbooks/rollout-halt.md` |
| Cold-start p95 regression | >15% vs prior release, 2 nightlies | TRACK-IOS-SHELL / TRACK-AND-SHELL | `docs/runbooks/perf-regression.md` |
| Ingest latency p95 (Android OEM) | >6h any OEM cohort | TRACK-ADAPTERS | `docs/runbooks/oem-background-sync.md` |
| Sync error rate | >2% cycles failing, 30 min | TRACK-CORE-DATA + TRACK-BACKEND | `docs/runbooks/sync-incident.md` |
| Vendor webhook silence | 0 receipts for 2× expected interval | TRACK-BACKEND | `docs/runbooks/vendor-outage.md` (incl. kill-switch decision) |
| Token-refresh failure spike | >5% per vendor, 1h | TRACK-BACKEND | `docs/runbooks/vendor-auth.md` |
| AI verifier-rejection spike | >5% of generations, 1h | TRACK-CORE-INTEL | `docs/runbooks/ai-quality.md` (incl. `ff_kill_ai_cloud` decision) |
| AI cost anomaly | >2× 7-day baseline daily spend | TRACK-BACKEND | `docs/runbooks/ai-cost.md` |
| Score-distribution drift | Population shape shift beyond envelope post-release | TRACK-CORE-INTEL | `docs/runbooks/algo-rederivation.md` §gate-3 |
| Notification disable spike | >2%/month cohort rate (§24.8 KPI) | TRACK-CORE-INTEL (notify) | `docs/runbooks/notification-budget.md` |
| Dedup suppression-ratio drift | ±30% vs baseline per family | TRACK-CORE-DATA | `docs/runbooks/dedup-drift.md` |
| Export failure rate | >3% of jobs, 24h | TRACK-CORE-DATA | `docs/runbooks/export-failures.md` |
| flag_config_rejected spike | >0.5% of clients daily | TRACK-QA-RELEASE | `docs/runbooks/flag-config.md` |

### 65.4 Privacy constraints on telemetry (forbidden fields)

Restating v1 §28/§36.2 as hard rules validated in code review + the analytics allowlist (§61.1): **forbidden in any crash report, log line, metric label, or event:** health values or their buckets; metric readings; free text (notes, symptom names, food names, chat contents); precise timestamps of health events (only app-interaction timestamps); location; device names ("Omar's Watch"); vendor account ids; raw user ids (only rotated pseudonymous ids); IP addresses beyond transient transport (not stored). Local-only mode sends nothing — dashboards must state their cohort excludes these users (v1 §36.3). Crash SDK configured with `beforeSend` scrubber whose rule list is versioned in `core/core-analytics/` and covered by `PropertyAllowlistTest`-style unit tests.

### 65.5 Incident severity and response SLAs

| Sev | Definition | Examples | Response SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEV-1 | Data loss/corruption risk, security/privacy breach, sync divergence, stores pulled | corrupt migration shipped; E2E key mishandling | Page on-call now; mitigation <1h; hotfix train; user comms if data affected; post-mortem ≤3 days |
| SEV-2 | Core promise broken for a cohort | ingestion dead on an OEM; scores wrong for a phase cohort; vendor integration down >24h w/o kill-switch messaging | Response <4h business; fix in ≤1 train or remote-config mitigation |
| SEV-3 | Degraded non-core feature | AI tier down with template fallback working; widget staleness | Next train |
| SEV-4 | Cosmetic/known-issue | snapshot drift, copy issues | Backlog, batched |

On-call: one rotation for backend (all nine services — the blind backend is small enough, v1 §31.1) and one client release captain per train; SEV-1/2 pages go to both plus the owning track from §65.3. User-facing incident comms follow the honesty register: the S-02 sync sheet and per-source freshness rows are the primary status surface (v1 §37.6), with a status page for backend outages; "silent staleness" is itself classified SEV-2.

Post-mortems are blameless, filed in `docs/runbooks/postmortems/`, and each must add at least one test, alert, or fixture (the §62.3.1 catalog grows this way).

## 66. Agent orchestration map and parallel execution plan

This is the capstone: how ~dozens of coding agents build BADAN in parallel without stepping on each other. It operationalizes v1 §40 (squads) into agent tracks, and v1 §41–42 (roadmap/epics) into waves and packets. Everything here assumes the monorepo tree of CONVENTIONS §2 verbatim.

### 66.1 Orchestration principles and the contracts-first freeze list

Principles:
1. **Contracts before concurrency.** No parallel fan-out until the freeze list below exists and IC-1 passes. Interface changes after freeze go through the §64.4 ADR path — expensive on purpose.
2. **Exclusive write ownership.** Every path in the repo has exactly one owning track (66.2); agents write only inside owned paths and read anything. Cross-track needs become interface requests, not edits.
3. **Registration over modification.** Shared surfaces (DI, navigation, strings, event taxonomy) are extended by adding per-feature files discovered by codegen/reflection lists — never by editing a central file (66.5).
4. **Vertical slice first.** Before the Wave-3 fan-out, one end-to-end slice (sleep pillar walking skeleton, 66.8) proves every seam under real data on both platforms.
5. **Checkpoints gate waves.** IC-1…IC-6 (66.6) are hard gates; a track may run ahead locally but nothing merges past an unmet checkpoint.

**Freeze list (must exist and validate before Wave-1 fan-out):**

| Artifact | Path | Why frozen |
|---|---|---|
| Metric registry schema + P1 seed families | `contracts/metrics/registry.schema.json`, `contracts/metrics/registry/{sleep,vitals,activity,workouts,body,nutrition,subjective,context}.yaml` | Every module keys off metric ids |
| Domain-event bus taxonomy | `contracts/events/domain-events.yaml` | Engines communicate only via these |
| Analytics taxonomy (P1 subset) | `contracts/events/analytics-events.yaml` | Features instrument at build time (§61) |
| Export schema v1 | `contracts/export/schema/v1/*.schema.json` | Export engine + dictionary generator |
| Sync protocol v1 | `contracts/sync/sync.proto`, `contracts/sync/protocol.md` | core-sync + backend sync service |
| Backend API v1 | `contracts/api/backend-openapi.yaml` | Client codegen + all services |
| Phrasing guardrails v1 | `contracts/phrasing/guardrails.yaml` | Linter is CI-blocking from day one |
| core-model types | `core/core-model/` (Sample, IntervalRecord, Session, EventRecord, DerivedValue, Baseline, Insight, Provenance, QualityFlags, AppError) | Every module's vocabulary |
| Port interfaces | `adapters/port-health/` (`HealthStorePort`, `CapabilityDescriptor`), `port-crypto/ port-files/ port-clock/ port-push/ port-locale/` interfaces | Adapters and fakes implement against these |
| DB schema v1 | `core/core-db/**/*.sq` for the §30.1 tables | Repositories + fixtures |
| Design tokens | `ios/BadanApp/DesignSystem/Tokens/`, `android/…/designsystem/tokens/` (generated from one `content/design/tokens.yaml`) | Both design systems consume, features never hardcode |
| Route registry | `contracts/events/routes.yaml` (route ids + deeplink patterns; both routers codegen from it) | Navigation without a contended file |
| Flag registry P1 | `core/core-flags/flags.yaml` | Features gate themselves from day one |

| AND-SHELL | C | ✅ | ✅ | C | ✅ | ✅ | — | ⚠ | ✅ | ⚠ | ✅ | C |
| AND-FEATURES | C | ✅ | C | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠ | — | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠ | C |
| BACKEND | C | C | C | C | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | C | C |
